title: Unforgettable Experiences and Exclusive Offers at Aeera Villa Canggu
content:
Unforgettable Experiences and Exclusive Offers at Aeera Villa Canggu
Treat Yourself to Our Premier Villa Canggu Services
Experience top-tier hospitality at Aeera Villa, proudly managed by Ini Vie Hospitality. As a premier villa in Canggu Bali, we offer exceptional services, including personalized assistance and daily care, ensuring a seamless and relaxing stay from start to finish.
The Water and Bije Blessing Ceremony has become a cherished symbol of renewal here, a quiet blessing offered for the journey that lies ahead. Rooted deeply in Balinese tradition, each ritual invites you to reconnect with gratitude, balance, and inner peace.
As you arrive at Aeera Villa Canggu, holy water touches your skin and grains of bije rest gently upon your forehead, marking a moment of spiritual cleansing and protection. More than just a tradition, it's a heartfelt way to begin your journey grounded, present, and at peace with your soul.
We honour your departure with the Tridatu Farewell Ceremony, a final, heartfelt celebration where every colour reflects harmony, strength, and protection. It's a meaningful moment that brings us together one last time.
More than just a goodbye, this gathering celebrates the connection we've shared and the memories you'll carry forward. Though your journey may lead you in new directions, the bond we've formed remains beautifully woven through the Tridatu.

title: Ajowa Resort Seminyak
content:
Ajowa Resort Seminyak
Return to Grounded Living in Bali
Step away from the noise and discover a slower way to experience Seminyak. Ajowa Resort is a biophilic grounded luxury sanctuary where nature and organic architecture shape every moment of your stay. Woven into lush tropical landscapes, the resort features warm terracotta textures and sculpted curves that invite you to pause, breathe, and reconnect.
This is not just another luxury hotel in Bali. We designed every pathway, water feature, and sun-baked wall to deliver a sense of intentional living. From golden hour on the rooftop to quiet mornings surrounded by greenery, Ajowa offers a deeply restorative escape. Reserve your stay and return to what feels grounded.
Grand Two Bedroom Villa With Private Pool
Grand One Bedroom Villa With Private Pool
Norii Restaurant, Contemporary Japanese Dining
Dining at Norii Restaurant is a slow, intentional ceremony where contemporary Japanese cuisine is prepared with quiet precision and local provenance. The warm lighting and natural textures of the space encourage you to savor every bite, offering an unhurried culinary experience that perfectly matches the rhythm of our biophilic resort.
Discover Experience Living at Ajowa Resort
Signature Facilities for Elevated Stays
Immersive Experience
Exclusive Offers from Ajowa Resort
We invite you to experience grounded luxury in Seminyak with our curated selection of exclusive offers. Whether you are planning an extended retreat, a romantic honeymoon, or a wellness-focused getaway, these packages are designed to enhance your stay with meaningful rituals. Booking direct ensures you receive the most restorative value, including priority access to our signature spa treatments and dining experiences.
Stories From Our Esteemed Guests and Partners
“Luxury in Bali often comes wrapped in grand gestures. At Ajowa Resort & Spa Seminyak, luxury is defined by a deeper connection to the natural world.”
“A nature-driven villa designed as a contemporary retreat with vibrant Seminyak flair, where simplicity and craftsmanship quietly shape the experience.”
“It is a place to linger between plans, watch the day unfold, and experience the changing rhythm of the destination from above.”
Ajowa Resort sits in the Seminyak area of Bali, at Jl. Umalas Lestari No.88, minutes from Seminyak's dining, beach, and shopping scene. It is a resort in Seminyak, Bali designed to stay calm amid the energy: close to everything, removed from the noise.
Ajowa Resort is approximately 15.9 km / 50 minutes from I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS), depending on traffic. Private airport transfers can be arranged through our reservation team or your e-butler.
Seminyak Beach and the Petitenget area are around 25 minutes by car from the resort. Our team can arrange transport, or your e-butler can help you plan the trip around the quietest hours.
Yes. The resort sits between the Seminyak and Canggu areas, putting the cafés, beach clubs, and sunset spots of both within a short drive, while the resort itself stays tucked away from the crowds.
Ajowa has just ten villas. This intimate scale is intentional: fewer neighbors, more privacy, and service that knows your name. It is one of the reasons couples choose Ajowa over larger resorts in the Seminyak area.
Yes. Every one of Ajowa's ten villas has its own private pool, making it one of the few villa resorts in Seminyak, Bali where a pool of your own comes with every stay.
Two types: the Grand One Bedroom Villa with Private Pool, made for two, and the Grand Two Bedroom Villa with Private Pool, suited to couples celebrating with close friends or family. Both feature open-air bath rituals, sculpted architecture, and warm terracotta interiors.
Yes, Ajowa Resort is a welcoming environment for families seeking a slower, more intentional getaway. While the resort focuses on calm and restorative living rather than high-energy activities, our Grand Two Bedroom Villa with Private Pool provides an ideal setting for families with children or small groups.
It is Ajowa's architectural identity: contemporary design softened by sculpted curves, warm terracotta tones, natural textures, and organic forms drawn from nature. Rather than decoration, nature shapes the spaces themselves, through daylight, greenery, water, and airflow.
Yes. Ajowa's rooftop pool and lounge is designed for the golden hour: a slow swim above the rooftops with the Seminyak area glowing below.
Norii Restaurant is Ajowa's signature venue, pairing timeless Japanese technique with a warm, modern sensibility. Expect precise, seasonal, quietly inventive dishes in an intimate setting.
Yes. Reservations are recommended and can be made through the resort or your e-butler.
Svaha Spa AJOWA offers signature Balinese rituals, floating sound healing, and private yoga sessions: an integrated wellness journey that makes Ajowa a true luxury spa resort in Seminyak, not a hotel with a spa attached.
Ajowa's most distinctive ritual. You lie back supported on the water while resonant tones move through it, creating weightlessness and deep stillness. Sessions are guided and suitable for beginners. It is the experience guests tend to describe first.
Yes. Signature couples' rituals at Svaha Spa AJOWA unfold side by side, combining Balinese techniques, warm oils, and unhurried time. Book ahead through your e-butler, as the spa's intimate size means sessions are limited each day.
Book directly through our website or by WhatsApp at +62 823-2289-3908. Direct bookings receive our best available rate, and WEINIVIE members earn exclusive rewards on every stay, including 15% off at Svaha Spa.

title: Aksari Resort in Ubud
content:
Aksari Resort in Ubud
An Eco-Luxury Resort with Multi-Experience Sacred Essence of Bali
Aksari Resort is a Ubud sanctuary where wisdom, art, and spirituality come together in harmony. The emblem of Aksari, encircled with intricate patterns around the letter “A,” symbolizes a gateway to sacred serenity. Its name, derived from Sanskrit meaning “letter” or “essence,” honors the written word as a vessel of knowledge and devotion.
At the resort’s entrance, the Ganesha statue welcomes guests as the guardian of learning, prosperity, and new beginnings. Like ink flowing across palm-leaf manuscripts, every guest writes their own story at Aksari Resort, a place where love, healing, and discovery unfold gracefully.

Each dish symbolizes equality and togetherness between the king and his soldiers, crafted from locally sourced ingredients and transformed by skilled chefs into a dining experience meant to be deeply felt, not merely tasted.
Kojin Japanese Restaurant Ubud
Kojin is a lively theatrical teppanyaki restaurant amidst Ubud’s lush forest, where refined Japanese culinary craftsmanship meets the elegance of Balinese nature. From delicate sashimi to vibrant teppanyaki, each course unfolds in an intimate, dramatic setting that celebrates precision, flavor, and artistry.

A special thank you to Ayu, who went above and beyond to help us during our stay. She was always kind, attentive, and truly made our experience even more enjoyable. Highly recommended!”

title: Experience and Exploration in Ubud with Aksari Resort
content:
Experience and Exploration in Ubud with Aksari Resort
As the best resort in Ubud for honeymoons, your stay is a shared journey of discovery. We welcome you as family to fully immerse in nature’s soothing beauty, restorative wellness, authentic culture, and spiritual healing. This is a holistic experience, designed to renew your connection, from the world around you, to the love within.
Daily Cultural Guest Activities
Wellness Exploration
Cultural Exploration
Our daily activities bring you closer through interactive and immersive experiences. Mix your own signature drinks, cook authentic dishes, or discover traditional crafts such as ngulat tipat and making canang. Don’t just witness culture, but become a part of it.
Daily Morning Yoga Class
Deepen your connection to Bali through the sacred Melukat ritual, a profound purification of heart and soul. This cleansing ceremony is designed to release negative energy and welcome a renewed sense of peace and rebirth. It is one of the many ways Aksari can guide you on a transformative spiritual journey.
Spiritual Awakening Journey
This journey is a seamless blend of sacred rituals, mindful movement, and restorative treatments, each crafted to bring balance and renewal. Guided by the wisdom of a Balinese healer, it unfolds as an intimate experience designed to harmonize body, mind, and spirit.
Private Sunrise Trekking
Begin thy day in gentle grace, where golden light breaks upon the sacred hills. Let the hush of dawn, the kiss of morning air, and nature’s quiet majesty lead thee to a realm where the sun crowns the earth in splendour.
Bali Island Tour (Half Day or Full Day Tour)
Unveil the beauty of Bali by walking hand in hand with her natural wonders and the noble soul of her people. Partake in the rhythm of daily life, where earth, culture, and spirit entwine to weave a living poem.
Shape your own journey and uncover what is most rare and wondrous in Bali. Discover her beauty through the whisper of forests and the timeless grace of her people, where nature and culture entwine as a living sonnet.
Bali Twin Lake Jungle Trekking & Canoeing
Trek through lush rainforest trails to breathtaking lake views, then glide peacefully across the water on a traditional canoe.
Enter the timeless craft of silver, where fire and hand unite in artistry. Guided by a master artisan, thou shalt shape beauty from raw metal, and carry home a treasure wrought by thine own touch.
Wander softly through the village lanes, where life flows gently as the paddy breeze. Greet the folk, walk the emerald fields, and let each step weave thee closer to the soul of Bali.
Traverse the hallowed path of Bali’s spirit, where the cliffs of Uluwatu whisper to the sea, Tanah Lot rises as a sentinel of the tides, and Taman Ayun blooms in regal grace—a journey through temples where divinity and beauty entwine.
In the hush of intimacy, thou art welcomed into counsel with a Balinese healer, keeper of ancient wisdom. Thereafter unfolds a sacred rite, where tradition breathes through touch and chant, guiding thee into stillness. Thus is revealed a restorative journey, where body, mind, and spirit are bound once more in harmony’s eternal embrace.
Immerse yourself in the art of culinary culture as you learn to craft exquisite dishes from the very first step. Guided by professional chefs, premium spices and handpicked ingredients are transformed into masterpieces that delight both the palate and the soul.

title: Experience a Romantic Villa for Your Honeymoon in Seminyak
content:
Experience a Romantic Villa for Your Honeymoon in Seminyak
Complimentary Shuttle Service
Exceptional Service from Aksari Villa Seminyak
Aksari Villa Seminyak offers a range of personalized services designed to enhance your stay and create unforgettable memories. For couples seeking a romantic escape, the villa provides bespoke experiences such as private candlelit dinners, couples' spa treatments, and all tailored to your preferences. The dedicated staff at Aksari Villa ensures every detail is taken care of, from arranging surprise romantic activities to organizing personalized excursions, so you can focus on enjoying each other’s company.
At Aksari, whose name carries the meaning of God's blessing, every stay opens with a moment set apart from the rest of the world. The Water and Bije Blessing Ceremony marks that beginning, a Balinese tradition offered to you and your partner as you step into this sanctuary together.
Holy water washes over you both in quiet reverence, while bije marks the start of something sacred between you and this island. Nothing about this moment is rushed; it exists simply to still the mind before love takes its place at the center of your stay.
Some blessings aren't meant to end at checkout, and Aksari sends you off with the Tridatu Farewell Ceremony to prove it. A bracelet, woven by hand in the island's oldest colors, is tied gently around each of your wrists before you leave.
It isn't just a keepsake. It's a thread back to this sanctuary, to the stillness you found here, and to the blessing that brought the two of you to Bali in the first place.

title: Stay in a Unique Bali Villa with Luxury and Romance
content:
Stay in a Unique Bali Villa with Luxury and Romance
Experience Seamless Service at Aleva Villa
Aleva Villa goes beyond exquisite design, it’s a unique place in Bali where every moment feels effortlessly personal. Delight in in-villa floating breakfasts, romantic room arrangements, bespoke spa treatments on demand, and round-the-clock attentive service.Thoughtfully managed by Ini Vie Hospitality, an esteemed name of boutique luxury in Bali. Every stay is crafted with warmth and precision. Turn your stay into a memory you'll cherish long after you leave
Every detail at Aleva Villa is designed with intention, starting from the moment you first arrive. We welcome you through the Water and Bije Blessing Ceremony, using holy water and blessed rice, a check-in ritual rooted in Balinese tradition and crafted with the same warmth found in every corner of Aleva.
Holy water is gently sprinkled over you, clearing away all the weight you carried in from outside. Bije is then placed on your forehead, a mark of love and welcome, signaling that you're received here, into Aleva and into Bali.
Intention never fades at Aleva Villa, not even as you prepare to leave. We send you home, or onward to your next destination, through the Tridatu Farewell Ceremony, a parting gesture rooted in generations of Balinese tradition.
Through this ceremony, a bracelet is tied around your wrist, keeping every beautiful memory of this island close. Wherever it travels with you, it carries Bali and Aleva along, a lasting reminder of the warmth found here.

Experience unparalleled hospitality at our honeymoon villa in Bali, thoughtfully managed by Ini Vie Hospitality. Every aspect of your stay is designed to provide comfort, privacy, and unforgettable moments, making it the perfect retreat for couples and honeymooners. Our dedicated team is always ready to assist you, to ensure your stay exceeds expectations.
We didn't want your stay to begin only once the door to your room opens. It begins the moment you first arrive, with the Water and Bije Blessing Ceremony marking your entrance into this sanctuary, welcoming you with warmth into an experience built for intimacy and celebration.
Through this ritual, you're invited into a state of serenity, harmony, and purity, as holy water cleanses the spirit and bije marks the beginning of something new. A meaningful journey unfolds here in Bali, carried forward with you at Astera Seminyak.

Through this ritual, we place a sacred Balinese bracelet on your right wrist, woven with deep symbolism drawn from the Trimurti and its cosmic balance. More than a symbol of strength, steadfastness, and protection, this bracelet becomes something you'll keep close, a lasting thread back to the beauty of Bali and the days you spent here at Astera Seminyak.

Ubud's town center is home to several historical landmarks that showcase intricate Balinese architecture and royal history. Ubud Palace is a historic landmark located in the heart of the town, serving as the official residence of the Ubud royal family. Pura Tirta Empul is one of Bali’s most important water temples, built around a bubbling holy spring. Sacred Monkey Forest is a jungle-enveloped temple complex home to over 1,200 long-tailed macaques.
Ubud is often considered the best place to stay in Bali because it serves as the island's cultural and spiritual heart, offering a stark and tranquil contrast to the bustling beach towns of the south. While areas like Seminyak or Canggu are known for surf and nightlife, Ubud provides an immersive experience into traditional Balinese life, surrounded by lush tropical landscapes.

Discover exceptional hospitality at Asvara Villa, a luxurious villa in Ubud designed to provide a memorable stay amidst tranquil rice fields. Our dedicated team ensures every detail is taken care of, offering personalized services that cater to your needs. Immerse yourself in the perfect harmony of comfort and sophistication at Asvara Villa, your tranquil haven nestled in the heart of Ubud.
We welcome your arrival as something to be honored, beginning your journey here with the Water and Bije Blessing Ceremony. Rooted in centuries of Balinese tradition, this rite draws on sacred water (tirta) and blessed rice (bije) to cleanse the spirit before it steps fully into the island's embrace.
Sacred water is gently sprinkled over your head, carrying away the weight of distant places from your mind, your words, and your soul. Grains of bije are then pressed onto your forehead, an offering of purity and awakening, as Bali welcomes you home.
Farewell is never truly the end, and Asvara Villa marks this parting through the Tridatu Farewell Ceremony. A woven bracelet is gently tied around each of your wrists, a quiet thread binding you both to this island long after you've left its shores.
It rests against your skin as a keepsake of these days together, carrying Bali with you wherever you go next. This is not goodbye, only a pause before the island calls you home again.

title: Discover Maar Resort Ubud: A Secret Retreat in the Heart of Nature
content:
There’s a place in Ubud where time slows down, the air smells of rain-soaked earth, and mornings begin with the sound of rustling leaves and distant birdsong. Maar Ubud, a quiet sanctuary tucked deep in Bali’s highland heart, where luxury feels personal and nature is part of every breath you take.
This isn’t your typical resort stay in Bali. Maar Resort Ubud feels more like a retreat you stumble upon in a dream, a place where you can finally exhale.
Built with Heart, Rooted in Nature
From the moment you arrive, the space feels different. Built from bamboo, reclaimed wood, and locally sourced stone, the architecture doesn’t impose on the land, it blends right into it, creating a gentle and thoughtful sanctuary for two.
Every corner is filled with natural textures, soft light, and the quiet comfort of a space designed to let you breathe. Each structure seems to grow out of the jungle floor, wrapped in greenery and surrounded by rice fields, waterfalls, and tall forest trees that sway as if they’ve been watching over this place for centuries.
Each villa is your own private world. Step outside your door and there it is, a private infinity pool that spills into endless green. Perfect for misty mornings or golden dusks, the view is always changing and always stunning.
Wellness That Goes Beyond the Spa
Introducing Svaha Spa Maar, where wellness is more than just a massage; it’s a journey of healing, rest, and reconnection. Drawing from generations of Balinese tradition, Maar’s signature treatments blend herbal oils, warm stones, and slow, intentional touch.
All this unfolds to the rhythm of flowing water and the quiet life of the forest. For those seeking deeper calm, sound healing under the stars or gentle yoga by the rice fields await, inviting you to pause, breathe, and return to yourself.
Dining That Feels Like Home But Better
Discover Cantina Classe Maar, where food is an act of care. Most ingredients are fresh and locally sourced, thoughtfully selected to celebrate the richness of the land. Each dish is crafted with love and flavor, showcasing what’s seasonal, vibrant, and true to Bali.
For something more intimate, enjoy private dining by the pool or indulge in a personal chef experience with every course tailored just for you. From sunlit lunches to candlelit dinners, every meal feels nourishing, heartfelt, and made with intention.
Experiences You’ll Actually Remember
Days here can be as quiet or adventurous as you like. Float in the public pool under the palms. Wander through nearby rice terraces. Visit Tegalalang, explore Payangan Palace, or take a scenic drive to Kintamani and Mount Batur. You can even try Ayung River rafting if you’re up for it. Maar’s team can arrange anything, always with a smile, never with pressure.
A Promise to the Earth
Maar Ubud was built with care, not just for guests, but for the land itself. From zero-waste practices and renewable energy to organic farming and low-impact design, everything here is shaped around sustainability. You feel it, without anyone having to say it.
Maar Ubud isn’t flashy or loud. It’s thoughtful, grounding, and quietly luxurious. It’s the kind of place you come to rest. And when you leave, you’ll carry a little piece of it with you. Not just in photos, but in how it made you feel: lighter, calmer, more connected.

title: Eco-Friendly Tourism in Bali: Ini Vie Hospitality’s Commitment to Sustainability
content:
Bali is currently placing a strong focus on environmental health, driven by growing concerns over various global environmental issues and their adverse impacts on society. As a result, numerous sectors, including tourism, are prioritizing sustainability initiatives.
Ini Vie Hospitality stands as a prominent contributor to sustainability within the tourism sector. Guided by a vision and mission that aim to create value not only for guests but also for the broader community, Ini Vie Hospitality’s dedication to sustainable practices has been recognized with an award from Eco Tourism Bali, along with both Golden and Silver Badges.
The eco-friendly initiatives are divided into four key categories: resource conservation, pollution reduction, preservation of biodiversity, ecosystems, and landscapes, and social benefits for local communities. Specific actions taken within each category include:
Resource Conservation:
Minimizing plastic use and prioritizing products made from recycled materials
Reducing reliance on single-use products
Repurposing food waste into valuable products, such as crafting jam from surplus fruit, creating body scrubs from coffee grounds, and drying overripe fruits for use as garnishes
Providing waste bins categorized by type to encourage effective recycling
Conserving electricity by configuring various electronic devices for energy efficiency
Managing water resources by installing Ultra-Low Consumption (ULC) systems at each ground tank
Pollution Reduction:
Offering low-emission transportation options, such as electric motorbikes and buggy cars
Recycling food waste into fertilizer
Selling used oil and soiled linens to certified vendors for proper disposal and repurposing
Eliminating the use of fogging practices in daily operations
Conservation of Biodiversity, Ecosystems, and Landscapes:
Establishing local plant nurseries to enhance greenery within villa and resort areas
Participating in mangrove conservation activities with team members
Partnering with Plastic Bank Indonesia to prevent plastic bottles from entering the ocean
Social Benefits for Local Communities:
Prioritizing local vendors and suppliers for villa and resort procurement needs
Creating employment opportunities for residents in surrounding communities
Organizing regular property and area cleaning initiatives
Supporting neighboring villages by providing resources, such as waste bins, for improved waste management
The initiatives outlined above highlight our commitment to being an active participant in the eco-movement within the hospitality sector. As a result of these efforts, seven of our properties have been honored by Eco Tourism Bali, with two properties receiving Gold Badges and five properties awarded Silver Badges.
The recognized properties are as follows:
Kaamala Resort Ubud – Gold Badge
Aksari Resort Ubud – Gold Badge
Canggu Cabana – Silver Badge
Astera Resort Canggu – Silver Badge
Monolocale Resort – Silver Badge
Seascape Resort – Silver Badge
Cyrus Villa – Silver Badge

title: Explore the Symbolism and Flavors of Tsune Japanese Restaurant
content:
When it comes to Japanese cuisine, the essence lies in its focus on fresh, natural ingredients. With minimal seasoning, this culinary tradition celebrates the pure, original flavors of its components, delivering a dining experience that is both simple and exquisite.
This philosophy is beautifully embodied by Tsune Japanese Restaurant in Sanur, where dining transcends into an art form. Tsune offers a luxurious culinary journey, showcasing the elegance of Japanese cuisine, often revered for its simplicity and refined beauty.
Uniquely, Tsune expresses its values in a distinctive way, such as through its ceiling decoration featuring woven wood in the shape of tsubaki flowers, also known as camellia flowers. It’s truly unique, but what does it symbolize?
The Symbolism of Tsubaki: Elegance in Simplicity
The Tsubaki, or Camellia Japonica, holds profound significance in Japanese culture. It symbolizes a beauty that is both simple and elegant, perfectly aligning with the wabi-sabi philosophy, which finds beauty in simplicity and imperfection.
This is the essence Tsune Japanese Restaurant in Sanur seeks to embody in every dish. Using locally sourced ingredients, Tsune masterfully transforms them into luxurious creations that reflect refined simplicity. These exquisite dishes are crafted to be savored, especially when shared with your loved ones, enhancing the joy of dining together.
A Unique Dining Experience at Tsune Japanese Restaurant
Perched on the rooftop of a renowned resort in Bali, Tsune Japanese Restaurant offers more than just a meal—it delivers an unforgettable experience. With breathtaking sea views and an ambiance of refined elegance, Tsune is the perfect destination for a unique culinary adventure.
One of its standout features is the floating sushi, a signature attraction that has captured the attention of many. However, for a truly immersive taste of Tsune’s values and philosophy, the Grilled Fish Set is a must-try.
This dish mirrors the restaurant’s focus on simplicity and harmony, much like its intricate decor and cultural essence. The flavors, though seemingly simple, come together in perfect balance to create a delightful culinary experience.
For an elevated experience, order the Ginhirasu Saikyoyaki Set—a beautifully prepared meal featuring black cod, steamed rice, miso soup, kyabetsu salad, tsukemono, and kobachi. This dish encapsulates the elegance and authenticity that defines dining at Tsune, offering a taste of Japanese culture with every bite.
Visit Tsune Japanese Restaurant in Sanur
Conveniently located at Jl. Aruna No.8A, Sanur, Denpasar, Tsune Japanese Restaurant welcomes guests every day of the week. Operating hours are from 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM, Monday through Sunday.
For reservations and further details, visit their website here and Instagram. Experience the harmony of Japanese cuisine and stunning sea views at Tsune, where every meal is an unforgettable journey.

title: Experience Relaxation and Wellness with Hot Stone Massage
content:
Who doesn’t love a relaxing spa session? Spas offer a wide variety of treatments, each designed to provide specific benefits. Whether you’re seeking relaxation, rejuvenation, or relief from stress, the freedom to choose a treatment tailored to your needs is what makes a spa visit so special. A calm and refreshed body is always the ultimate goal.
Among the many treatments available, one of the most popular is the Hot Stone Massage—a perfect combination of relaxation and therapeutic benefits.
What is Hot Stone Massage?
According to Healthline, Hot Stone Massage is a form of massage therapy designed to promote relaxation, ease muscle tension, and repair damaged tissues throughout the body.
This technique involves the use of smooth, flat stones that are heated and strategically placed on specific areas of the body. These stones, typically made of basalt—a volcanic rock known for its excellent heat retention—help to enhance the therapeutic benefits of the massage by soothing muscles and improving circulation.
Read more: Top 20 Things to Do in Sanur: Explore the Beauty of Southeast Bali
What are the benefits of a hot stone massage?
Hot stone massage is one of the most popular holistic treatments, offering a range of health and relaxation benefits:
Relieves Muscle Tension and Pain
According to Healthline, heat has long been used to alleviate muscle tension and pain. The warmth from the stones helps increase blood flow to the muscles, improving flexibility and relieving discomfort.
Improves Circulation
As noted by WebMD, the combination of heat and massage boosts blood flow and improves circulation. This not only helps reduce pain and inflammation but also promotes faster recovery and healing.
Reduces Stress and Anxiety
Quoting WebMD, heat and massage are excellent for relaxation, but massage goes a step further. The gentle pressure from a massage stimulates the release of endorphins, which relax muscles, ease pain, and improve your mood, leaving you feeling calm and refreshed.
This treatment is a powerful way to rejuvenate your body and mind while promoting overall wellness.
Hot Stone Massage in Svaha Spa
If you’re looking for a luxurious spa experience, Svaha Spa is a must-try. This well-known spa brand in Bali has multiple locations, including Ubud, Canggu, Sanur, and Seminyak, making it easily accessible no matter where you are.
One of their signature treatments is the Hot Stone Massage, which uses carefully selected stones and precise temperature control to ensure a deeply relaxing and rejuvenating experience. For more details and updates, visit their website and follow them on Instagram to explore everything Svaha Spa has to offer.

title: Ini Vie Hospitality Unveils La Mewali Resort & Spa Canggu, a Design-Led Eco-Wellness Sanctuary Shaped by Water
content:
The group’s latest Canggu opening draws its identity from water, expressed through sculptural curved architecture, cave-inspired interiors, and a layered lagoon pool that winds through the entire resort.
Ini Vie Hospitality has announced the newest addition to its expanding portfolio: La Mewali Resort & Spa Canggu, a property that articulates a fresh vision of design-led luxury grounded in eco-wellness. Uniting architecture, water, and sensory-driven hospitality within a single, meticulously conceived destination, the resort is crafted to feel both lived-in and deeply connected to nature. La Mewali will welcome its first guests in June 2026.
The name itself carries the property’s philosophy. “La” means “The,” while “Mewali” draws on the Balinese word for “return,” a homecoming to balance, stillness, and self. That idea takes physical form across the resort in sculptural silhouettes, natural rhythm, immersive water features, and quiet rituals that encourage guests to slow their pace and reconnect.
Set within minutes of Canggu’s beaches, dining hotspots, and vibrant lifestyle scene, La Mewali nonetheless preserves a distinct sense of seclusion, offering connection and retreat in equal measure. Throughout the property, accommodations follow an organic architectural language of softened forms, open-plan living, and a fluid dialogue between indoor and outdoor space.
Where Water Becomes a Way of Living
Guided by a philosophy that turns nature into a lived experience, La Mewali weaves flowing water, sculptural geometry, and tactile materials such as terracotta, stone, wood, and bamboo into the way guests move, feel, and inhabit each space. The resort offers a curated collection of accommodation categories suited to different styles of stay.
One Bedroom Pool Villa with Lagoon Access
King Bed | 75 m² | 2 Adults
Distinguished by a sculptural terracotta form inspired by Pocahan Padi, this villa delivers a cave-like stay with richly textured interiors, a private plunge pool, and direct entry to the resort’s layered lagoon. A hammock and in-room projector complete a setting designed for couples seeking privacy, atmosphere, and immersive tropical living.
King Bed | 40 m² | 2 Adults
Located in the main building with direct access to the flowing lagoon pool, the Suite Lagoon pairs warm contemporary interiors and soft textures with an outdoor bathtub, hammock, and in-room projector, creating a space made for slow, effortless tropical living.
Occupying a corner position for added privacy, the Grand Suite Lagoon offers a more generous footprint, elevated contemporary interiors, direct access to the layered lagoon pool, and an in-room bathtub that deepens the connection to water.
Overlooking the resort’s main pool, the Suite Pool View presents a relaxed, comfortable stay with warm contemporary interiors and a clean, open layout. An outdoor bathtub on the private balcony adds an open-air bathing ritual to everyday tropical living.
Grand Suite Pool View
The most spacious of the pool-view category, the Grand Suite Pool View combines elevated contemporary interiors with a larger, more private layout. An in-room bathtub and refined living area cater to guests who value comfort and openness throughout their stay.
A Journey Through Flavor and Wellness: Wisteria Brunch & Svaha Spa
Dining at La Mewali unfolds in one destination with two distinct identities. Wisteria Brunch sets the tone for unhurried mornings, serving a contemporary breakfast-and-brunch menu built around comforting flavors in an airy setting that blurs indoor and semi-outdoor space. As daylight fades, Puri Pure takes over with an evening-only concept that reimagines modern Indonesian cuisine, elevating local flavors through contemporary technique and considered presentation in a warm, intimate room.
Completing the sensory arc is Svaha Spa at La Mewali, home to Bali’s first Nekara-inspired sound healing experience, a restorative dimension unique to the resort. From lagoon-connected villas and cave-inspired interiors to the sunken swim-up bar and modern Indonesian dining, every element has been deliberately composed to achieve seamless balance.
La Mewali’s facilities are built around comfort, wellness, and closeness to nature. Arrival begins with a personalized ritual: a welcome herbal drink, oshibori service, face mist, and a relaxing shoulder massage with foot wash at check-in.
The layered lagoon pool flows through the property as its connective thread, anchored by a sunken swim-up bar conceived as a laid-back social hub. After dark, a soft illuminated glow transforms the lagoon into an ambient nighttime landscape, while a cave lounge offers a warm, intimate corner for quiet repose.
For movement and wellbeing, the resort provides dedicated yoga and pilates spaces alongside a fully equipped fitness centre. Guest services extend to an EV shuttle, airport transfers on request, concierge assistance, complimentary parking, and curated candlelight dinners for intimate evenings in-resort.
More than a destination, La Mewali Resort & Spa Canggu is conceived as a sanctuary of modern restoration: a place where architecture, water, and sensory experience meet in quiet harmony. From sunrise beside the lagoon to evenings shaped by sound, flavor, and atmosphere, every moment is designed to evoke calm, connection, and contemporary tropical living. For more information and reservations, please visit La Mewali Resort & Spa’s official website.
About Ini Vie Hospitality
Ini Vie Hospitality is a Bali-based hospitality management group with a growing portfolio of more than 90 brands and properties across the island’s key destinations. Spanning luxury villas and resorts, lifestyle venues, curated dining concepts, spa and wellness destinations, and family entertainment spaces, the group specializes in brand development, operations, marketing, and guest experience, building distinctive hospitality concepts defined by strong identity and long-term growth.
La Mewali Resort & Spa Canggu presents a new expression of eco-wellness hospitality in Bali, bringing sculptural architecture, lagoon-connected spaces, curated dining, wellness, and social experiences together within one immersive sanctuary. Designed to balance restoration, privacy, and contemporary comfort, the resort delivers a seamless stay shaped by water, nature, and intentional design.

title: Nyepi in Bali 2026: A Complete Guide to the Day of Silence
content:
Nyepi Day 2026 falls on Thursday, March 19, marking the Saka New Year 1948. The day before, on March 18, the island comes alive with Tawur Kesanga, better known as the ogoh-ogoh festival, where massive, demonic statues are paraded through the streets in a dramatic prelude to the silence.
During Nyepi in Bali 2026, all roads, beaches, and sidewalks are completely closed to everyone including tourists for 24 hours starting March 19 at 5:59 AM. In this guide, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about experiencing Nyepi in Bali.
To really understand what Nyepi Day is in Bali, you have to go back more than two thousand years. Long before the island became a travel hotspot, there was a bitter conflict between tribes in India, the Saka, Pahiava, Yuetchi, Malava, and Kuraka, all fighting for power and land.
It was a violent, unstable time. Eventually, the Saka tribe emerged victorious under King Kaniska I of the Kushana Dynasty. But here’s the thing: King Kaniska knew that winning a war wasn’t enough. He wanted real, lasting peace.
So in 78 AD, instead of throwing a grand victory celebration, he did something unexpected. He created the Saka Year, not as a trophy, but as a symbol of unity, tolerance, and reconciliation. That moment marked the beginning of the calendar that shapes Nyepi in bali today.
Later, this Saka calendar made its way to Indonesia, carried by priests and scholars from India. One name you’ll often hear is Aji Saka, a figure deeply woven into Javanese and Balinese mythology.
When the tradition arrived in Bali, it didn’t stay exactly the same. The Balinese blended it with their own local wisdom, adding a powerful new layer: Penyepian, or complete silence.
So why silence? Philosophically, Nyepi Day in bali is a chance for humans to turn inward. After a year of noise, activity, and yes, the kind of chaos those ancient tribes experienced, we need one day to simply stop. To reflect. To reset.
It’s also a gift to the earth, a rare 24 hours with no pollution, no traffic, no distractions. And if you really want to experience this stillness in the most intimate way, imagine watching it unfold from the peaceful seclusion of a private villa in Bali, where the silence feels even deeper, and the reflection feels even more personal.
Prohibitions During Nyepi in Bali (Do’s and Don’ts for The First Visitor)
If you are wondering when is Nyepi Day in Bali 2026, it falls on March 19, which is a unique time to experience the island’s Day of Silence. It’s important to know that the island will pause completely for 24 hours. Nyepi, often called the Day of Silence, marks the Balinese Hindu New Year and is observed only in Bali, making it a truly unique cultural experience.
During Nyepi Day in Bali 2026, locals observe Catur Brata Penyepian, four sacred rules that guide the day. Here’s what they mean in practice:
Amati Geni (No Fire or Light)
On a spiritual level, this is about cooling the flames of desire within. But practically speaking, it means no lights after dark. The entire island goes dark, homes, streets, everything. No one lights stoves or fires either.
For travelers staying in luxury hotels, you’ll usually still have lights inside your room, but curtains must be drawn tight so not a single ray escapes. Public areas use only the dimmest lighting, if any at all.
Amati Karya (No Work)
This day is made for stillness and reflection, not productivity. Every shop, restaurant, market, and ATM is closed. Even Wi-Fi and mobile data often go quiet.
Emergency services like hospitals and police stay operational, and hotel staff remain on duty to care for guests, but everything happens in near silence, with activities kept to an absolute minimum.
Amati Lelungan (No Travel)
This is the rule you’ll see with your own eyes. The streets are completely empty. No cars, no scooters, no bicycles.
You cannot walk on roads, sidewalks, or even the beach. Bali’s international airport shuts down entirely, no flights in or out. Traditional security, known as Pecalang patrol every corner, gently ensuring no one wanders where they shouldn’t.
Amati Lelanguan (No Fun)
Nyepi is a day for quiet introspection, not entertainment. Loud music, shouting, or any unnecessary noise is forbidden.
Most Balinese don’t watch TV or listen to the radio, and the government often turns off mobile data and broadcast signals across the island to preserve the peace. It’s a full pause, for people, for technology, for the island itself.
The Consequence of Breaking the Rules
Violating the rules during Nyepi can lead to several consequences, both socially and legally, because the day is considered sacred in Bali. The island works together to maintain peace and silence throughout the day.
1. Customary Sanctions
The most immediate consequences usually come from traditional authorities. During Nyepi, Pecalang (traditional security officers) patrol villages to ensure everyone respects the rules. If someone is seen walking outside or using bright lights, the Pecalang will ask them to return to their home or hotel.
In some cases, violators may also receive traditional penalties, such as paying a fine or participating in community service, like helping clean temples or village areas after Nyepi.
2. Administrative and Legal Sanctions
In recent years, enforcement has become stricter through coordination between traditional authorities and the police. People who ignore the rules or disturb public order may be taken to a local guard post or police station until Nyepi ends.
For foreign visitors who commit serious violations such as causing disturbances or refusing instructions from officers, immigration authorities may impose additional sanctions, including possible deportation for disrespecting local regulations.
3. Social Consequences
Balinese communities strongly value collective respect for Nyepi. When someone breaks the rules, the incident can quickly spread on social media, which often leads to public criticism and social pressure for the person involved.
4. Spiritual Impact (for Hindus)
For Balinese Hindus, Nyepi is a sacred time for Mulat Sarira, or self-reflection. Breaking the rules is believed to disrupt personal spiritual balance and interfere with the ritual purification of both the human world (Bhuana Alit) and the universe (Bhuana Agung).
Before Nyepi For Balinese Hindus
As Nyepi Day of the Saka Year 1948 approaches, which falls on March 19, 2026, the Island of the Gods will be bustling with various magnificent and meaningful purification rituals. Here are the important steps taken before the total silence begins:
1. Melasti (Around March 16–17, 2026)
A few days before Nyepi, you’ll witness something magical. Thousands of Balinese Hindus, dressed in pure white traditional clothing, make their way to the sea or to sacred lakes.
They carry Pratima, sacred objects symbolizing divine presence, from village temples. The procession moves slowly, accompanied by soft gamelan music, as locals walk toward the water’s edge.
This ritual is called Melasti, and its purpose is beautifully simple: to wash away all impurities, both within the self and the universe, into the vast ocean. It’s a cleansing of the soul, a reset before the new year begins. Watching devotees in white against the backdrop of Bali’s coastline is a deeply moving sight.
2. Pengrupukan and Ogoh-ogoh Parade (March 18, 2026)
The day before Nyepi, the mood shifts dramatically. Pengrupukan is all about chasing away negative spirits, Bhuta Kala, so they don’t disturb the sacred silence to come. And the way they do it is spectacular.
Enter the Ogoh-ogoh: towering, terrifying statues crafted by village youth to represent evil forces and human flaws. As dusk falls, these giants are paraded through the streets with torches, chanting, and thunderous noise.
It’s loud, chaotic, and absolutely unforgettable. Finally, the Ogoh-ogoh are burned to ashes, symbolically destroying negativity before the new dawn.
Where to experience the Ogoh-ogoh Parade in 2026:
Denpasar (Catur Muka Intersection):
The heart of the action. The best Ogoh-ogoh from across the city gather at this iconic zero-kilometer point for a massive, competitive showcase.
Along Jalan Raya Kuta and toward the beach, the atmosphere is lively and welcoming, with crowds of travelers mixing with locals for a more spontaneous celebration.
If you prefer something more organized, GWK often hosts large-scale Ogoh-ogoh festivals and competitions in a stunning cultural setting.
Local Banjar (Neighborhoods):
For the most authentic experience, just step outside your accommodation. Almost every village parades its own Ogoh-ogoh along local streets, no ticket needed, just curiosity and respect.
What You Can Do For Nyepi Day 2026 in Bali
Just because you can’t step outside doesn’t mean you’ll be bored, far from it. Nyepi might actually be the best day of your trip to slow down and soak in your surroundings in a way you normally wouldn’t.
Total Relaxation with Spa Treatments
With no traffic noise and nowhere to rush off to, Nyepi is the perfect excuse to treat yourself. Many hotels offer special spa packages just for the occasion, and the silence outside makes the experience feel even deeper.
Book a traditional Balinese massage or a soothing herbal bath, and let the stillness do its work. Just remember to reserve a few days in advance; therapists are limited on the day itself, and slots fill up fast.
Explore Hotel Cuisine
Since every restaurant, cafe, and warung outside is closed, your hotel becomes your culinary home for the day. And honestly? That’s not a bad thing. Many hotels go all out with special Nyepi menus featuring local dishes you might not find on a regular day.
It’s a great chance to try something like babi guling Bali (Balinese suckling pig) in the comfort of your hotel, often served with care and ceremony. Some places even set up intimate candlelight dinners, romantic, quiet, and unexpectedly special.
Enjoy the Best Stargazing of the Year
This one stays with people. When the whole island goes dark, the sky comes alive. No light pollution, no headlights, nothing.
If the night is clear, you might just spot the Milky Way stretching above you. Step onto your balcony, lie back in the hotel garden, and look up. It’s the kind of view you can’t get anywhere else.
Many resorts offer gentle yoga or guided meditation on Nyepi morning. And here’s the thing: the air on Nyepi is the cleanest it’ll be all year.
No scooters, no cars, no exhaust, just fresh, quiet air. Breathing that in while you move or sit in stillness? It’s a small kind of magic.
Stay in in Hotel with the Nyepi Package Offering
The smartest way to experience Nyepi is to book a hotel package designed specifically for it. Most resorts across Bali offer special “Nyepi Packages” that usually cover a 3-day, 2-night stay, check-in on March 18th, just in time for the ogoh-ogoh parade, and check-out on March 20th, after the silence lifts.
One worth looking into is from Ini Vie Hospitality. Their “Silence Symphony” package gives you two nights at one of their resorts or villas, with daily breakfast included.
But here’s the nice part: lunch and dinner are also covered with an à la carte breakfast spread, so you don’t have to think about a thing. And if you book through WEINIVIE, you’ll earn extra coins to sweeten the deal. It’s comfort, convenience, and a front-row seat to one of Bali’s most unforgettable days.
Recommendation Accommodation for Nyepi in Bali
1. Aksari Resort Ubud
Aksari Resort & Spa Ubud has become a favorite for couples and travelers who want to experience luxury tucked into nature. Its main pool is hard to forget, terraced like Bali’s famous rice paddies, with a view that drops into a lush green valley.
When it comes to dining, there’s Japanese Teppanyaki at Kojin, and at Ankhusa, you can dive into Balinese food with a contemporary twist. For spa lovers, Svaha Spa Kenderan offers valley views and the calming sound of a river flowing below as you unwind.
For Nyepi on March 19, 2026, Aksari is a peaceful choice. Tucked away in Kenderan Village, it’s far from Ubud’s busier spots.
The silence here feels deeper, more sacred, especially in a traditional village setting. And with no city lights around, the night sky opens up completely. It’s one of those rare places where stargazing on Nyepi becomes something truly special.
2. Asvara Resort Ubud
Another favorite among couples is Asvara, a romantic hideaway in Ubud where privacy comes first. Every villa comes with its own private pool and jacuzzi, and the jacuzzi placement is especially popular, often tucked right next to the bed or pool for that extra touch of indulgence.
Dining here means enjoying contemporary Thai food with a view, as the restaurant overlooks the rice paddies. The setting alone makes the meal feel special. There’s also Svaha Spa Kelusa, where you can unwind with sweeping views of the greenery.
What makes Asvara ideal for Nyepi? The villas are designed with high walls and everything you need inside, pool, jacuzzi, comfort, so you never feel the need to step out. They also offer a 3-day, 2-night Nyepi package that covers breakfast, lunch, and dinner.
Tips for Nyepi Day in Bali
1. Shop for Supplies Early
On Nyepi Day, everything shuts down. We mean everything. Shops, minimarkets, and even pharmacies will be closed. If your stay doesn’t include meals, pick up some instant food, bread, and bottled water a day or two before.
Don’t forget basics like a small first aid kit or any personal medication you might need. Emergency vehicles are only for critical cases, so it’s best to be prepared. Also, ATMs often go offline starting the day before Nyepi, so withdraw enough cash in advance.
2. Prepare for Limited Internet
Mobile data and cable TV are usually switched off across Bali during Nyepi to maintain the silence. The good news? Hotel Wi-Fi typically stays on.
Still, it’s a nice opportunity to embrace a mini digital detox, read that book you’ve been meaning to start, or simply sit still and meditate. You might be surprised how meaningful those quiet hours can feel.
3. Make the Most of Your Accommodation
Hotels in Bali know how to do Nyepi right. Most offer special packages or promotions to keep guests comfortable and well-fed. Meals are often included, and resort restaurants usually remain open for those staying on-site.
So if you’ve booked somewhere with good facilities, you’re already set. Just relax, wander around your hotel, and let the day unfold at its own slow pace.
FAQs About Silent Day in Bali
1. Can we talk on Nyepi Day?
Yes, you can. There’s no rule against speaking quietly in private spaces like your hotel room or villa. That said, the day is all about silence, so keeping your voice low is a simple way to be respectful. Avoid shouting or playing loud music, you never know who might be meditating nearby.
2. Can I walk outside during Nyepi?
No, this one’s strict. Everyone (locals and tourists alike) must stay inside their accommodation. Roads, sidewalks, and even beaches are completely off-limits.
Traditional security officers called Pecalang patrol everywhere to make sure no one is wandering about. The only exception is a genuine medical emergency that requires an ambulance.
3. What can you not do on Nyepi?
The day follows four core rules known as Catur Brata Penyepian. As a visitor, you’re expected to respect them:
No fire or light: Lights shouldn’t be visible from outside your room.
No work: Physical activity and work are paused.
No travel: Stay put, no leaving your hotel or home.
No entertainment: Keep it quiet. No loud music, parties, or noise.
4. Can you eat on Nyepi Day?
Yes, you can. While devout Hindus often fast for 24 hours, tourists are free to eat and drink inside their hotels.
Just keep in mind that all outside restaurants and shops are closed. If your stay doesn’t include meals, it’s smart to stock up on snacks and water beforehand.
5. Is Nyepi only in Bali?
For the most part, yes. The island completely shuts down, and that’s what makes it so unique. Hindus in other parts of Indonesia (like Java or Lombok) also observe Nyepi privately at home or in temples, but life outside Bali carries on as usual.
6. Is the internet available on Nyepi?
It’s limited. Mobile data and cable TV are usually switched off across Bali for the full 24 hours to preserve the silence. Hotel Wi-Fi, however, generally stays on. Essential services like hospitals, police, and the airport keep their internet running too.
There’s something about Nyepi Day 2026 that stays with you long after you’ve left Bali. It’s a full pause, a rare moment when the island breathes and you get to breathe right along with it.

title: Savor the Fire: Shichirin Canggu’s Ultimate Japanese Grill Experience
content:
Fire, Flavor, and Fun: Shichirin Canggu
Looking for an unforgettable dining experience during your summer break? Escape the everyday routine and treat yourself to some amazing food in Canggu. If sushi is on your mind, Shichirin Canggu is the perfect spot for a Japanese feast you won’t forget.
Shichirin Canggu isn’t just about food—it’s about an experience. With their Japanese Konro Grill & Teppanyaki dishes, every meal comes with a fiery live cooking show that’s as exciting as it is delicious. From the moment you walk in, the aroma of smoky spices will have your mouth watering.
Must-Try Dishes at Shichirin
Kick things off with their Fresh Oyster with Shichirin Trio Salsa. Think fresh oysters paired with spicy salsa and a refreshing ponzu sauce. Dining with friends? The Sashimi Set is perfect for sharing and includes tuna, salmon, white fish, ebi, and hotate.
For the main course, meat lovers can’t miss the Gyukatsu Set—breaded santuri wagyu beef served with katsu salad and wasabi. Another favorite is the Saikoro, tender wagyu tenderloin cubes grilled to perfection.
And of course, don’t skip the sushi. Whether you’re a sushi purist or love trying something new, Shichirin’s got you covered. One standout? The Sexy Lady Pink—a fun twist on sushi featuring pink rice, ebi tempura, spicy mentai sauce, tobiko, and more. It’s as Instagram-worthy as it is tasty!
Visit Shichirin Canggu
Shichirin Canggu is more than just great food—it’s about the vibe, the flavors, and the fire-filled cooking show that makes every meal special. Don’t miss out! Follow them on Instagram @shichirinbali or book your table here to make sure you don’t miss the action, especially during busy dinner hours.

title: The Most Iconic Dining Experience: Seven Paintings Ubud, A Once-in-a-Lifetime Culinary Journey at Kaamala Luxury Resort & Spa
content:
Wonderspace is proud to unveil Seven Paintings Ubud, a mesmerizing interactive dining experience that fuses art, animation, and gastronomy. Set in the serene chapel at Kaamala Resort, DITS Asia brings this one-of-a-kind experience to life, redefining the dining scene in Bali.
Launching this week, Seven Paintings Ubud offers guests a unique seven-course culinary journey inspired by the masterpieces of legendary artists such as Da Vinci and Van Gogh. This immersive experience invites diners to explore the creative process behind some of the world’s most iconic artworks through food, flavor, and imagination.
A Dazzling Dining Show at the Da Vinci Table
Guests seated at the Da Vinci table will embark on a sensory journey like no other, where art and food seamlessly come together. The experience invites diners to become part of the masterpiece by creating their own edible art, painting the paper, and spraying the dessert with colors. This interactive process adds an extra layer of fun to each bite, transforming every meal into a participatory work of art.
“At the heart of the Da Vinci table, the boundaries between diner and artist blur. Each course is an artistic tribute, transforming the plate into a canvas while iconic works of art come alive around the table” said Fenty S. Prawiraatmadja, Marketing Director Of Wonderspace. “Our goal is to immerse guests in the art of dining. Seven Paintings Ubud is Bali’s first interactive dinner animation, where guests are not merely watching the artwork unfold—they become the maestros. Each dish is inspired by iconic artists, combining culinary brilliance with a playful, artistic twist. From Da Vinci to Van Gogh, each course served at the Da Vinci table invites diners to unleash their creative side. It’s more than just dining; it’s a celebration of art and culinary craftsmanship.” she concludes.
The Menu: A Masterpiece of Flavors
The Artisan Menu at Seven Paintings Ubud begins with a golden brioche paired with foie gras, fig onion jam, and edible flowers, followed by sliced octopus with truffle anchovies and roasted almonds. Hamachi with green grapes and pickled daikon represents Picasso, while a splash of goma tare with purees embodies Pollock. Braised beef cheek in a Coca-Cola bottle brings a nod to Warhol and a white chocolate soufflé with mashed potatoes and truffle oil evokes Dali. The final course, inspired by Van Gogh, features a white chocolate bar with colorful edible paints.
The Vegetarian Menu includes Michelangelo’s crispy lumpia with sweet corn, Banksy’s grilled vegetables with truffle anchovies, and Picasso’s poached pear with green grapes. Pollock has a splash of spinach and beetroot purees. Warhol offers tofu steak with cauliflower purée, while Dali
presents a white chocolate soufflé. Van Gogh closes with a colorful edible paint-inspired white chocolate bar. Each dish is a vibrant tribute to iconic artists.
Reserve Your Seat Today
This exclusive dining experience invites art and food lovers to indulge in a one-of-a-kind feast is the perfect fusion of food, art, and creativity. Whether you’re an art enthusiast or a food lover, Seven Paintings Ubud offers a unique opportunity to experience Bali in a way like no other.
The event is available from Tuesday to Sunday at 7 PM, and reservations are required due to the intimate nature of the event, with only 16 seats per show. Don’t miss your chance to be part of this extraordinary culinary and artistic journey. The price for this extraordinary experience is:
• Artisan Menu: IDR 850.000++/ person
• Vegetarian Menu: IDR 650.000++/ person
• Kids Menu : IDR 450.000++/ person
To secure your seat at Seven Paintings Ubud, visit www.sevenpaintingsubud.com today and book your unforgettable experience.

title: How Wonderspace Is Driving the Zero-Waste Movement Through Hospitality
content:
Indonesia continues to face a growing challenge in managing food waste, particularly within the hospitality and food service sectors. According to the Ministry of Environment, food waste accounted for 40.79% of the country’s total waste generation, reaching 20.25 million tons throughout 2025.
In response to this challenge, Wonderspace is taking a proactive stance by hosting Nothing Wasted, a platform designed to drive meaningful dialogue and implement real-world hospitality solutions. This commitment is perfectly embodied in their newly opened outlets: Terra Verte, the sustainable culinary concept now operating within Wonderspace, and Equipoise, a newly launched eco-resort designed with a deep sensitivity toward environmental and food waste issues.
Introducing Nothing Wasted: Wonderspace and BRCA Join Forces
Organized by Wonderspace in collaboration with the Bali Restaurant & Cafe Association (BRCA), Nothing Wasted brings together key stakeholders committed to advancing sustainable practices across Bali’s hospitality sector. The event is supported by a diverse network of partners, including Magi Farm, Urban Compost, Eco Tourism Bali, and Revivo Wellness Resort, each contributing valuable insights into hospitality waste management and sustainability initiatives.
Beyond the panel discussions and dining experience, the event also featured a sustainability showcase by Youthopia, a youth-led platform that empowers young people to take action on environmental issues. Through its interactive booth, Youthopia highlighted various initiatives and community-driven projects that demonstrate how Bali’s younger generation is actively contributing to environmental conservation, waste reduction, and sustainable living practices. The presence of Youthopia reinforced the event’s core message that addressing food waste and building a more sustainable future requires participation from all sectors, including the next generation of changemakers.
Inside the Panel: Policy, Composting, and Bali’s New Landfill Regulation
Taking place on June 5, 2026, at Terra Verte Restaurant within Equipoise Resort Ubud, the forum aims to foster meaningful conversations around responsible operations, circular economy practices, and innovative approaches to building more sustainable restaurants Bali. Through collaborative dialogue and knowledge sharing, Nothing Wasted seeks to inspire actionable solutions that can create lasting impact across the industry.
The event opened with a food waste panel discussion featuring industry practitioners and sustainability advocates, who shared practical insights into the challenges and opportunities surrounding food waste in the hospitality and F&B sectors. One of the key topics highlighted was the implementation of the Bali landfill regulation 2026, which restricts landfill access and encourages businesses to adopt independent waste management practices.
Throughout the session, speakers explored a range of solutions on how restaurants reduce food waste, from composting initiatives and waste segregation systems to regenerative approaches that transform organic waste into valuable resources through maggot farming. The discussion provided participants with actionable ideas while showcasing the importance of cross-sector collaboration in addressing food waste challenges.
“Nothing Wasted was created not only to introduce Wonderspace and commemorate World Environment Day Bali, but also to broaden perspectives and encourage meaningful action toward issues that affect us all,” said Nanda Priscilia, Marketing Manager of Wonderspace. “By bringing together different voices and practical solutions, we hope to contribute to the growth of a more sustainable and responsible tourism industry in Bali.”
The evening continued with a curated dining experience overlooking Ubud’s lush rice fields, where guests were invited to explore the principles of zero-waste dining in Bali through a specially crafted menu by Chef Armen. Designed around a holistic use of ingredients, the menu featured dishes such as Fish Satay & Grilled Fish, Pumpkin Puff, Roasted Pumpkin, Pumpkin Custard, and Roast Chicken, demonstrating how thoughtful sourcing and preparation can minimize waste without compromising flavor.
The creativity of the renowned zero-waste chef Bali extended beyond the kitchen and into the bar program. Ingredients that would typically be discarded were transformed into innovative beverages, including the Pineapple Revival, Garden Leftover Cooler, and Second Life Tonic Spritz, alongside a curated wine selection.
Chef Armen’s Zero-Waste Dinner: Sustainability Served on a Plate
Through this immersive culinary experience, Chef Armen highlighted that regenerative hospitality is more than an industry aspiration. It is a practical and achievable approach that can be experienced firsthand, proving that sustainability and exceptional dining can go hand in hand.
Building a more sustainable hospitality industry is not a destination to be reached, but an ongoing commitment embraced every day. Through the combined efforts of government policies, industry innovation, and consumer awareness, the vision of more sustainable restaurants in Bali and a responsible food system is becoming increasingly achievable.
What’s Next for Sustainable Restaurants in Bali
As the movement toward sustainable F&B Indonesia continues to gain momentum, every stakeholder has a role to play. By supporting businesses that prioritize sustainability and adopting more mindful consumption habits, consumers can help shape a healthier, more resilient, and more responsible food ecosystem for Bali and beyond.

At Canggu Cabana Beach Resort, guests are invited to experience the island at a gentler pace, where contemporary design meets the warmth of Balinese hospitality.
