title: Bali in June: Weather, Dry Season Tips and What to Expect
content:
Many travelers don’t realize it, but visiting Bali in June can be one of the best decisions for your holiday. This month is one of Bali’s best-kept secrets, marking the start of the dry season when the weather is perfect for tropical adventures, yet the island is not as crowded as the peak season months of July and August.
If you’re planning a trip in June, there are plenty of things to look forward to. In this guide, you’ll discover everything you need to know about Bali in June, from the weather and travel tips to the best things to do, places to visit, and what to expect during your stay.
What is the Weather Like in Bali in June?
1. Temperature and humidity
June is considered a great month to visit the island, with ideal weather and relatively dry conditions.
Average temperatures range between 26°C and 30°C, while coastal areas can occasionally reach highs of 31°C to 32°C during the day. Humidity levels typically range from 75% to 85%, but June feels noticeably more comfortable than the rainy season.
Sunny days, clear skies, and cooling ocean breezes make exploring the island much more enjoyable. Cooler mornings and evenings open up the day for everything from sunrise walks to sunset dinners by the beach.
2. How many days does it rain in June?
Rain can be refreshing, but when you’re on a tropical holiday, it can sometimes get in the way of your plans. Outdoor activities become more limited, and exploring the island isn’t always as enjoyable when the weather doesn’t cooperate.
Fortunately, June is one of the driest times to visit Bali, with rainfall typically occurring on only 6 to 7 days throughout the month.
As the start of the dry season, June still sees occasional rain, but it is usually light and unlikely to affect your holiday. Most days are dominated by sunny skies and dry weather, making it a comfortable time to explore the island.
Whether you’re planning to go surfing, trekking, hiking, or simply spend more time outdoors, June offers some of the best conditions for enjoying Bali to the fullest.
3. Ocean conditions in June
Sea conditions in June are strongly influenced by Bali’s dry season. The ocean stays warm and comfortable throughout the day.
Visiting Bali in June is ideal if you’re planning to spend time at the beach or enjoy water activities such as swimming, snorkeling, diving, or surfing. Sea temperatures average around 28°C, creating comfortable conditions for long hours in the water.
Popular southern beaches such as Kuta, Nusa Dua, and Uluwatu usually see stronger swells and bigger waves. For surfers, this is prime season in Bali.
Meanwhile, the northern and eastern coasts are typically calmer and offer better underwater visibility, making them excellent spots for snorkeling and diving.
If you’re planning a boat trip to Nusa Penida, the Gili Islands, or Lombok, keep in mind that sea conditions can be rougher during this period. Wave heights may range from around 0.5 to 4 meters, depending on wind conditions and daily weather patterns.
4. June vs. July/August
June to August is part of Bali’s dry season. Since these months fall close together in the same season, many travelers assume they offer a very similar experience.
In reality, there are noticeable differences, especially in crowds, prices, and overall travel conditions.
Crowds: Bali’s crowds in June offer a more balanced and enjoyable atmosphere. As the dry season begins, it falls just before Bali’s peak travel period, so the island feels lively without being overcrowded. Roads are generally less congested, popular attractions are easier to enjoy, and the overall pace feels more relaxed. July/August, on the other hand, marks the start of peak season. Visitor numbers increase significantly, traffic becomes heavier, and many popular attractions can get crowded throughout the day.
Prices: Visiting Bali for a holiday in June is often the smarter choice for budget-conscious travelers. Accommodation rates are usually lower, and it’s still possible to find hotel deals, dining promotions, and activity discounts. By July/August, demand rises sharply, causing hotel prices to increase by as much as 30% to 50% in some areas. Many popular accommodations also sell out quickly, making bookings almost essential.
Weather: Weather conditions in both months are very similar since they fall within the dry season. You can expect plenty of sunshine, low rainfall, and ideal conditions for outdoor activities. The main difference is that July/August tends to be slightly cooler and windier, while June is generally a bit warmer and calmer.
Best Things to Do in Bali in June
If you are wondering what to do in Bali in June, water activities are among the top experiences that should be included in your holiday itinerary on this tropical island. June offers ideal dry-season conditions for enjoying the ocean, with excellent underwater visibility, clear skies, lower humidity, consistent waves, and minimal rainfall.
Visiting Bali in June is perfect for surfing, diving, and snorkeling because the conditions are at their best. Whether you want to ride the waves, explore colorful coral reefs, or discover Bali’s rich marine life, this is a prime time to do it.
For surfers, Bali in June offers some of the best surf conditions of the year, with consistent swells and favorable winds across many of the island’s most popular breaks.
2. Temple and cultural tours
June temperatures in Bali are pleasantly comfortable, and skies are clear and sunny. This makes June a standout choice to enjoy temple visits and cultural tours across the island.
Many of Bali’s iconic temples are located in areas that can be more challenging to access during the rainy season, such as mountain slopes, cliffside locations, and forested regions. In June, the dry conditions make these routes much easier to navigate, allowing you to explore Bali’s spiritual landmarks in greater comfort while enjoying their peaceful atmosphere and natural beauty.
Bali is not just about beaches and temples; the island also offers plenty of exciting outdoor activities, from exploring waterfalls and rice terraces to trekking up mountains. These outdoor adventures are best enjoyed during Bali’s dry season, especially around June, when the weather is generally sunny, and there is very little rain.
While outdoor hiking can be physically demanding, the experience is often incredibly rewarding. Whether it’s watching the sunrise or sunset from a mountain peak, enjoying the refreshing atmosphere of a waterfall or river, or simply unwinding among Bali’s lush rice terraces, these moments can add a whole new dimension to your holiday experience.
4. Beach clubs and sundowners in June light
The finest Bali activities to enjoy in June are visiting a beach club to soak in the sunset and vibrant atmosphere. While beach clubs are worth visiting throughout the year, June offers a particularly enjoyable experience that feels more relaxed and comfortable.
Beach clubs are generally less crowded during this time, allowing you to enjoy the ocean views, lively ambiance, and beachfront setting without feeling overwhelmed by large crowds. June also tends to bring clearer skies and more pleasant weather conditions, creating stunning sunsets that add an extra touch of magic to the experience.
5. Festivals or ceremonies in June
Beyond enjoying Bali’s natural beauty, June is also a wonderful time to experience the island’s rich spiritual and cultural heritage. This month features several important Hindu religious celebrations, as well as cultural festivals that showcase Bali’s traditions, arts, and community spirit.
Here are some of the major events taking place in June 2026:
Hindu Religious and Spiritual Celebrations
Galungan Day: June 17, 2026
Kuningan Day: June 27, 2026
Cultural and Arts Festivals
Bali Arts Festival (Pesta Kesenian Bali): June 13 to July 11, 2026
Karangasem Festival: June 19–22, 2026
Penglipuran Culture Festival: June 9–11, 2026
Best Places to Visit in Bali in June
Uluwatu is a great place to visit in Bali in June, offering dramatic cliffside views and breathtaking ocean scenery. The area is also known for its spectacular romantic villas perched above the cliffs, which makes it an ideal destination for couples looking to enjoy a peaceful and memorable getaway.
June’s clear skies make the experience even more enjoyable, especially when watching the famous Kecak Dance at Uluwatu Temple. Set against a stunning sunset backdrop, the performance is one of the most magical cultural experiences you can enjoy in Bali.
If you’re looking for great beach clubs and surf breaks in Bali during June, Canggu is the place to be. Home to some of Bali’s most popular beach clubs, the area offers a vibrant atmosphere, beautiful sunsets, and endless opportunities to enjoy the island’s laid-back coastal lifestyle.
June is also a fantastic time to go surfing in Canggu, with conditions that attract everyone from beginners to experienced surfers. Whether you’re catching waves, relaxing at a beach club, or simply enjoying the lively beachside scene, Canggu is one of the most exciting destinations to visit in Bali during this time of year.
Moving to the heart of the island, Ubud is also an ideal place to visit in Bali during June. This time of year brings pleasant weather, clear skies, and fresh air, allowing you to fully appreciate Ubud’s lush green landscapes and natural beauty.
The dry conditions also make outdoor activities more enjoyable, whether you’re exploring forest trails, walking through rice terraces, or trekking across the surrounding hills. Beyond its natural scenery, Ubud offers rich cultural experiences that add a deeper and more memorable dimension to your Bali holiday.
West Bali is one of the island’s most underrated regions, yet it can easily become a cool place to visit in June. During this time, the area enjoys sunny weather, refreshing temperatures, remarkably clear waters, and a peaceful atmosphere that feels far removed from Bali’s busier tourist hubs.
June is a great time to explore the natural beauty of West Bali, whether you’re diving in the pristine waters of Menjangan Island or catching waves at the laid-back surf destination of Medewi Beach. With fewer crowds and plenty of outdoor adventures, the region offers a more relaxed and authentic side of Bali that’s well worth discovering.
June’s dry season is the perfect time for island hopping. Be sure to visit the Nusa Islands, including Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan, and Nusa Ceningan, for some of the most breathtaking coastal scenery in the region.
The boat journey may be a little challenging at times due to stronger ocean swells, but the views waiting on the other side make it well worth the trip. Expect crystal-clear turquoise waters, dramatic cliffs, and a peaceful island atmosphere that’s ideal for slowing down and escaping your daily routine.
Bali is incredibly enjoyable to visit in June, with warm sunshine, clear skies, and pleasant weather across the island. It’s a prime time to experience everything from beautiful beaches and cultural attractions to lush landscapes and outdoor adventures.
The favorable conditions also make it easier to spend more time outdoors, whether you’re hiking, surfing, sightseeing, or simply relaxing by the coast. Before your trip to Bali, be sure to check a few June travel tips to help make your holiday smoother, more comfortable, and even more enjoyable.

title: Bali or Thailand: Which is Better for a Holiday in 2026
content:
Choosing between Bali vs Thailand can be tricky since both places offer stunning beauty and endless adventure. These two destinations are among the most popular in Southeast Asia, each with its own vibe and attractions.
Whether you’re after a peaceful, spiritual retreat or a lively, action-packed vacation full of entertainment, both Bali and Thailand have something special. It all comes down to your personal style and what kind of experience you’re looking for. Let’s help you decide between Bali or Thailand, which is better for holiday in 2026!
Location & Accessibility
When it comes to deciding between Bali or Thailand, both offer amazing travel experiences, but Bali has its own unique charm. This Indonesian island, nestled between Java and Lombok, is known for its stunning beaches, lush mountains, and rich cultural attractions.
Getting to Bali is easy, with Ngurah Rai International Airport being the main gateway to the island. It connects Bali to major cities worldwide, with direct flights from places like Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, and Europe.
Domestically, Bali is well-connected with flights from other Indonesian cities like Jakarta, Surabaya, Yogyakarta, and Makassar. A flight from Jakarta to Bali is only about 1.5 hours, and if you’re flying in from Sydney, expect a 5-hour journey.
Thailand, located on the Indochina Peninsula in Southeast Asia, is bordered by Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Malaysia. It offers a variety of destinations, from the bustling streets of Bangkok to the beaches of Phuket, the mountains of Chiang Mai, and the tropical paradise of Koh Samui.
Suvarnabhumi International Airport in Bangkok is the main hub, connecting the city to destinations across the globe. Direct flights come in from Europe, the Americas, Asia, and Australia.
Phuket, Chiang Mai, and Krabi also have major airports that handle both international and domestic flights, making travel around the country smooth and easy. The flight from Jakarta to Bangkok is around 4 hours, and from Sydney to Bangkok, it’s about 8 hours.
Bali and Thailand both have rich cultures, but their traditions and heritage are quite different.
Bali is deeply influenced by Hinduism, which shapes almost every aspect of daily life. The island is the only part of Indonesia with a majority Hindu population, and this religion plays a huge role in the island’s culture, from festivals to rituals.
This island’s spiritual traditions come to life through ceremonies like Ngaben (cremation rituals) and Odalan (temple anniversary celebrations). The culture also shines through in its art and dance. The island is known for its stunning paintings, sculptures, and intricate carvings that often decorate temples.
Traditional dances like Legong, Kecak, and Barong carry deep meanings and are part of religious rituals. The temples are an architectural marvel, made from red brick and wood, blending beautifully with the natural surroundings. These temples are more than just places of worship; they are the heart of many important ceremonies and celebrations.
Thailand has a vibrant cultural heritage shaped by Buddhism, the monarchy, and Malay traditions. Known as the “Land of a Thousand Temple,” Thailand is home to countless wats (Buddhist temples) scattered across the country, each with its own unique story.
The majority of Thais follow Theravada Buddhism, which impacts everything from their daily routines to big celebrations like Songkran (Thai New Year) and Loy Krathong. Buddhist monks are highly respected and play an important role in Thai society, offering spiritual guidance and wisdom.
In addition to its rich religious influences, Thailand is famous for its arts and crafts, like woodcarving, silk weaving, and traditional paintings. Muay Thai, the country’s traditional martial art, is also a major cultural symbol. Thai classical dance and traditional music are also celebrated, with graceful movements that hold deep meaning.
The architecture in Thailand is heavily influenced by Buddhism. Temples like Wat Pho and Wat Arun feature grand structures with towering stupas and stunning Buddha statues. These temples are not just places of worship, but also cultural hubs and centers for learning.
At first glance, Bali and Thailand may seem similar, both are deeply spiritual places with rich religious traditions and ceremonies, influenced by Hinduism and Buddhism. But there are some key differences between the two.
In Bali, Hinduism is the dominant religion, while in Thailand, Buddhism takes the lead. These two religions have their own unique rituals and ways of practicing spirituality.
When it comes to architecture, Bali is famous for its intricate temples and sculptures, while Thailand shines with its impressive wats (Buddhist temples) and stupas.
Bali also stands out for its traditional dances like Legong and Kecak, often performed in religious ceremonies. Meanwhile, Thailand is known for its Khon dance, which tells cultural stories and folklore through dramatic performances.
Activities & Things to Do
1. Adventure Activities
Bali is a playground for adventure seekers, with plenty of exciting activities to get your adrenaline pumping. Here are some of the best adventures you can add to your itinerary in Bali:
This island is a surfer’s dream! With world-famous beaches like Kuta, Canggu, and Uluwatu, there’s a wave for every skill level, from beginners to pros. Canggu is so popular for its laid-back vibe and great surf spots.
For something truly memorable, hike up Mount Batur for an unforgettable sunrise trek. The views from the top are absolutely stunning, making it a must-do for nature lovers and adventurers alike.
Scuba Diving and Snorkeling
If you love the underwater world, Bali has some of the best diving and snorkeling spots, like Menjangan Island, Nusa Penida, and Amed. With vibrant coral reefs and abundant marine life, diving in Bali is an experience you won’t forget.
Bali isn’t just about adventure – it’s also a haven for relaxation and rejuvenation. Holistic wellness is a big draw, especially in areas like Ubud, where you can focus on your body and mind.
If you’re looking to unwind, Bali’s yoga retreats are the perfect escape. In Ubud, you’ll find a variety of programs focused on yoga, meditation, and healthy eating, all designed to help you feel your best.
Health Resorts and Spas
For a full wellness experience, Bali’s luxury health resorts and spas offer traditional Balinese treatments, like relaxing Balinese massages, flower and spice therapies, and other treatments to relax your mind and body.
3. Cultural Activities in Bali
Bali is filled with culture, and there’s no better way to experience it than by diving into its rich traditions.
Bali is home to some stunning temples, each with its own unique charm. You can visit Tanah Lot, famous for its breathtaking sunsets, or head to Uluwatu Temple, which sits on a high cliff offering incredible views of the Indian Ocean. These temples give you a real sense of Balinese spirituality, and they’re great spots to relax and take in the beauty of the island.
Balinese Dance Performances
One of the best ways to connect with Bali’s culture is by watching a traditional Balinese dance. Performances like Legong, Barong, and Kecak are often staged at places like the Ubud Palace and Uluwatu Temple.
These dances tell stories that have been passed down through generations and are a great way to immerse yourself in the island’s heritage. And, yes, Bali is safe, so you can enjoy these cultural experiences without any worries.
1. Adventure Activities in Thailand
Thailand is packed with thrilling adventures for nature lovers and anyone looking for a bit of a challenge.
Thailand is home to some seriously beautiful islands like Koh Phi Phi, Koh Samui, Koh Lanta, and Koh Tao. Island hopping here is a must! You can explore secluded beaches, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, or just soak in the stunning views.
If you love hiking, head to Chiang Mai where you can trek through lush forests, pass waterfalls, and visit small villages. You can even challenge yourself with a hike up Doi Inthanon, the highest peak in Thailand, offering jaw-dropping views of the landscape.
For an adrenaline boost, try zip-lining in Chiang Mai. You’ll soar through the trees and get a bird’s-eye view of the beautiful wilderness, definitely an unforgettable experience.
2. Beach Activities in Thailand
This country’s beaches are world-famous, and there’s no shortage of fun water activities to enjoy.
For crystal-clear waters and diverse marine life, check out Koh Tao and Koh Phi Phi. Snorkeling here is a treat, you’ll get to swim with tropical fish, turtles, and explore vibrant coral reefs.
If you’re into scuba diving, Thailand is a top spot with amazing dive sites like Similan Islands, Koh Lanta, and Koh Phi Phi. You’ll discover underwater treasures like shipwrecks and colorful reefs that make diving here unforgettable.
The beaches offer a bunch of exciting water sports. From windsurfing and kitesurfing to jet skiing, there’s something for everyone. Popular spots like Phuket, Koh Samui, and Koh Phi Phi are perfect places to catch some waves and enjoy the natural beauty around you.
3. Cultural Experiences in Thailand
Thailand is rich in culture and traditions. If you’re looking to dive into the local culture, here are some awesome experiences you shouldn’t miss.
Thailand is home to stunning temples (wats) full of history and beauty. Some must-see temples include Wat Pho and Wat Arun in Bangkok, Wat Phra That Doi Suthep in Chiang Mai, and the mesmerizing Wat Rong Khun (White Temple) in Chiang Rai.
Visiting these sacred places offers a peaceful experience, with jaw-dropping architecture to admire.
Thailand’s night markets have a whole vibe. Chatuchak Market in Bangkok is massive, but you’ll also find unique treasures in markets across Chiang Mai and Phuket.
From local snacks to handmade crafts and clothes, these markets give you a taste of the local life and are perfect for picking up one-of-a-kind souvenirs.
Muay Thai, the traditional Thai martial art, is a huge part of the country’s culture. For a thrilling experience, attend a Muay
Thai match at iconic stadiums like Lumpinee Boxing Stadium or Rajadamnern Stadium in Bangkok. The energy and excitement of the fights are an unforgettable part of Thailand’s cultural scene!
If you’re after adventure, Thailand is packed with islands to explore and incredible diving spots. On the other hand, Bali is perfect for surfers and trekkers, with jaw-dropping volcanic views to take in. So we recommend picking Thailand for adrenaline activities.
For ultimate relaxation, Bali is hard to beat with its abundance of yoga retreats and luxury spas, especially in Ubud. While Thailand, especially Koh Samui and Phuket, also offers amazing spots to unwind, Bali has a stronger focus on spiritual wellness.
When it comes to culture, Bali offers a rich Hindu experience, deeply rooted in ceremonies and festivals. Thailand, with its Buddhist traditions, is also home to stunning temples and meaningful festivals. Which one is more interesting? That depends on what you’re looking for, both offer unique and unforgettable cultural experiences!
Beaches & Natural Beauty
1. Beautiful Beaches
Kuta is the go-to beach in Bali, known for its long stretch of white sand, awesome waves for surfing, and lively nightlife. Whether you’re here to surf, shop, or just chill, Kuta offers something for everyone.
Looking for a peaceful escape? Nusa Dua is where you’ll find calm, crystal-clear waters and luxurious resorts. It’s the perfect spot for a relaxing, romantic retreat, with top-notch facilities to enjoy.
Seminyak is a modern beach destination with a ton of restaurants, bars, and chic boutiques. It can get crowded, but the sunsets here are stunning, and you can kick back with fresh seafood or a cocktail by the beach.
Jimbaran Beach is famous for its seafood dining on the shore. Enjoy fresh seafood as you watch the sun set. It’s a quieter, more relaxed vibe, perfect for a romantic evening by the sea.
2. Unique Landscapes
Ubud’s rice terraces are a must-see! The Tegallalang Rice Terrace is especially famous for its lush, green views. You can take a peaceful walk through the fields or explore nearby villages to really soak in the natural beauty.
Bali is home to some amazing waterfalls, and Ubud has a few of the best. Visit spots like Tegenungan and Gitgit Waterfall to enjoy the refreshing water and stunning scenery. You can take a swim or simply enjoy the calm vibe of these natural wonders.
These island volcanoes are awe-inspiring. Mount Batur is a popular sunrise trek, offering amazing views from the top. If you’re feeling more adventurous, you can try Mount Agung, Bali’s highest peak, for even more spectacular views (though it’s a tougher climb!).
The island of the gods isn’t just about white sand. Lovina and Amed offer unique black sand beaches, perfect for a quieter, more peaceful day by the water. These spots are great for snorkeling or diving, with crystal-clear waters and fewer crowds.
1. Famous Islands and Beaches in Thailand
Phuket is Thailand’s largest island and a top beach destination. Known for its powdery white sand, clear blue waters, and lively vibe, you can enjoy everything from water sports to vibrant nightlife at places like Patong Beach, Kata Beach, and Karon Beach.
Krabi is famous for its dramatic limestone cliffs, crystal-clear water, and stunning beaches like Railay Beach and Ao Nang. It’s also the perfect spot for island-hopping, snorkeling, or just chilling out in paradise.
Koh Samui offers a laid-back vibe compared to Phuket. Chaweng Beach and Lamai Beach have luxury resorts, beachside dining, and nightlife. But for some peace and quiet, you can easily find secluded spots to unwind.
The Phi Phi Islands, made famous by the movie The Beach, boast jaw-dropping views of towering cliffs, turquoise water, and white sandy beaches. Whether you’re into diving, snorkeling, or just soaking in the scenery, this spot is a tropical dream.
2. National Parks and Tropical Forests
Khao Sok National Park
One of the world’s oldest rainforests, Khao Sok offers beautiful lakes like Cheow Lan Lake, towering limestone cliffs, and hidden caves. Activities here include trekking, kayaking, and staying in unique floating houses for a true nature escape.
Mu Ko Ang Thong National Park
Near Koh Samui, this park features over 40 islands with stunning beaches, lagoons, and limestone cliffs. It’s perfect for island-hopping, snorkeling, and hiking to catch breathtaking views of the archipelago.
Erawan National Park
Erawan is famous for its seven-tiered waterfall, where you can trek through lush forests while taking in beautiful natural scenery. It’s the perfect place for nature lovers and adventure seekers.
Chiang Mai & the Northern Mountains
While not on the coast, northern Thailand offers lush mountains, charming villages, and picturesque hiking trails. It’s a great way to explore a different side of Thailand’s natural beauty beyond the beaches.
Bali offers a vibrant mix of party spots like Kuta and Seminyak, but also quiet, romantic beaches such as Nusa Dua and Jimbaran. Thailand has its share of lively beaches like Patong and Koh Phi Phi, but it excels in offering peaceful escapes on islands like Koh Lanta and Koh Samui. So, whether you’re looking for energy or tranquility, each destination has its own unique vibe.
Bali is famous for its lush terraced rice paddies, volcanoes, and unique black sand beaches, offering a one-of-a-kind natural experience. Thailand, on the other hand, is known for its stunning tropical islands, white sand beaches, and dense tropical forests full of diverse wildlife and breathtaking views. When it comes to natural beauty, which is more beautiful, Indonesia or Thailand? It really depends on what kind of scenery you prefer.
Bali offers accommodations for every budget, from affordable stays at places like Aleva Villa and budget guesthouses (IDR 150,000–400,000 per night) to stylish mid-range options like Astera Seminyak and Seminyak Sanctuary (IDR 600,000–1,500,000), and luxury villas with private pools starting around IDR 2,000,000 per night.
Food options range from cheap, authentic meals at local warungs (IDR 25,000–60,000) to mid-range international restaurants (IDR 80,000–150,000), and upscale fine dining with prices between IDR 300,000–1,000,000 per person.
Transportation includes limited public buses, affordable motorbike rentals (IDR 60,000–150,000 per day), car rentals for groups (IDR 350,000–800,000 per day), and cheaper, reliable ride-hailing apps like Grab and Gojek, with fares starting at IDR 20,000
You can stay in guesthouses or homestays, they’re budget-friendly and offer a more authentic Bali vibe than big hotels.
If you are really on a tight budget, skip the fancy restaurant and try local warungs. You can gain more experience from authentic local dishes.
For freedom and savings, renting a motorbike lets you explore at your own pace without breaking the bank. And do not be afraid to use Grab and Gojek, because they can save you money on transport compared to regular taxis.
If you’re traveling on a budget in Thailand, you can find hostels or guesthouses starting around THB 200–500 per night. Street food is super cheap too, usually about THB 40–80 per meal. Getting around with tuk-tuks or local buses won’t cost much either. Plus, low-cost activities like temple visits or checking out night markets are perfect for saving money.
For a bit more comfort, 3- to 4-star hotels run about THB 1,000–3,000 per night, and meals at mid-range restaurants typically cost between THB 150–400 per person. Want some fun? Island tours or Thai cooking classes usually fall in the THB 800–2,000 range.
If you’re looking to splurge, five-star resorts in hotspots like Phuket or Koh Samui go from THB 5,000 up to 15,000 per night. Fine dining meals can be THB 1,000–3,000 per person, and exclusive experiences like private yacht trips or high-end spa treatments start around THB 5,000.
When it comes to travel costs, which is cheaper, Bali or Thailand? Thailand can be pretty affordable depending on your style. Budget stays start around THB 200 a night, while luxury resorts can go up to THB 15,000 or more.
Street food is a highlight, usually costing about THB 40–80 per meal, delicious and filling. Getting around is easy too, with motorbike rentals around THB 200–300 per day and taxis starting at THB 35 plus distance fees.
For traveling between cities, domestic flights can be found for as low as THB 1,000. Activities vary: island-hopping tours in Krabi or the Phi Phi Islands usually cost THB 1,000–1,500, cooking classes around THB 1,000, and top-tier Muay Thai shows start at about THB 1,500. Overall, Thailand offers a range of options to fit most budgets.
Bali’s food scene is a tasty mix of classic flavors, global influences, and healthy options gaining popularity. Don’t miss Babi Guling, a roasted suckling pig dish often enjoyed at special events and top restaurants.
Nasi Goreng (fried rice) comes in all kinds, from simple street versions to creative twists in trendy cafes. Lawar, a mix of veggies, grated coconut, minced meat, and special spices, is another local favorite that gives you a real taste of Bali.
Local Dining Options
If you want authentic flavors without breaking the bank, check out traditional warungs serving up affordable Balinese dishes. Along the coast in places like Seminyak, Canggu, and Jimbaran, you’ll find plenty of beachside cafes where you can enjoy fresh seafood with a sunset view.
Plus, Bali is a hotspot for vegan and vegetarian food lovers, especially in wellness hubs like Ubud and Canggu, where organic and plant-based meals are everywhere.
Thai food is all about bold flavors that mix sweet, sour, spicy, and savory in every dish. You can’t miss Pad Thai, the iconic fried noodles with shrimp, chicken, or tofu, topped with peanuts and a squeez

title: Bali SIM Card Guide for Tourists: SIM and eSIM Options
content:
Staying connected is essential during a holiday, in case you need to search for the best places to eat, locate viral destinations, order transportation, or update your travel on social media. That is why having a reliable SIM card is important for every visitor, especially for a first timer in Bali.
Fortunately, Bali offers many easy and affordable connectivity options, including the increasingly popular digital SIM, which allows you to activate mobile data instantly upon arrival in this romantic destination. Here’s complete information about SIM card and eSIM options in Indonesia, including where to buy them, how to activate them, and which providers offer the best eSIM for Bali.
Where to Buy a SIM Card in Bali?
Physical SIM cards are still widely used in this island, which is also really easy to get. If you prefer a physical SIM card, these are the most reliable options:
Upon arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS), you will find authorized kiosks selling SIM cards. This is the most convenient option, as staff can immediately activate and register the SIM card for you.
Prices here are usually slightly higher than outside the airport, but bargaining is possible to get the best deal.
Some authorized providers allow you to purchase and register a SIM card online before you arrive. You can pick it up at a specific counter at the airport or a city store, which saves time, but make sure you use the official provider’s website to guarantee legitimacy and safety for travelers in the Island of God.
While street vendors are widely available, purchasing a SIM card from general street vendors is not recommended. These vendors may charge inflated prices, and the registration process may not be fully legal or reliable.
Stick to official stores for the best service. If you hire a private driver or a tour guide, you can ask them where to get a trustworthy SIM card for your holiday or even honeymoon in this paradise island.
How to Get an eSIM in Bali
The digital option of eSIM Bali is increasingly popular for its convenience, eliminating the need to swap physical cards. This is also widely used among locals, making it one of the best choices to stay connected on this island.
The easiest way to get an eSIM in Bali is by purchasing it directly from an online platform or an international provider before your trip. You will receive a QR code via email, which you scan to instantly activate the profile on your device, which means your phone is connected as soon as you land.
The Recommendation eSIM is Best for Tourists
When deciding to buy a digital SIM, international providers offer excellent options. Providers like eSIM Bali Saily are highly recommended, as they offer packages specifically designed for travelers. Look for data-rich plans such as eSIM with unlimited data, ensuring you never run out of connectivity while exploring activities in Bali.
Choosing the best one often depends on coverage reliability, competitive pricing, and easy activation, making international providers a convenient option.
FAQs about SIM Card and eSIM
1. What is the biggest provider in Bali?
Telkomsel is the largest and most reliable mobile provider in this island. Their network offers the broadest coverage, especially in remote areas, although if you travel to smaller islands like Lombok or Java, the signal may vary.
2. Which SIM Is Best In Bali?
For tourists prioritizing coverage and speed, Telkomsel is generally considered the best eSIM or SIM card option. XL Axiata also offers competitive plans, while Indosat Ooredoo provides the cheapest eSIM Bali, but occasional promotional pop-up messages may appear.
3. Can I use an International SIM Card in Bali?
Yes, you can. However, international roaming typically offers slower data and very high costs. Purchasing an Indonesian eSIM or a local SIM card is the most practical and affordable choice.
4. What does a SIM card in Bali cost?
Prices vary significantly based on the data package and the point of purchase. Expect to pay anywhere from IDR 100,000 to IDR 300,000 for a package that includes enough data for a two-week trip.
Travel in Bali with Reliable Connectivity at Ini Vie Hospitality Accommodation
Ensuring you have reliable connectivity with your eSIM Bali is the first step; the next is finding the perfect place to stay. All properties under Ini Vie Hospitality are equipped with modern and futuristic electrical features, including fast WiFi, seamless Alexa integration, Netflix access, and modern AirEV charging facilities.
Ini Vie Hospitality is a premium hospitality company in Bali that manages luxurious yet affordable accommodations, ensuring your stay is comfortable, connected, and convenient.

title: 15 Recommended Bali Tattoo Shops with Talented Artists
content:
Bali tattoo shops are renowned not only for their artistry but also for the memorable experience they provide to body art enthusiasts from around the globe. From intricate traditional Balinese patterns to sleek modern fine line styles, body art artists continuously set new standards in design, technique, and hygiene.
If you’re exploring tattoo inspiration or searching for a reliable place with the best tattoo artist Bali has to offer, this list will guide you through some of the most trusted studios on the island. Here are 15 recommended Bali tattoo shops with top-tier artists, specialties, and studio vibes.
1. Seminyak Ink Tattoo Studio
Founded in July 2007, Seminyak Ink is one of the most established tattoo studios in Bali. Known for its clean, calm space, this studio helps guests feel at ease before receiving their body art.
Specializing in realism, geometric, and custom designs, this studio features award-winning artists like Kadek Leo, which is also its owner. Prices begin at IDR 1.5 million, depending on size and complexity.
You don’t need to worry about the safety because this studio is following the Australian hygiene standards and using hospital-grade equipment. Located in a strategic place on Nakula Street, it’s a great pick for anyone staying in nearby Seminyak villas.
Bloodline is famous for its Realistic and Japanese style design and is widely considered one of the best tattoo studios in Bali. Their globally recognized artists are also experts in realism, Chicano, mandalas, and portraits.
This studio operates under Australian standards, ensuring both safety and quality by strictly using disposable grips, tubes, needles, inks, and cleaning all of the equipment with disinfectant for every new client.
The tattoo prices start at IDR 2 million, average among the tattoo shops in Bali. Located in a strategic location in Kuta, it makes this tattoo studio easily accessible from the best villas in Bali.
3. Bali Tattoo Studio Gods Of Ink
As a specialized branch of Bali Tattoo Studio, Gods of Ink focuses on fantasy art and high detail realism. Known for 3D effects and hyperrealistic design, the skin art atelier is led by some of the best Bali artists that have to offer.
Prices start from IDR 1.7 million, slightly higher than average, but justified by the level of detail and quality provided. They also use disposable tubes, grips, and needles, with all of the equipment covered with sterile plastic.
If you’re searching for the best body art studio that is known for lifelike body art, this is a must-visit for guests staying in Seminyak hotels or villas.
Ink Inc is a modern studio with branches across Southeast Asia, including prime locations in Seminyak and Canggu, within walking distance from popular villas in Bali. This studio is a favorite for those seeking traditional, Japanese, mandala, and many other body art styles.
They always ensure a sterile and safe environment with strict sterilization protocols and use disposable needles, tubes, and grips. Prices start from IDR 1 million, offering a relaxed, female-friendly environment that makes it comfortable, especially for first-timers exploring the world of body art in this island of paradise.
5. Charlie Rose Tattoo
Charlie Rose is one of the most popular body art studios in the Canggu area. Known for its lounge-like ambiance and adjoining art gallery, the shop attracts guests seeking neo-traditional and illustrative design.
The studio is named after Kim and Yulia Angel’s daughter, Charly Rose, and was inspired by their love for quality tattooing. Their vision is rooted in ethics and humanity, aiming to create something that brings people together through love, truth, and family.
Getting inked here starts at IDR 1.5 million, with the high hygiene standards following the Western practice with imported quality tattoo equipment and ink. The artists are praised for blending storytelling with technical skill, creating pieces that are both artistic and personal.
Located near Batu Bolong Beach, Canggu Ink Club is a highly rated tattoo shop in Bali with over 2,000 Google reviews. The studio offers a wide range of styles, from traditional to color realism, making it a great place to collaborate with local talent.
What makes it stand out is the hygiene standards that follow the Professional Tattoo Association of Australia with comprehensive standards. They use vegan-friendly and non-animal-tested ink and needles that are imported from trusted Western manufacturers.
Base rates start from IDR 1.3 million. A deposit of 25% of the tattoo charge or a minimum of IDR 500,000 is required, and this deposit is non-refundable. Their friendly community vibe sets them apart, offering one of the best body ink experiences in Bali.
7. Two Guns Tattoo Bali
Two Guns is an Australian-owned studio in Legian that operates above Australian health standards. This Bali studio tattoo has gained popularity among tourists seeking bold and colorful body art designs.
International guest artists frequently visit, and the studio requires a minimum deposit of IDR 500,000. Prices start at approximately IDR 1.5 million for the best quality and design.
This tattoo parlor in Bali is well-known for its safety standards by using single-use needles, cleaning and sterilizing the surface with hydrogen peroxide and alcohol. They also provide aftercare advice and products, elevating their service among customers.
Another standout among tattoo parlors in the Seminyak area, Mason Ink boasts over 10 years of experience. Renowned for spiritual and mandala designs, it’s a top choice for couples seeking matching tattoos in Bali.
This studio is one of the best options, offering a serene and clean atmosphere that reflects professionalism and artistic excellence. The skin art sessions start at IDR 1.6 million, and guests are encouraged to make online bookings in advance.
Once inside, you’ll be welcomed by a calming vibe, ideal for those seeking the best tattoo in Bali with a personalized experience. Adhering to the Australian hygiene standards, Mason uses their hospital-grade sets and equipment.
9. Wave Tattoo Seminyak
Wave Tattoo Seminyak may be new, but it has quickly gained popularity among Bali body art enthusiasts. This parlor specializes in surfer themed and tribal designs, using high quality ink and equipment to deliver stunning results.
Prices are affordable, starting under IDR 1,000,000, depending on size and design. The relaxed, air conditioned space makes it one of the most comfortable Bali tattoo studios for travelers looking to get a tattoo near the beach.
It’s relatively safe for every tattoo enthusiast because this studio uses sterile equipment and properly disinfects their work area.
10. Karma House Tattoo Temple
Looking for a peaceful setting to get body inked in Bali style? Karma House in Ubud is the perfect match. This one-of-a-kind parlor combines inking with wellness, creating a tranquil ambiance especially appreciated by first-timers.
Their Canggu location blends body artistry with yoga and cultural events. Specializing in dotwork and sacred geometry, this is an ideal place to experience tribal tattoos with a spiritual touch.
Rates begin at $100, it’s quite worth it for all the sterile equipment and non-toxic hypoallergenic vegan ink, following the western safety standards. Beyond the body ink, they also host yoga sessions, music nights, and more, making it more than just a parlor for travelers to visit Bali.
11. Artful Ink Tattoo Studio Bali
Established in 1999, Artful Ink is one of the most established parlors, with locations in both Seminyak and Ubud. Founded by Agung Irianto and Paul Martino from Perth, the studio is internationally recognized for its elegant tattoo styles and clean-line precision.
They maintain the high hygiene standards by using single-use and sterile equipment. They also use Italian and Californian ink to maintain design standards.
The session prices start from IDR 1.8 million, with pre-consultation services available for custom work. Known as one of the best tattoo studios in Bali, it delivers an international-level experience for those seeking timeless ink with artistic finesse.
Once an underground studio, Mex has evolved into one of the best tattoo shops in Bali for bold, vibrant designs. Known for American traditional and colorful design, this tattoo studio in Bali attracts both local and international fans.
Mex ensures its client safety by using single-use and sterile needles with equipment that is upgraded regularly. For the skilled artists who prioritize hygiene and creativity, no wonder that their price ranges are a little bit high, from IDR 1.2 to 2.5 million.
The lively atmosphere and walk-in availability make it a hotspot for body ink near popular beach towns like Canggu and Seminyak.
13. Tara Ink Tattoo Studio
Specializing in realistic tattoos, this local tattoo shop is owned by skilled artist Ngurah Tara, who was born and raised in Bali. Located in Tabanan and Kesambi, Denpasar, about a 20-minute drive from Canggu, this studio is the perfect place to get your first tattoo, with prices starting from just IDR 350,000 for small and simple designs.
It can also handle full-leg and full-arm tattoos with refined and intricate designs. Even though it’s a local studio, it follows high Western safety standards by using single-use needles and equipment, high-quality ink, and offering a cozy environment for its customers.
Inspired by the traditional body art culture of Indonesian tribes, Suku Suku Tatau offers a unique experience for travelers who want to connect with heritage through ink. Located in Denpasar, this is one of the few studios offering authentic hand-tapped design.
Even though it’s a local tattoo studio, Suku Suku Tatau maintains high standards of hygiene by using sterile needles and equipment. Their prices start from under IDR 1,000,000, depending on design complexity.
As a cultural studio, visitors love its authenticity; it’s a great way to honor the archipelago’s rich body art history.
15. Balinesia Tattoo Studio
Combining local traditions with contemporary techniques, Balinesia is a must for anyone seeking cultural immersion through body art. Known for Barong masks, floral motifs, and intricate script, this studio stands out for its artistic diversity.
Rates start at IDR 1.3 million, depending on the design. As one of the best tattoo studios in Bali supporting local talent, Balinesia regularly hosts guest artists in a clean, air-conditioned space, with Australian-level sterilization practice and using disposable needles.
Tips for Getting A Tattoo in Bali
There are several important tips to ensure you get the best skin art that you dreamed of. From choosing the right studio to post-ink care, following these tips will help you get the most out of your experience with Bali tattoo shops.
1. Do Your Research and Choose a Reputable Studio
Start by researching studios that showcase strong portfolios and follow certified hygiene standards. Focus on Bali tattoo artists who specialize in your desired style.
Visiting a studio that Bali travelers trust will give you peace of mind and a higher-quality result. Reading reviews, checking healed results, and comparing portfolios will help you find the best tattoo studio in Bali.
2. Understand the Price Range and Quality Expectations
Getting inked in Bali style is often more affordable than in many Western countries. A small piece may cost around IDR 800,000 to 2 million (~ USD 50–130), while medium-to-large tattoos typically range between USD 200 to $600 or more.
A $500 design can often cover a detailed back piece, a half sleeve, or an intricate dinner plate sized design, depending on the artist and complexity. The best tattoo in Bali doesn’t always mean the cheapest; it also means that quality, cleanliness, and artistry matter most.
3. Tip Your Artist Respectfully
Tipping is welcome and appreciated at most studios in Bali, especially when you’re satisfied with the outcome. For a $350 body art, tipping $50 is a kind gesture, and it reflects respect for the artist.
A good tip can also help build a positive relationship if you plan to return for more sessions.
4. Be Mindful of Timing and Aftercare
Avoid booking a session right before swimming, beach days, or intense physical activities. Plan your session at the start of your holiday to allow healing time.
The body art process involves fresh ink that’s sensitive to sun, humidity, and ocean water, factors common in a tropical climate. Avoid getting inked during the rainy season in Bali, and always follow your artist’s aftercare instructions.
5. Communicate Clearly with Your Artist
Come prepared with a clear idea or reference, but be open to suggestions. The best tattoo artist Bali has to offer will know how to adjust your design for better placement, longevity, and balance.
Take your time reviewing the stencil before the session. Most professional studios will walk you through the process, ensuring you feel comfortable and confident.
Final Thought on Tattoo Shops in Bali
With many Bali tattoo shops offering world-class artistry and strict hygiene standards, getting body art is both safe and unforgettable. title: Bali Tourist Tax Explained: What, Why, and How to Pay It
content:
The Bali tourist tax was officially implemented on February 14, 2024, specifically for international visitors. The levy is mandatory for anyone planning a trip to the Island of the Gods, serving as a contribution to preserve the island’s natural beauty and cultural heritage while maintaining its status as one of the most romantic destinations in the world.
This payment, also known as the Bali tourist fee, is separate from your visa and must be paid by every international arrival. Below is detailed information about the levy, explaining what it is, why it has been introduced, and step-by-step instructions on how to pay the Bali tourist levy efficiently.
What is the Bali Tourist Tax?
The tax applies to all international visitors of all ages, including infants, and is charged per person, per entry. The fee is IDR 150,000 (approximately USD 10) and is levied on all foreign visitors entering Bali.
This tax is enforced under Governor Regulation No. 6 of 2023, regarding the International Traveler Tax to Preserve Bali’s Culture and Nature. For first-timers visiting this island of God, note that this is a provincial tax, not a national one, meaning it is separate from your visa, including when using a Visa on Arrival (VoA).
If you leave the island to visit another country or another part of Indonesia and then return (depending on your visa type), you will be required to pay the tourism tax again. This differs from Thailand, where travelers pay a single tourism tax covering air, land, and sea entry throughout the country.
However, this tax applies only to tourists. Those holding student visas, KITAS/KITAP permits, diplomatic status, or work visas are exempt from the levy and are not required to pay this retribution.
Why You Need to Pay The Tourist Tax?
The government introduced the tourist levy to help preserve the island’s unique culture and natural environment. Funds collected from this tax are allocated to projects such as environmental conservation, waste management, and cultural preservation, including the protection of temples, arts, and heritage.
By paying this fee, visitors directly support efforts to maintain the island’s beauty and cultural integrity, addressing concerns from travelers about sustainability and whether Bali is safe and clean. The government also distributes the tax revenue to local Desa Adat (traditional Balinese villages), empowering communities to continue their cultural practices and rituals.
This initiative ensures that tourism remains sustainable, allowing the island to flourish while preserving what makes it one of the world’s top honeymoon destinations.
How to pay the Tourist Tax?
The easiest and most convenient method is to pay the levy online before you arrive, so it won’t affect your activities on the island. This will help you avoid delays at the airport.
Go to the Official Website: Visit Love Bali, the only authorized portal, or download the mobile app.
Enter Your Details: Fill in your full name, passport number, email address, and arrival date.
Make the Payment: Pay the IDR 150,000 fee using a credit or debit card.
Receive Your QR Code: Once the payment is successful, a levy voucher with a unique QR code will be emailed to you.
Save Your Voucher: Keep the QR code on your phone or print a physical copy.
Scan at Arrival: Upon arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport or local seaports, scan your QR code at the designated checkpoint.
While it’s also possible to pay at dedicated airport counters (cashless only), completing the tourism tax payment online process before arrival is faster and more reliable.
Faq’s Bali Tourist Tax
1. Is it mandatory to pay the tourist tax in Bali?
Yes, the tourism tax is a mandatory requirement for all international travelers visiting the island. Exemptions only apply to certain visa holders, such as KITAS/KITAP, diplomatic, and student visa holders, who must apply for exemption through the website before arrival.
2. How much is the tourist tax in Bali?
The tourist fee is IDR 150,000 per person, per entry (about USD 10). Payments are processed in Indonesian Rupiah (IDR).
3. Is there a fine for not paying the tax?
While enforcement is still being strengthened, officials conduct random checks at tourist attractions and airports. If you are found not to have paid, you will be required to settle the tourism tax immediately.
Authorities may issue warnings and could restrict future entry for non-compliance. Stricter penalties are also being reviewed to improve adherence.
4. How to pay the new tourist tax in Bali?
The best option is to pay the tourist levy online before your trip through the official Love Bali website or app. You’ll receive a digital payment voucher (QR code) via email, ensuring a seamless arrival experience.

title: Bali Volcanoes: A Complete Guide to the Island’s Majestic Peaks
content:
As part of the Indonesian Ring of Fire, Bali is home to several magnificent volcanoes, from the towering Mount Agung to the tranquil Lake Batur caldera, which not only defines the island’s dramatic landscape but also shapes the deep spiritual and cultural identity of Bali. Beyond the Bali volcanoes, the island is also graced with non-volcanic mountains that add to its breathtaking natural beauty and ecological richness.
Each volcano here is more than just a geological wonder, it holds profound religious significance in Balinese Hinduism. Here is your complete guide to exploring Bali volcanoes’ stories, eruption records, and travel insights into both active volcanoes and dormant peaks that define the island’s soul.
Active Volcanoes in Bali
Every mountain on this island carries spiritual symbolism and ecological importance. According to the local philosophy of Nyegara Gunung (the unity of mountain and sea), all elements of nature are interconnected. What happens on the mountain affects the ocean and all forms of life.
Volcanoes are seen as sacred homes of the gods, and ceremonies are regularly performed to honor and protect them. In this guide, we’ll explore both the active volcanoes in Bali and their serene dormant counterparts, uncovering what makes each one a breathtaking highlight to include in your Bali itinerary.
1. Mount Agung (Gunung Agung)
Standing at 3,031 meters above sea level in Karangasem Regency, this is the tallest and most active volcano in Bali. It last erupted in 2019, releasing minor ash clouds that caused no major damage but briefly disrupted air traffic, leading to international headlines such as “Bali volcano eruption flights cancelled.”
This volcanic eruption was a reminder of the mountain’s immense power, yet for the Balinese, Mount Agung remains the holiest site on the island. At its slopes lies Besakih Temple, also known as the Mother Temple, regarded as the spiritual heart of the island’s Hinduism.
Climbing is prohibited during active periods, but visitors can admire this sacred peak from surrounding villages like Sidemen or Selat, where the mountain rises majestically over rice terraces and misty valleys. Even when dormant, it stands as a symbol of balance between destruction and creation, the living embodiment of the island’s spiritual resilience.
Located in the Kintamani region of Bangli, Mount Batur is another active volcano in Bali, renowned for its sunrise treks and its majestic Lake Batur caldera. Rising 1,717 meters above sea level, this Bali volcano last erupted in 2000, and it remains one of the most popular Bali destinations for both adventure seekers and spiritual travelers.
Hiking its peak is relatively easy, making it a favorite among beginner hikers. From its summit, the view of the glowing sunrise above the mountains, with layers of mist and shimmering lake reflections, is simply unforgettable.
Despite being an active volcano, this mountain in Bali is safe for trekking under the guidance of local experts who follow official safety procedures.
According to local legend, Mount Batur and Mount Agung are considered symbolic parents of the island, Mount Batur representing feminine, nurturing energy, while Mount Agung embodies masculine strength and divine protection.
Non-Active (Dormant) Mountains in Bali
Beyond its fiery peaks, Bali is also home to a range of non-active mountains that hold both spiritual and ecological importance. These serene mountains are ideal for those seeking peace, nature, and moderate adventure.
While active volcanoes in Bali, like Agung and Batur attract thrill-seekers, these dormant peaks offer a tranquil escape into lush rainforests and misty highlands.
Standing at 2,276 meters above sea level, Batukaru is the second-highest mountain is one of the island and one of its most sacred sites. Unlike the active volcanoes in Bali, this dormant peak is covered by dense tropical rainforest and is home to the revered Pura Luhur Batukaru temple.
The area is part of the Wanangiri–Batukaru Nature Reserve, making it ideal for nature lovers and hikers who prefer quiet, less-traveled trails. However, frequent rainfall can make the trek challenging, so preparation is essential. With its mist-covered slopes and tranquil atmosphere, Batukaru embodies spiritual calm and natural harmony.
Located on the eastern rim of the Batur caldera, Mount Abang rises 2,152 meters above sea level, making it the third-highest peak among the Bali mountains. It’s a dormant peak surrounded by pine forests and peaceful trails, perfect for beginners or those looking to escape the crowds of more famous volcanoes in Bali.
From the summit, hikers are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views of Lake Batur and its surrounding landscapes. The mountain is also home to Pura Tulukbiyu, a sacred temple that holds spiritual significance for the local community.
Also known as Puncak Mangu, Catur stands 2,096 meters above sea level, making it one of the tallest non-volcanic peaks on the island. This mountain is distinguished by two ancient trees near its summit, forming a natural “gate” that welcomes trekkers.
According to Balinese legend, a king from Mengwi once meditated here after losing a war and was blessed with divine insight to rebuild his kingdom. Today, hikers can enjoy stunning views of the Beratan, Buyan, and Tamblingan Lakes, framed by swirling clouds and cool mountain air.
This is also a perfect escape for adventurous couples. Its enchanting lake views make it one of the most romantic places to go in Bali for a honeymoon.
Mount Sanghyang is a hidden gem nestled between Tabanan and Buleleng, surrounded by pristine wilderness. It is surrounded by Mount Pohen, Batukaru, and Lesung, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the Tamblingan Forest and beyond.
Locals often refer to it as the “Twin Mountain” due to its dual peaks. Though less visited by tourists, it’s beloved by locals for its sacred water springs and tranquil trails. The raw, untamed paths make it an ideal destination for explorers seeking a deeper connection with Bali’s natural landscape.
In northern Bali, Mount Patas forms a twin peak with Mount Sanghyang, standing at 1,414 meters above sea level. This dormant volcano offers mild hiking routes and scenic views of forested valleys and traditional villages.
It’s perfect for travelers wanting to experience the island’s quieter northern side, away from crowded tourist hubs. With beginner-friendly trails, Mount Patas is often used by hikers for training before attempting taller peaks like Mount Agung or Mount Batukaru.
Mount Lesung, rising 1,885 meters above sea level, is a favorite among hikers for its breathtaking views of Lake Tamblingan. The mountain is cloaked in dense rainforest, home to hydrangeas and diverse wildlife, creating a magical, untouched atmosphere.
The trek usually takes 2–3 hours starting from Tamblingan Village, making it suitable for first-time climbers. The clean air and unspoiled nature of Mount Lesung offer a refreshing escape from the busier trekking routes of the volcano region.
Located in western Bali, Gunung Merbuk is one of the least-visited peaks on the island due to its secluded location and undeveloped trails. Rising approximately 1,386 meters above sea level, it remains largely unexplored and is best visited with a local guide.
Its pristine surroundings offer panoramic views of rice fields, rivers, and the ocean, providing a rare glimpse of untouched mountains and natural serenity.

title: 4 Dreamy Bamboo Houses in Bali for Your Next Getaway
content:
Bali is world-renowned for its diverse accommodation options, from traditional lumbung huts, boutique hotels, and ultra-modern beachfront villas. However, for a truly immersive and unforgettable escape, nothing compares to staying in a beautifully crafted bamboo house in Bali.
These unique structures blend seamlessly with Bali’s lush environment, offering a tranquil retreat that feels both luxurious and deeply connected to nature. If you are seeking an eco-conscious yet comfortable holiday stay, here are four highly recommended Bali bamboo house options perfect for your next getaway.
Understanding the Concept of a Bamboo House
For centuries, the bamboo house is the most popular architectural design across China, Japan, India, South America, and Southeast Asia due to its strength, versatility, and natural beauty. The concept remains timeless because bamboo is flexible, durable, and perfectly suited for both traditional and modern architecture.
1. Versatile for Every Design
Architect Markus Roselieb from Chiangmai Life Architects explains that bamboo’s tubular shape and reinforced nodes give it exceptional tensile strength that is stronger than steel, while its flexibility allows for organic, flowing designs that blend with nature. Species like Thyrsostachys oliveri provide straight, elegant culms ideal for construction, requiring no paint thanks to their natural aesthetic appeal.
2. Unmatched Durability & Affordable Elegance
Based on Design Like, bamboo is not just a grass but a highly resilient woody material capable of outperforming concrete and steel in durability, making bamboo houses better at handling natural forces. Its wide availability also makes it more affordable than conventional building materials, allowing homeowners to create elegant, well-designed spaces at lower costs.
3. Sustainable and Environmentally Friendly
As one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth, bamboo regenerates quickly after harvesting, ensuring a renewable and eco-friendly supply. It is also carbon-negative, absorbing more carbon dioxide than it emits, making bamboo homes a sustainable choice for environmentally conscious living.
Recommended Bamboo Houses in Bali
Experience architectural artistry and peaceful serenity in these top-rated bamboo villa Bali properties.
1. Equipoise Resort & Spa (Ubud)
Set in the lush and serene Kenderan Village, Ubud, this new resort in Bali offers a peaceful sanctuary with sweeping rice fields and jungle views, while still providing convenient access to central Ubud.
Built with bamboo and reclaimed wood, its semi–open-air interiors create a harmonious blend of nature and comfort, perfect for elevating your Bali holiday package with a soulful, grounding experience.
As an innovative natural material house, Equipoise blends natural materials with high-end comforts, creating an authentic yet luxurious jungle retreat. Guests can enjoy meaningful activities such as Melukat purification at Manuaba Waterfall, rice field exploration, wood carving, and romantic dining at Terra Verte or Riserva, its signature restaurants.
2. Hideout Eco Bamboo House Bali (Selat)
Located in East Bali, Karangasem, Hideout invites guests to disconnect from the busy tourist zones and reconnect with nature. This iconic collection of hand-built Bali bamboo house villas is nestled near Mount Agung, offering dramatic views and complete serenity, an ideal setting for a romantic experience in Bali.
Renowned for its rustic luxury and sustainability, Hideout is a top choice for adventurous travelers seeking a private, eco-friendly stay. Each house offers a distinctive open-air design with calming river views, making it one of the most sought-after and serene villas in Karangasem.
3. Aksari Resort & Spa (Ubud)
Aksari Resort blends the warmth of a natural material house with the refined charm of a luxury resort in Ubud. Surrounded by lush Ubud jungle, many of its villas incorporate innovative Bali bamboo house concepts, giving guests a tropical and serene atmosphere.
Known for its exceptional service, the staff ensures every guest feels welcomed and cared for. The resort features two restaurants, Ankhusa for elevated local cuisine and Kojin for authentic Japanese dining, offering a perfect balance between natural elements, a villa with curated experience, and full resort comforts.
4. Amarea Resort (Ubud)
Located gracefully in the rice fields of Peliatan, Amarea Resort is one of the top resorts and spas in Bali that provides a peaceful hideaway that is quiet yet still close to the vibrant center of Ubud. Natural elements, including bamboo, enhance the ambience of peaceful luxury throughout the resort.
This is an excellent choice for couples seeking a romantic experience in a serene setting, while still enjoying easy access to many things to do in Ubud. Amarea’s beautifully designed accommodations embrace natural materials, creating a tranquil, stylish, and deeply relaxing stay.
Why Choose a Bamboo House for Your Sweet Escape in Bali?
Choosing to stay in a luxury bamboo house in Bali offers more than aesthetic beauty, it is an environmentally friendly and deeply restorative experience. Here’s what makes this type of house sustainable:
Renewable Resource: Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth, making it a highly sustainable building material.
Carbon Sequestration: Bamboo absorbs significant amounts of carbon dioxide, helping reduce the building’s environmental impact.
Natural Cooling: Open-air architecture and the breathable structure promote natural airflow, reducing reliance on air conditioning.
Local Craftsmanship: Every bamboo house in this island supports Balinese artisans skilled in traditional and modern construction.
Minimal Waste: The use of whole bamboo poles helps reduce waste compared to conventional building methods.
