As the burger spots are deployed in many areas in Bali, choosing the right accommodation becomes an essential part of the culinary journey. Ini Vie Hospitality is located in a prime location, right next to some burger spots in Dewata Island.
Booking a room in our accommodation helps the culinary enthusiasts to explore more burger spots without having to be stuck in traffic. Let’s discover more about the best accommodation choice with Ini Vie Hospitality for the best place to stay after having a culinary experience.

title: 27 Top Spots in Canggu for Shopping, Guide for Shopaholics
content:
Canggu shopping offers a unique and laid-back experience compared to the more commercialized areas like Kuta. Here, you’ll find a mix of trendy boutiques, bohemian-chic clothing stores, and artisan markets, creating a relaxed yet stylish atmosphere for shoppers.
In this article, we’ll guide you through the best shopping spots in Canggu, where you can find everything from unique jewelry to stylish clothing. Here are 27 top spots in Canggu for shopping, recommended for shopaholics:
Jewelry Shop in Canggu
1. STACKED by Celeste Canggu
If you’re shopping in Canggu and looking for something unique, STACKED by Celeste is a must-visit. This London-based piercing studio and luxury jewelry brand brings a fun and stylish vibe to Bali, with its eye-catching pink aesthetic that’s perfect for your next Instagram shot. Another reason why Canggu is so popular is that these kinds of shops liven up the area.
They specialize in durable, gold-plated stainless steel jewelry that’s water-resistant, sweat-resistant, and rust-resistant, ideal for those who love the beach or staying active. From rings and earrings to necklaces and bracelets designed for stacking, you can also personalize your pieces at their Charm Bar with a selection of lucky talismans.
For elegant and timeless designs, Serenity Jewelry offers beautiful pieces in 925 Sterling Silver and Rose Gold. With a focus on serene beauty, their collections feature popular motifs like Clover, Symphony, and Daisy, perfect for both everyday wear and special occasions.
If you’re after something even more luxurious, their international collections also include 10k to 14k gold options, ideal for engagement or wedding rings. It’s definitely one of the best shopping areas in Canggu, especially if you’re looking for luxury activities in this area.
3. Barefoot Aristocracy
For a truly unique shopping experience, head to Barefoot Aristocracy, a multi-brand boutique offering a mix of exclusive jewelry brands. This store embodies a “luxury bohemian” style, combining the laid-back freedom of Bali with a touch of high-end sophistication.
They focus on rare and one-of-a-kind pieces, from rings to body accessories, reflecting the high-end Canggu lifestyle. If you’re looking for shops in Canggu that offer something different, this is the place after you laid-back in a nearby cafe.
4. Echo Silver Canggu
Tucked along the creative lanes of the Canggu shopping street, Echo Silver feels like a natural extension of Canggu’s surfy, laid-back soul. Instead of just browsing, you get to dive in and create your own jewelry alongside skilled local artisans in a relaxed, hands-on setting.
Their silver jewelry workshop is the main highlight. You’ll usually work with around 5–7 grams of pure silver to craft a ring, pendant, or bracelet based on your own design.
Want to level it up? You can add gemstones or gold plating for an extra touch. Bonus point: there are plenty of cafés and a great restaurant nearby, so it’s easy to turn your workshop day into a full Canggu outing.
5. Big Tree Jewelry Classes Canggu
Big Tree Jewelry Classes offers a more structured yet still welcoming experience for anyone curious about silversmithing. Popular with beginners, couples, and even families, this studio is easy to reach from Seminyak to Canggu, making it a convenient stop on your Bali itinerary.
They run a wide range of jewelry-making classes, from short 1–3 hour sessions to full-day workshops that go deeper into the craft. You’ll learn classic techniques like cutting, soldering, shaping, and polishing, not only with silver but also brass and wax carving.
If you’re exploring beyond a Canggu shopping mall and want something meaningful to take home, this is a creative experience that truly tells a story.
Women’s Boutique in Canggu
1. Boogieta Boutique Canggu
Boogieta captures the essence of Canggu shopping with its elevated bohemian style and effortless resort elegance. The designs feel feminine, bold, and free-spirited, made for sunny days and slow island living with a touch of luxury.
This boutique is best known for flowing sundresses, beautifully tailored linen sets, and swimwear with unique cuts. Earthy color palettes and exclusive prints make each piece feel special, perfect for moving seamlessly from daytime exploring to a chic beach club moment.
2. GlowGirl Boutique Canggu
GlowGirl is all about looking fresh, confident, and Instagram-ready. With a modern and youthful vibe, it’s a favorite stop when shopping in Canggu for outfits that stand out and follow the latest fashion trends.
Inside, you’ll find party-ready dresses, cute crop tops, stylish mini skirts, and statement accessories. It’s the kind of place you visit when planning sunset cocktails, a stylish dinner, or deciding where to party in Canggu later that night.
3. Cin Cin Batu Bolong
Sitting right on one of Canggu’s most iconic streets, Cin Cin brings a playful mix of retro and modern style. The atmosphere is fun, colorful, and full of energy, instantly putting you in a holiday mood.
Their collections feature bold prints, vibrant colors, and eye-catching designs, from mini dresses and light knit tops to quirky sunglasses and handbags. Perfect for anyone who wants their outfit to feel just as fun as their Bali adventure.
4. Erika Peña Boutique
Erika Peña is a well-known name among the most stylish shops in Canggu, celebrated for its luxurious bohemian flair. The designs feel dramatic yet graceful, blending Latin-inspired romance with Bali’s tropical soul, perfect for moments when you want to stand out.
You’ll find flowing maxi dresses, bold flared skirts, and statement accessories made from light, airy fabrics that move beautifully. Located close to the main shopping street in Canggu, it’s a favorite stop for special events, elegant dinners, or high-end photo shoots, with cafés and even gyms nearby to balance fashion with lifestyle.
Bamboo Blonde is one of Bali’s most loved fashion brands, known for delivering stylish, affordable island wear. It’s especially popular with younger travelers who want to keep up with trends influenced by Australia and Bali’s laid-back fashion scene.
Their collections range from floral dresses and jumpsuits to swimwear and easy accessories, all refreshed frequently with new prints. If you’re exploring the main shopping street in Canggu, this store is a must-visit for effortless holiday outfits you can wear from day to night.
6. Now or Never Bali
Now or Never Bali brings a clean, modern take to shops in Canggu, focusing on an urban-resort lifestyle. The designs are simple, functional, and stylish, ideal for travelers who prefer a minimalist look that works everywhere.
The store offers both women’s and men’s pieces, from quality cotton tees and linen shorts to contemporary swimwear. You’ll also find lifestyle accessories like sunglasses and beach bags, making it an easy stop while exploring Canggu, especially with cafés and gyms nearby to complete the day.
Uma and Leopold is an artisan luxury boutique that beautifully blends island elegance with traditional craftsmanship. The brand focuses on timeless fashion, creating pieces for women who appreciate thoughtful design, fine details, and lasting quality rather than fast trends.
Their collections highlight hand embroidery, delicate beading, and precise laser-cut techniques, resulting in clothing that feels refined yet effortless. From graceful evening dresses to soft silk tops and premium cotton or linen pieces, every item feels carefully made, almost like wearing a piece of art.
Men’s Boutique in Canggu
1. Above the Clouds Natural Wear
Above the Clouds Natural Wear is a boutique rooted in the idea of slow fashion and conscious living. The brand focuses on clothing that feels gentle on the skin and respectful to the planet, using organic fabrics and natural dyes inspired by earthy tones.
Their menswear collection centers on comfort and simplicity, with breathable shirts, relaxed shorts, and everyday essentials made from organic cotton and linen. It’s an ideal choice for men who value comfort, understated style, and sustainability in their wardrobe.
2. Blood+Bone Canggu
Blood+Bone is one of Canggu’s most recognizable lifestyle brands, blending urban street style with laid-back surf culture. The look is clean, masculine, and effortlessly cool, designed for everyday coastal living.
Their range includes premium graphic t-shirts, minimalist printed shirts, and comfortable boardshorts. Known for ultra-soft fabrics and flattering fits, Blood+Bone pieces are easy to wear from morning coffee runs to sunset sessions by the beach.
Le Concept is a thoughtfully curated concept store for men who enjoy fashion with character. With its industrial, gallery-like interior, the store showcases modern, minimalist, and slightly avant-garde designs.
Inside, you’ll find unique menswear such as asymmetrical linen shirts, relaxed silhouettes, and handcrafted leather accessories. Beyond clothing, Le Concept also offers carefully selected lifestyle items, including fragrances, sunglasses, and small art objects that complete a refined, creative look.
Desu Clothing is all about a dark, minimalist look with a strong artistic edge. The brand blends tropical comfort with bold silhouettes, creating pieces that feel modern, slightly mysterious, and effortlessly cool.
Their menswear collections are dominated by black and grey tones, featuring asymmetrical cuts, high-quality t-shirts, relaxed harem pants, and lightweight outer layers. It’s a great choice for those who want to stand out quietly, without loud colors or heavy designs.
KOHEI Men draws inspiration from Japanese minimalism mixed with Bali’s relaxed island vibe. The style is clean, structured, and thoughtfully designed for men who appreciate simplicity done right.
The boutique offers linen shirts, straight-cut trousers, and premium cotton tops in calm, neutral shades. With boxy yet refined fits, KOHEI pieces feel modern, polished, and easy to wear for both casual and smart occasions.
LES.BASICS focuses on elevated essentials, creating timeless wardrobe staples with exceptional quality. The brand emphasizes premium fabrics, ethical production, and designs that never go out of style.
You’ll find ultra-soft organic cotton t-shirts, breathable linen shorts, and lightweight knitwear that are easy to mix and match. Perfect for Bali life, these pieces are made to move seamlessly from relaxed days to casual evenings.
7. Triple J Bali (Jalan Nelayan)
Triple J Bali is more than just a place to shop or eat; it’s a laid-back lifestyle hub that captures Canggu’s creative energy. With its open, modern design, this spot feels like a natural meeting point for surfers, creatives, and digital nomads.
Inside, you’ll find great specialty coffee, wholesome breakfast dishes, and flavorful fusion meals perfect for a relaxed hangout. Triple J also regularly showcases and collaborates with local brands, offering curated lifestyle items that reflect Bali’s youthful, contemporary spirit.
Yasar delivers a calm, futuristic shopping experience built around clean concrete textures and soft LED lighting. The space feels quiet, curated, and intentionally exclusive, making every visit feel personal and refined.
This menswear boutique focuses on contemporary streetwear and elevated essentials. Expect limited-edition shirts, premium t-shirts, and tailored trousers with architectural details, designed for men who want strong character pieces that still feel minimal, modern, and effortlessly polished.
Concept Store in Canggu
1. Fav Concept Store
Fav Concept Store feels like a cozy style stop where Bali’s creative fashion scene comes to life. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it easy to browse and discover pieces that feel both current and effortlessly island-cool.
Inside, you’ll find a thoughtfully curated mix of clothing and accessories that follow modern trends while keeping that free-spirited Bali character. It’s a great place to pick up something stylish that still feels relaxed and wearable.
2. Sun Concept Store
Sun Concept Store is all about celebrating feminine style with a playful, feel-good vibe. The boutique is beautifully styled and designed to inspire women who love dressing up for holidays, parties, or special moments.
Their collection includes statement dresses, stylish sets, and trendy corsets, alongside eye-catching jewelry and accessories. Everything is curated to help you create a polished, standout look without trying too hard.
3. REFERENCE Concept Store
REFERENCE Concept Store blends fashion, art, and lifestyle into one creative space. It’s a favorite for shoppers who enjoy discovering unique pieces with strong design character.
The store features a mix of men’s and women’s fashion, handcrafted jewelry, and artistic home décor from local and international designers. With bold designs and premium materials, REFERENCE is perfect if you’re looking for something a little different and thoughtfully made.
Love Anchor feels like a stylish open-air bazaar where shopping meets art and community. With its traditional wooden structure, glowing chandeliers, and lively atmosphere, it’s one of those places you’ll want to explore slowly, and photograph from every angle, day or night.
More than just a store, Love Anchor brings together local makers and curious travelers in one vibrant space. You’ll find everything from swimwear, linen dresses, and handmade silver jewelry to bohemian home décor, small artworks, and wood crafts.
On weekends, it becomes even livelier as local artisans fill the area with rattan bags, wooden sunglasses, vintage pieces, and other unique finds that capture the creative spirit of Bali.
Sunday Markets in Canggu
1. La Brisa Sunday Market
Held every Sunday inside the iconic La Brisa at Echo Beach, this market feels like a relaxed seaside gathering with a purpose. Built around a zero-waste and organic mindset, it brings together local farmers, eco-conscious brands, and creatives in a setting that opens straight out to the ocean.
Stalls are filled with fresh produce, tropical fruits, wild honey, and homemade jams, alongside sustainable swimwear, linen clothing, and handmade jewelry. You’ll also find natural skincare, aromatherapy candles, woven bags, and bohemian home décor, perfect for slow browsing after a beach walk.
2. The Flea Market (Seminyak / Kayu Aya)
Right in the heart of Seminyak, The Flea Market offers a more polished take on a traditional Balinese market. With permanent stalls neatly arranged under one roof, shopping here feels easy, comfortable, and unrushed.
It’s a great place to pick up Bali-style souvenirs, from breezy summer dresses and beach shirts to straw hats, rattan bags, and silver jewelry. Some vendors even offer custom touches, like name engravings on accessories or leather goods, making your finds feel a little more personal.
Final Thought on Canggu Shopping Spot
Canggu shopping is all about relaxed browsing, creative finds, and discovering styles that feel effortlessly cool. From bohemian boutiques and artisan jewelry studios to lively concept stores and weekend markets, this area turns shopping into an experience rather than a checklist.
After exploring Canggu’s vibrant shopping scene, complete your Bali getaway with a stay that matches the vibe. Discover why Ini Vie Hospitality offers some of the best hospitality experiences in Bali, perfectly located to enjoy Canggu’s lifestyle, dining, and shopping all in one seamless escape.

title: Chef Adalah: Kenali Peran, Jenis, dan Tanggung Jawabnya
content:
Chef adalah aktor utama di balik semua hidangan lezat yang kamu nikmati di sebuah restoran atau hotel. Ia berperan sebagai juru masak profesional yang memimpin dapur atau tim memasak di berbagai industri kuliner.
Dengan kepiawaian tangan, pengetahuan kuliner, dan kepemimpinannya, seorang chef dapat menyulap bahan mentah menjadi hidangan mewah, kaya rasa, dan menggugah selera. Namun, tidak semua orang yang pandai memasak bisa disebut chef. Karena itulah, artikel ini akan mengupas lebih dalam soal profesi yang satu ini, mulai dari pengertian, jenis, tugas, hingga prospek kariernya.
Apa Itu Chef? Pengertian dan Asal Usul Kata
Secara garis besar, pengertian chef adalah seorang profesional dengan keterampilan tinggi di dunia kuliner yang berperan sebagai pemimpin di dapur atau tim memasak. Tugasnya tidak sesempit menyiapkan makanan, tetapi juga mengatur jalannya proses memasak, mengawasi staf, menyusun menu, serta memastikan kualitas rasa pada setiap hidangan yang disajikan.
Kata “chef” sendiri berasal dari bahasa Prancis, “chef de cuisine”, yang memiliki arti sebagai kepala dapur atau direktur dapur. Istilah ini berakar dari bahasa Prancis Kuno yang lahir dari bahasa Latin “caput”, yaitu kepala atau pemimpin.
Dalam sejarahnya, pelopor kuliner modern Prancis, Georges Auguste Escoffier, melembagakan istilah ini sebagai standar kepangkatan profesional dalam dunia memasak melalui sistem brigade dapurnya pada abad ke-19. Sejak itu, gelar chef diberikan kepada juru masak profesional yang tidak hanya memasak, tetapi juga mampu memimpin seluruh operasional dan tim di dapur.
Dengan kata lain, tugas chef tidak hanya bergelut dengan rasa, tetapi juga menjalankan manajemen yang baik dan memiliki kreativitas tinggi. Pada waktu tertentu, ia tidak hanya memimpin dan mengatur tim, tetapi juga harus menciptakan resep baru.
Meski chef sering disandingkan dengan koki dan dianggap sama oleh masyarakat awam, kedua profesi ini sebenarnya memiliki perbedaan cukup signifikan. Chef memiliki peran strategis dan kepemimpinan dalam berlangsungnya sebuah dapur, sedangkan koki lebih fokus pada tugas memasak harian.
Jenis-Jenis Chef Berdasarkan Kitchen Hierarchy
Sebagai orang awam, kamu mungkin melihat bahwa aktivitas di dapur hanya diisi oleh para juru masak yang fokus pada tugas masing-masing. Padahal, dalam dunia dapur profesional terdapat sebuah struktur organisasi atau jabatan yang jelas, di mana setiap chef memiliki tugas dan tanggung jawab yang berbeda-beda sesuai tupoksinya.
Struktur hierarki tersebut dikenal sebagai brigade system, sebuah sistem yang mengatur tingkatan peran di dapur secara sistematis. Tujuannya yaitu untuk memastikan bahwa setiap tugas atau pekerjaan yang berkaitan dengan memasak, mempersiapkan makanan, serta pengelolaan dapur dapat berjalan dengan baik dan efisien.
Adapun jenis-jenis chef berdasarkan sistem hierarki ini adalah sebagai berikut:
Hierarki Dapur (Brigade System)
Executive Chef: Jabatan tertinggi dalam hierarki dapur, biasanya mengawasi operasional kuliner di lebih dari satu dapur atau outlet (misalnya beberapa restoran dalam satu hotel), dengan tanggung jawab penuh terhadap manajemen operasional, perencanaan menu, kontrol biaya, hingga pelatihan staf.
Head Chef/Chef de Cuisine: Kepala chef yang memimpin operasional satu dapur secara langsung sehari-hari, mengawasi berlangsungnya proses memasak, sekaligus memastikan kualitas serta konsistensi hidangan sebelum keluar dari dapur.
Sous Chef: berperan sebagai tangan kanan Head Chef, bertugas menggantikan perannya saat tidak hadir serta mengoordinasikan para chef de partie di masing-masing stasiun.
Chef de Partie: Chef yang memimpin bagian atau stasiun memasak spesifik, seperti bagian pemanggangan atau lainnya.
Commis Chef: Juru masak tingkat pemula atau asisten yang bekerja di bawah arahan Chef de Partie untuk mempelajari setiap stasiun di dapur.
Cook Helper: Bukan seorang chef, melainkan staf yang bertanggung jawab membantu persiapan dasar, seperti mengupas bahan makanan, mencuci, serta menyiapkan bahan dan kebutuhan lainnya.
Selain berdasarkan brigade system, jenis-jenis chef juga dapat dibagi berdasarkan keahliannya, seperti Pastry Chef yang bertugas dalam pembuatan roti, kue, serta hidangan penutup. Saucier yang bertugas sebagai spesialis pembuatan saus, kaldu, hidangan rebus, dan tumis.
Kemudian, Garde Manger berperan sebagai spesialis pembuat hidangan pembuka dingin seperti salad dan sejenisnya. Terakhir, butcher chef bertanggung jawab sebagai spesialis pemotongan, pemisahan, dan penyediaan daging atau unggas sebelum diolah.
Tugas dan Tanggung Jawab Chef
Setiap jenis chef di dapur memiliki tugas dan tanggung jawab masing-masing seperti yang sudah disebutkan di atas. Profesi ini memiliki peran sangat penting sebagai pemimpin manajerial sekaligus kreator hidangan dalam industri F&B (Food and Beverage).
Adapun rincian tugas dan tanggung jawab utama seorang chef adalah sebagai berikut:
Mengatur manajemen operasional dapur, seperti merencanakan menu, mengendalikan biaya, serta memantau inventaris dan pengadaan bahan makanan.
Berperan sebagai pemimpin dan mengelola administrasi, termasuk manajemen staf seperti menyusun jadwal kerja, merekrut, melatih, mengevaluasi kinerja, serta mengoordinasikan tim seperti memimpin pengarahan staf sebelum operasional dimulai untuk memastikan kelancaran.
Menjaga kualitas dan keamanan makanan, termasuk membuat resep standar agar rasa dan mutu hidangan tetap konsisten, serta memastikan kebersihan dan keamanan makanan sesuai regulasi kesehatan.
Mengawasi pelaksanaan teknis, seperti persiapan (mise en place) untuk memastikan semua bahan sudah diracik dan dipotong sebelum waktu memasak dimulai, serta memeriksa setiap hidangan sebelum disajikan kepada tamu agar sesuai dengan standar restoran.
Perbedaan Chef dan Koki
Profesi chef sering kali dikaitkan dengan koki. Banyak yang menganggap keduanya sebagai satu hal yang sama. Meski sama-sama bekerja di dapur, keduanya memiliki perbedaan yang sangat signifikan.
Perbedaan chef dan koki yang mendasar dapat dilihat pada tanggung jawab dan keahlian mereka. Koki umumnya berfokus pada aktivitas teknis seperti memasak dan mengikuti resep, sedangkan chef berperan sebagai seorang pemimpin di dapur yang tidak hanya memiliki tugas memasak, tetapi juga merancang menu, mengatur staf, serta mengelola operasional bisnis sebuah restoran.
Untuk pemahaman yang lebih mendalam, berikut adalah perbandingan utama antara chef dan koki:
Berasal dari kata bahasa Inggris yaitu cook yang berarti memasak atau juru masak.
Berasal dari bahasa Prancis, yaitu chef de cuisine yang artinya kepala dapur.
Bertugas untuk menyiapkan atau mengolah makanan berdasarkan sebuah resep atau arahan dari chef.
Bertugas untuk memimpin dapur, mengatur jalannya operasional, serta mengendalikan dana.
Tanggung jawab utama
Bertanggung jawab untuk memastikan bahwa makanan dimasak dengan baik.
Bertanggung jawab untuk mengelola tim, mengontrol stok bahan, serta menjaga standar kebersihan makanan.
Umumnya, akan menjalankan instruksi teknis, termasuk memastikan kecepatan dan efisiensi jalannya produksi.
Bereksplorasi untuk menciptakan sebuah resep baru, inovasi menu. Serta standar presentasi makanan yang disajikan.
Biasanya akan berkembang dari pengalaman secara langsung selama bekerja di dapur.
Memiliki sertifikasi atau pendidikan formal di sekolah atau akademi kuliner.
Prospek Karier dan Gaji Chef di Indonesia
Profesi chef merupakan salah satu jenis pekerjaan yang cukup diminati di Indonesia. Apalagi di tengah pertumbuhan sektor kuliner dan pariwisata yang cukup pesat di beberapa daerah dalam beberapa tahun terakhir.
Prospek karier chef juga menawarkan jenjang yang jelas dengan gaji yang cukup menjanjikan, mulai dari posisi entry-level hingga puncak kepemimpinan. Setiap levelnya memiliki cakupan kerja yang berbeda-beda, dan tentu saja semakin tinggi levelnya, tugas, tanggung jawab serta pendapatan yang diterima akan semakin besar.
Mengutip dari platform karier seperti Jobstreet dan Indeed, rata-rata gaji pokok untuk profesi ini di Indonesia berada di kisaran angka Rp7.300.000-Rp7.500.000 per bulannya. Namun, nominal tersebut tentu saja sangat bervariasi tergantung pada jenjang karier, tempat bekerja, dan berbagai aspek lainnya.
Adapun estimasi besaran gaji yang diterima oleh chef di Indonesia berdasarkan tingkatannya adalah sebagai berikut:
Commis Chef: Rp3.100.000 s.d. Rp3.600.000 per bulan.
Chef de Partie: Rp3.000.000 s.d. Rp6.000.000 per bulan.
Head Chef / Chef de Cuisine: Rp7.000.000 s.d. Rp10.000.000 per bulan.
Executive Chef: Rp28.000.000 s.d. Rp49.000.000 per bulan.
Perlu diingat, besaran gaji di atas dapat berbeda-beda tergantung pengalaman, lokasi kerja, jenis restoran atau hotel, dan keahlian khusus yang dimiliki. Kota-kota besar atau yang memiliki tingkat pariwisata tinggi seperti Jakarta dan Bali juga biasanya akan menawarkan gaji relatif lebih tinggi dibandingkan dengan kota kecil.
Cara menjadi seorang chef atau berada di posisi puncak seperti executive chef agar bisa mendapatkan gaji yang tinggi tentu saja tidak mudah; dibutuhkan waktu dan pengalaman yang tidak sebentar. Untuk menggapai tingkat tertinggi dalam profesi ini, biasanya harus dimulai dari dasar, termasuk mengikuti sekolah kuliner.
Chef di Dunia Hospitality Bali
Dalam sebuah data yang dibagikan oleh Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Bali, sepanjang tahun 2025 Bali mengalami pertumbuhan ekonomi sebesar 5,82%. Sektor hotel, restoran, dan kuliner menjadi penyumbang terbesar, dengan kontribusi lebih dari 22% dari total nilai ekonomi tersebut.
Data lain menunjukkan jumlah restoran di pulau ini naik hingga 28,16% pada tahun yang sama, sementara 65% pengeluaran wisatawan dialokasikan untuk bidang F&B. Ini membuktikan bahwa Bali memiliki pertumbuhan industri hospitality dan kuliner yang sangat dinamis, sehingga profesi chef dan bidang terkait sangat diminati di pulau ini.
Kebutuhan terhadap chef profesional di Bali terus meningkat setiap tahun untuk segala skala, mulai dari restoran lokal, hotel butik, hingga resor mewah. Tak heran, banyak orang memilih Bali sebagai tempat yang tepat untuk meniti karier di bidang ini, sekaligus menjadikannya panggung untuk bersaing dan berkembang di level pariwisata internasional.
Jika melihat peran chef di hotel, resor, dan vila yang banyak dibangun di Bali, seorang chef memiliki peran yang jauh lebih besar daripada sekadar memasak. Mereka menciptakan cerita kuliner yang menjadi bagian penting dari pengalaman tamu, mulai dari pemilihan bahan yang tepat dan berkualitas, penyajian, hingga momen yang dirasakan saat menyantap hidangan tersebut.
Tren kuliner di Bali juga berkembang pesat, di mana para Executive Chef mulai merespons gaya hidup tamu yang semakin sadar akan asal-usul hidangan yang mereka santap. Banyak chef di pulau ini mulai menyajikan konsep farm-to-table, local sourcing, dan zero waste sebagai standar kuliner baru, di mana chef tidak hanya memasak, tetapi juga berperan penting dalam menjaga keberlanjutan dari hulu ke hilir.
Semangat tersebut tercermin dalam properti-properti iNi ViE Hospitality, setiap resor, vila, hingga restoran berusaha menghadirkan pengalaman kuliner autentik dengan bahan-bahan lokal Bali, mengantar tamu merasakan cita rasa serta cerita pulau ini di setiap suapan.
Di setiap properti iNi ViE, tim dapur memiliki peran besar dalam cerita tamu, menghasilkan hidangan yang tidak hanya lezat di lidah, tetapi juga bermakna dan tak terlupakan, bahkan setelah tamu meninggalkan Bali, baik saat menikmati sarapan terapung (floating breakfast) maupun makan malam romantis di resor.
Meskipun bergelut dalam dunia kuliner dan dapur, chef adalah profesi yang tidak hanya fokus pada memasak, tetapi juga pada kepemimpinan, kreativitas, sekaligus dedikasi untuk menciptakan pengalaman kuliner yang berkesan. Menjadi seorang chef, artinya harus siap dengan berbagai kendala, tekanan, tuntutan konsistensi rasa, serta tanggung jawab dalam memimpin sebuah tim di tengah ritme kerja yang sangat cepat.
Jika kamu tertarik mengembangkan sayap di bidang pekerjaan ini, langkah utama yang harus disiapkan adalah menempuh jalur pendidikan kuliner formal atau magang langsung di dapur profesional. Dari titik ini, kamu akan mulai mempelajari dasar-dasar untuk menjadi seorang chef sekaligus merasakan ritme kerja dapur secara nyata, sebelum akhirnya menapaki jenjang karier yang lebih tinggi di industri ini

title: Chinese New Year 2026 in Bali: Celebrate the Year of the Fire Horses
content:
The Chinese New Year 2026 holiday will be a spectacular time to visit the Island of the Gods, with the official date of this celebration falling on Tuesday, 17 February 2026. According to the Chinese calendar, this festive moment marks the beginning of the Year of the Fire Horse, bringing vibrant energy, passion, and adventure, perfect for families, couples, and groups exploring Bali.
This article is designed to guide you through the best ways to celebrate the 2026 Chinese New Year in Bali, from dining promotions to cultural traditions, especially for those looking for cultural activities while staying in a boutique hotel in Bali. From a lively gathering or a quiet family celebration, here’s how to enjoy your Chunjie in paradise.
Understanding the Chinese Lunar New Year
Based on the traditional Chinese calendar, 2026 welcomes the Year of the Fire Horse, a zodiac sign associated with enthusiasm, courage, and bold transformation. This Lunar New Year encourages fresh starts and dynamic experiences, making it an auspicious time to travel and create new memories.
The celebration is more than a change of date; it is a cultural celebration that influences travel trends, personal rituals, and festive traditions across Asia. Understanding the Fire Horse’s symbolism adds deeper meaning to your holiday, especially when celebrating Imlek 2026 in Bali.
Bali also celebrates the Lunar New Year, locally known as Imlek or Galungan China, reflecting the centuries-old presence of Chinese communities on the island. Interestingly, Galungan is the most important Balinese religious celebration, and the term Galungan Cina highlights the long-standing harmony between Balinese and Chinese cultures.
According to Balinese historian A.A. Bagus Wiriawan, as quoted by Detik Bali, Chinese merchants first arrived on this island through Bali’s northern ports. Their influence remains visible today, from porcelain wall decorations to patra Cina, a Balinese ornamental art style inspired by Chinese motifs.
Celebrate Chinese New Year (Imlek) 2026 in Bali: Year of the Fire Horse
If you’re planning to say Happy Chinese New Year 2026 over a delicious meal, the island offers festive dining experiences to mark the occasion in your Bali holiday packages. During Imlek 2026, several restaurants are hosting special promotions designed to bring luck, prosperity, and togetherness.
For a fun and relaxed celebration with friends, head to Workmates Canggu on 17 February 2026 for The Fortune Feast. Celebrate the Lunar New Year with a lucky twist, spend a minimum of IDR 200,000, and receive an Angpao voucher redeemable for free coffee, ice cream, sliced fruit, or cake.
It’s an easy, cheerful, and also romantic thing to do when you enjoy the spring holiday in Bali together.
Looking for a restaurant in Sanur during the Chinese New Year 2026 holiday? Don’t miss Paed Thai Sanur’s Fortune Feast. From 17–20 February 2026, spend IDR 500,000 and receive a lucky Angpao that may include free dessert, side dishes, or discounts for your next visit. Let bold Thai flavours spark your New Year’s luck.
Things to Do on Chinese New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day for Year-Long Good Luck
To welcome prosperity during the Chinese New Year 2026, there are meaningful traditions you can enjoy even while on holiday. These customs are family-friendly, culturally rich, and easy to include during Imlek 2026 in Bali.
1. Family Dinner with Traditional Dishes
The reunion dinner is the heart of the celebration. According to Tempo, dishes like Siu Mie (Long Life Noodles) symbolise longevity and are a must-have during this celebration. In Bali, you’ll find similar noodle dishes at many Asian and Japanese fusion restaurants, perfect for sharing with loved ones.
2. Clean the House and Decorations
Before New Year’s Day, it’s customary to clean the house to remove bad luck and welcome fresh energy. If you’re staying in a villa in Bali, a simple tidy-up can symbolise a new beginning during the Chinese New Year 2026 holiday. This can also be a fun way to introduce children to cultural traditions.
3. Red Envelopes (Lucky Money)
Exchanging red envelopes or Hong Bao with children or unmarried relatives is a cherished tradition, often accompanied by the greeting “Gong Xi Fa Cai.” When preparing Angpao, avoid using the number 4 (such as IDR 40,000 or IDR 400,000), as it sounds like the word “death” in Chinese culture.
Wearing new clothes, especially in red or gold, symbolises renewal and good fortune. It’s also a great excuse to explore Bali’s boutiques and dress up for a festive dinner while celebrating the tradition.
5. Watching Lion and Dragon Dances
Lion and Dragon dance performances are common during Imlek 2026, especially at malls, hotels, and public venues. These energetic dances are believed to chase away negative energy and bring luck for the year ahead.
Some restaurants in Seminyak and Canggu also perform some of the unique Chinese performances to light up the atmosphere during the Chinese New Year. This means you can combine dinner experiences with the cultural experience to save money and time during holiday in Bali.
Celebrate The Year of the Fire Horse with Ini Vie Hospitality
Make your Chinese New Year 2026 celebration even more special by staying with Ini Vie Hospitality. From festive dining experiences to romantic and family-friendly stays, we offer unique ways to welcome the Year of the Fire Horse in style.
Bali celebrates the new start with vibrant enthusiasm, blending Chinese traditions with Balinese culture. Expect red lanterns lining the streets, special prayers at temples, and festive menus across the island, creating a truly unforgettable way to say Happy Chinese New Year 2026.

title: Christmas in Bali 2025: Best Holiday Packages, Resorts, and Things to Do
content:
Bali, one of the most diverse islands in the world, offers a unique Christmas experience. Although the majority of the population is Hindu, Christmas in Bali is a symbol of cultural tolerance for the Christian community that has lived on the island for decades.
December is an especially popular time for tourists, making Christmas in Bali a lively and unforgettable experience for those who want to swap snow for sand. Here’s your complete guide to celebrating Christmas in Bali, including top activities, dining options, and the best places to stay during this festive season.
Why Must You Celebrate Christmas in Bali?
Christmas in Bali has a special charm, combining tropical sunshine with the island’s vibrant holiday spirit. Here’s why you should consider celebrating Christmas in Bali this year:
Trade Winter Chill for Tropical Sunshine
Swap snowy landscapes and heavy coats for warm sunshine, gentle ocean breezes, and sandy beaches, especially for those who stay in Uluwatu which offers stunning beach and ocean view.
Experience Unique Festive Vibes
Enjoy a magical blend of traditional Christmas cheer and vibrant Balinese culture, complete with stunning tropical decorations.
Offers in World-Class Festive Dining
Savor exclusive holiday set menus, gourmet dinners, and special events at Bali’s renowned restaurants and beach clubs.
Access Special Holiday Wellness Offers
Rejuvenate with discounted spa packages and special treatment promotions available only during the festive season. After enjoying the wellness offers, you can also go shopping nearby since shops in this island are always open even on Christmas.
Where to Dinner to Celebrate Christmas in Bali for Couples or Families
Bali offers a variety of dining experiences for Christmas, with special events and promotions perfect for families or couples. Here are some top options:
Gather your loved ones for a festive evening where celebration meets reward with the special Festive Season at Cantina Classe. Spend a joyful minimum of IDR 1,000,000 between December 24th and 31st and be gifted a special token of the season, a fine bottle of wine, a crafted cocktail, a decadent dessert, or a generous 20% discount.
The lively atmosphere makes every moment sparkle with holiday spirit for those looking for things to do in Canggu with kids or family. It’s the perfect setting to toast to Christmas cheer in Bali.
Imagine a Christmas Eve illuminated by the soulful notes of a live saxophone. From 7 to 8 PM on December 24th, the air fills with music as you savor a curated dinner set menu for IDR 550,000++ per person.
You can enjoy a cured salmon as an appetizer, choose between braised beef cheek or grilled king prawn, and finish with coconut semifreddo, all accompanied by a glass of house wine. Be sure to reserve your table for this memorable festive experience in Ubud on the 24th or 25th.
Step into a cozy, intimate space where Japanese culinary tradition meets Christmas warmth. Available from 2 PM to 9 PM, their festive set menu for IDR 550,000++ includes tuna tataki, miso soup, grilled grouper, and mango mousse.
Guests who spend a minimum of IDR 500,000 will receive a special Santa surprise gift, a delightful way to celebrate the end-of-year holiday season in Canggu. It also offers a convenient location for those staying in a honeymoon resort nearby.
In the heart of Ubud, enjoy a joyful set dinner brimming with festive flavors for your Christmas in Bali. The menu includes red snapper usukuri, comforting crab meat soup, savory chicken teriyaki, and sweet mango mousse.
Each course is paired with house wine or a signature cocktail to elevate your holiday indulgence, creating a perfect Christmas celebration.
Celebrate “Merry Feastmas” at Norii Ubud with a joyful set dinner featuring succulent pork belly, a heartwarming Christmas soup, and your choice of Norwegian salmon or grilled Wagyu sirloin steak.
Finish your festive meal with coconut panna cotta and a festive drink, such as a lychee martini or tequila sunrise. Enjoy every bite and sip as you celebrate with loved ones in Ubud.
Where To Relax and Enjoy Christmas Rejuvenation in Bali
Bali is home to many luxurious spas offering special promotions and events for wellness treatments during the Christmas season. Here are some top spots to unwind and enjoy rejuvenating treatments:
1. Svaha Spa (Canggu Area)
Treat yourself to the gift of tranquility this Christmas season at Svaha Spa’s locations in Berawa, Padang Linjong, Batu Bolong, or Nelayan. Book any one-hour treatment between December 20th and 31st, and as a special festive treat, you’ll receive a complimentary 25-minute massage to extend your relaxation.
This exclusive offer provides a peaceful pause for both in-house and outside guests, making it a perfect way to embrace Christmas in Bali.
2. Svaha Spa Kenderan
Celebrate the season’s warmth with a shared journey of calm and connection. Book a 90 to 120-minute couple’s treatment between December 21st and 31st and enjoy an exclusive 15% discount.
This “Merry Bliss Christmas” promotion is designed for partners to relax and unwind together, offering the perfect serene escape to cap off your Bali at Christmas experience.
Experience pure togetherness and serenity this Christmas with a deeply rejuvenating ritual for two. The Couple Royal Svaha Package offers a 120-minute blissful experience, complete with an exclusive 15% discount from December 20th to 31st.
This offer is perfect for couples seeking a tranquil escape to celebrate the festive season side by side. It’s a beautiful way to create lasting memories during your Christmas dinner in Bali celebration.
4. Svaha Spa Seminyak
Enhance your relaxation this holiday season with an exclusive time upgrade. Book a 60-minute treatment during the morning or evening upgrade windows, from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM or 7:00 PM to 8:30 PM, and enjoy an extended 90-minute session.
This thoughtful extension allows you to enjoy more precious time to unwind, adding an extra layer of peace to your Bali for Christmas experience. This should be on your bucket list of things to do in Seminyak.
Embrace festive wellness throughout December and January with a special treatment that offers a little extra. Book any one-hour treatment and receive a complimentary 15-minute head and shoulder massage to melt away tension.
Alternatively, opt for the Deep Tissue Massage during specified hours to include a luxurious 30-minute jacuzzi bath. This holistic invitation is the perfect way to relax and rejuvenate during the holidays.
Where to Stay in Bali to Celebrate Christmas
For those looking to combine modern luxury with Balinese warmth during the holiday season, here are some of the best places to stay in Bali for Christmas:
1. Kaamala Resort and Spa Ubud
Located in the heart of Ubud near Jalan Bisma, this resort offers proximity to the Sacred Monkey Forest and Ubud Palace. The name “Kaamala” (lotus flower) symbolizes purity and peace, incorporating locally made wood and stone carvings into its design.
Surrounded by lush forests and valleys, Kaamala Resort provides a serene and intimate setting, ideal for families and couples. Its luxury villas come with private pools and hot tubs, perfect for a relaxing Christmas holiday in Bali.
2. Asvara Villa Ubud
Asvara Villa offers a highly private and exclusive experience, nestled amidst tranquil rice fields just outside Ubud’s bustling center. The villas are designed with modern lines and natural accents, framing stunning views of the surrounding paddies.
Each villa features a floating-style jacuzzi and private pool, with extensive romantic amenities perfect for honeymooners seeking seclusion in Bali for Christmas. All of these experiences you can get with a special promotion for Christmas and an end-of-year stay, making it a perfect budget-friendly villa with a private pool.
3. Dedary Resort Ubud
Known for its romantic ambiance, Dedary Resort blends traditional Balinese village charm with luxury. Located about 15 minutes from Ubud’s city center, the resort offers private pool villas with forest or garden views.
Its tranquil setting makes it ideal for honeymooners or families looking to enjoy Christmas in Bali with a perfect blend of luxury and nature.
4. Amarea Resort Ubud
Situated about 5km from central Ubud, Amarea Resort offers a peaceful and artistic retreat surrounded by lush rice fields. This boutique resort, with only 20 rooms, provides an intimate and creative atmosphere.
It’s known for incorporating traditional Balinese bamboo architecture in select areas and offers a serene ambiance with facilities like an infinity pool with forest views and the on-site Norii Japanese Restaurant, perfect for a Christmas dinner in Bali.
True to its name, Suara Alam offers seclusion while being only an 8-minute drive from Ubud’s center. Located in the midst of deep jungle and rice paddies, this resort focuses on connecting guests with nature through a modern, sleek design.
It offers tranquility and intimacy with three public pools overlooking the jungle, making it a perfect choice for a peaceful Bali at Christmas.
Known for its unique Balinese coastal style, Seascape Sanur offers a blend of green landscaping and modern luxury. The “Oasis Pool” resembles a beachside lagoon, and it features ocean-view suites and 1-bedroom pool villas.
This peaceful location is perfect for a romantic getaway with easy access to Sanur Beach and the harbor, offering an ideal Christmas dinner in Bali experience with a relaxing coastal charm.
7. Astera Resort Canggu
A “smart resort” that features in-room Alexa speakers and integrated streaming services, Astera Resort offers a seamless experience with its private pools and spacious, contemporary villas. Located near Padang Linjong, it balances the high energy of Canggu with the intimacy needed for a honeymoon.
Astera Resort also provides easy access to the vibrant hubs of Canggu, making it an excellent choice for Christmas in Bali.
8. Cabana Resort Canggu
Situated on Jalan Nelayan, Cabana Resort is just a short distance from Canggu and Berawa beaches. This resort features a unique design with an infinity pool and offers a relaxing retreat for couples who still want to be close to the action.
The Grand Cabana Rooftop Seaview rooms offer spectacular ocean views, making it a perfect spot for a romantic Christmas holiday in Bali.
9. Sini Vie Resort Seminyak
Known as a “Haven of Romance and Modern Elegance,” this romantic hotel in Seminyak is designed for adult guests seeking luxury, privacy, and proximity to Seminyak’s vibrant lifestyle. It features sleek, contemporary architecture with villas that offer private pools, air-conditioning, and high-end amenities.
With its prime location near Seminyak Square and Eat Street, it’s an ideal choice for those wanting to enjoy both a peaceful Bali at Christmas and the convenience of Seminyak’s attractions.
10. Aksari Villa Seminyak
This contemporary yet private sanctuary offers only 14 units of 1-bedroom villas, each designed for ultimate privacy. Equipped with private pools and Jacuzzis, Aksari Villa is perfect for couples seeking a peaceful escape during Christmas in Bali.
Located in a quieter area of Seminyak, it offers tranquility while remaining central, making it the perfect place to unwind and celebrate the holiday season.
Bali Weather in December
Before planning your December trip to Bali, it’s important to understand what to expect from the weather in Bali at Christmas. December marks the Bali rainy season, but the weather still offers plenty of opportunities to enjoy the island’s beauty.
Beginning of the Rainy Season
December signals the start of Bali’s rainy season, bringing high humidity and warm temperatures. While it is wetter than other months, Bali remains a tropical paradise with plenty of sunshine mixed with occasional showers.
Consistently Warm Temperatures
Expect daily temperatures averaging between 27°C and 32°C. These warm, consistent temperatures are perfect for tropical beach holidays and casual resort attire, making it an ideal time for outdoor activities during the day.
Afternoon Rainfall Pattern
Occasional heavy rain showers are common in December, typically in the late afternoon or evening. These downpours are usually brief, so they won’t significantly disrupt your plans but may offer a refreshing break from the heat.
Ample Morning Sunshine
Mornings in Bali are usually sunny and clear, offering the perfect weather for beach visits, tours, and outdoor adventures. You can enjoy a peaceful start to your day before the afternoon rain arrives.
Festive Spirit Unaffected
While rain is common in December, it rarely impacts Christmas celebrations in Bali. The showers are typically short-lived and followed by fresh, warm evenings.
Most Christmas events are held indoors, so you can still enjoy the festive atmosphere despite the weather.

For those planning to spend Christmas in Bali, Ini Vie Hospitality offers the perfect accommodations for a memorable holiday experience. Our resorts and villas provide luxurious comfort for couples and families alike, ensuring your stay is filled with warmth and festive joy.
We offer excellent service and access to fantastic events, so you can enjoy your Bali at Christmas in style. Visit our website for more information on the best holiday options and accommodations in Bali.

title: Coffee Shops Canggu: 14 Local Favorites and Hidden Gems
content:
For coffee lovers, Canggu delivers more than just a good cup. The area’s café scene has grown into a full lifestyle experience. Shaped by Australian specialty standards, locally roasted beans, and an easygoing Bali atmosphere that makes lingering over coffee feel like the natural thing to do.
From long-standing roasteries to hidden neighborhood gems, here are 14 of the best coffee shops in Canggu to explore.
Best Specialty Coffee Shops in Canggu

title: 18 Coffee Shops in Ubud with Cozy Spaces for Digital Nomads
content:
Coffee shops in Ubud is more than just a place to grab your morning brew, it’s a whole vibe. Surrounded by rice fields, jungle, and a slower pace of life, Ubud is the ultimate spot for anyone chasing peace, nature, and inspiration. From the lush Monkey Forest to endless yoga studios and art spaces, this town is where you come to slow down and reconnect.
And if you’re a caffeine lover, you’re in luck. Ubud has a buzzing coffee culture with spots that aren’t just about good beans, but also about unique experiences. Whether you’re a digital nomad looking for a cozy corner or just want to sip coffee with a view, here are 18 coffee shops in Ubud worth checking out:
1. Ubud Coffee Roasting
Tucked away on Jalan Goutama Selatan, this little gem is often called a secret spot, quiet, cozy, and perfect if you need focus without the hustle. With solid Wi-Fi and a few sweet treats like croissants and donuts, it’s great for working or just relaxing.
The real star here is the coffee. As a true roastery, they serve speciality coffee Ubud style with beans roasted in-house. If you’re a coffee purist, this is easily one of the best coffee shops in Ubud to check out when you’re deciding what to do in Ubud beyond temples and rice fields.
2. Suka Espresso [Ubud]
If you’re after good vibes, Suka Espresso is one of the best cafés in Ubud. Spacious and lively with two floors of seating, it’s a hotspot for digital nomads thanks to its fast Wi-Fi and all-day menu. Think pancakes, smoothie bowls, hearty brunches, and consistently excellent Aussie-style coffee.
Their brews are top-notch, which is why Suka is often mentioned among the best coffee shops in Ubud. Plus, the location is unbeatable, right on Jalan Raya Pengosekan, near Monkey Forest and Ubud Art Market, making it a perfect pit stop on your things to do in Bali list.
3. Monkey Cave Espresso
Right across from the entrance of Ubud Monkey Forest, Monkey Cave Espresso is a cozy spot with indoor and outdoor seating that feels laid-back and welcoming. Head up to the second floor and you’ll find a breezy view of the street, a favorite perch for remote workers.
The Wi-Fi is reliable, the vibe is calm, and the menu has more than just coffee, think sandwiches and smoothies for quick bites. But what really makes it shine is the brew. Many say their espresso rivals Australia’s finest, which easily puts it on the list of best coffee Ubud has to offer. With its strategic location and stylish setup, it doubles as an Instagrammable café Ubud visitors love to post about.
4. Prince Coffee & Kitchen
If you prefer a quieter escape, Prince Coffee & Kitchen on Jalan Gaotama is like a hidden gem in the middle of Ubud. With its small, homey vibe, it’s perfect for getting work done in peace. The coffee here is consistently praised, but what makes it stand out is the full food menu, from Asian to Western dishes, breakfast to dinner, so you can happily camp out for hours.
Whether you’re a digital nomad or just exploring between luxury hotels and top resorts in the area, this spot feels both functional and welcoming. Definitely one of the best cafés in Ubud for comfort, great flavors, and that cozy-local charm.
5. Titik Temu Coffee – Ubud Palace
If you’re hunting for the best coffee shop in Ubud, Titik Temu is a solid pick. With its semi-open design filled with wood accents and greenery, the vibe is super cozy and refreshing. There’s even a floor-seating area that’s perfect for getting work done.
People love it here because it’s “laptop-friendly” with good Wi-Fi, so you can sip and type in peace. The menu is varied enough for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, and their single-origin coffees are a must-try. Definitely a great stop after exploring the rice fields or waterfalls in Ubud.
6. Namaskara Coffee & Superfoods
Namaskara is another favorite when it comes to the best coffee shop in Ubud, especially if you’re after a calm, productive spot. With modern-meets-Balinese decor and strong Wi-Fi, it’s ideal for working or video calls.
The menu is all about healthy, mostly plant-based eats like smoothie bowls, avocado toast, and falafel wraps. Coffee lovers will appreciate their organic specialty brews, while non-coffee fans can go for superfood lattes like matcha or adaptogen blends. It’s the kind of place that feels good for both body and mind.
7. Anomali Coffee Ubud
If you’re looking for a solid work-friendly spot, Anomali Coffee is a go-to in central Ubud. The space is big, with air-conditioned indoor seating, an outdoor area, and plenty of communal tables perfect for digital nomads. The Wi-Fi is fast and stable, and there are tons of power outlets; no wonder it’s often packed with laptop warriors.
The menu ranges from hearty brunch plates and pancakes to cakes and snacks, plus they roast their own beans sourced from all over Indonesia. Many say it’s some of the best coffee in Ubud. Conveniently located on Jalan Raya Ubud, it’s super easy to reach, especially if you’re staying nearby at one of the luxury hotels in Ubud or grabbing dinner later at an Indian restaurant Ubud style.
Tucked away in the quiet Nyuh Kuning area, Blend Cafe is all about calm vibes and rice paddy views. It’s the kind of coffee shop in Ubud that feels homey, with fast Wi-Fi and a few handy power outlets for getting work done.
Their menu leans healthy, with smoothie bowls that are almost too pretty to eat, plus plenty of plant-based meals and breakfast favorites. The coffee here is strong, delicious, and slightly unique compared to other cafes. Perfect if you want a peaceful escape from Ubud’s busy center before heading out to explore temples, markets, or even a cozy Indian restaurant in Ubud for dinner.
If you’re hunting for the best coffee shop in Ubud with artsy vibes, Lazy Cats is a gem. The space feels vintage-bohemian, filled with cozy sofas, communal tables, and plenty of quirky artwork. It’s the kind of spot where you can easily lose track of time, whether you’re working, people-watching or just chilling.
The Wi-Fi is solid, power outlets are available, and the menu leans vegetarian and vegan, with smoothies, hearty breakfasts, and healthy bites. Don’t skip their pastries, they’re perfect with a cup of their smooth brews. Perched on the second floor of Jalan Raya Ubud, it offers quiet vibes and a nice view of the street below.
10. Monsieur Spoon Ubud
For fresh pastries and some of the best coffee Ubud has to offer, Monsieur Spoon is a must. This French bakery-turned-café has a chic, modern look with plenty of seating, including an outdoor area overlooking rice fields. It can get busy, but the fast Wi-Fi makes it a favorite for digital nomads.
Their croissants, breads, and brunch plates are baked daily and pair perfectly with their consistently excellent coffee. Located on Jalan Hanoman, it’s right in the heart of Ubud, easy to reach and worth the buzz if you love buttery pastries with your caffeine fix.
11. Watercress Cafe Ubud
If you’re after a spot with tropical, rustic vibes, Watercress Cafe is the place to be. With its open-air design, cozy communal seating, and breezy atmosphere, it’s the kind of café where you can settle in with your laptop or just chill over brunch. The Wi-Fi is strong and reliable, making it digital-nomad approved.
The menu is all about wholesome, organic goodness, from colorful superfood bowls and fresh salads to their famous “Watercress Benny.” Pair it with a cup of their excellent locally roasted coffee, and you’re set for the day.
12. Milk & Madu Ubud
A favorite among digital nomads, Milk & Madu combines a modern, stylish setting with plenty of seating both inside and out. You’ll find power outlets everywhere and Wi-Fi that rarely lets you down, which explains why it’s always buzzing with people working or catching up.
The menu is diverse and generous, think hearty breakfasts, wood-fired pizzas, and big portions that look as good as they taste. Their coffee game is strong too, making it one of the most popular café hangouts in Ubud. Located on Jalan Suweta, with sister cafés in Canggu and beyond, it’s a must-try for great food and caffeine in Bali.
13. BGS Ubud – Coffee Bar & Lifestyle Shop
If you’re looking for a calm and cozy spot to sip coffee and get work done, BGS is a gem. The space is minimalist with Balinese accents, giving off a laid-back vibe perfect for focus. Seating is limited, so it’s best to come early to grab a good spot. The Wi-Fi here is fast and reliable, no wonder it’s a favorite among remote workers.
But the real star is the coffee. BGS roasts its own locally sourced beans, so every cup has that rich, authentic taste. Their almond milk latte is especially popular, and you can pair your brew with light bites like pastries or cakes. Tucked away on Jalan Raya Mas, just outside central Ubud, it’s a quieter alternative to the busier coffee shops in town.
With its airy design and natural touches, Ivy Cafe is a stylish yet comfy spot in central Ubud. You can choose to sit indoors or outdoors, both are great whether you’re working on your laptop or just chilling out. The Wi-Fi is fast and dependable, and the menu is packed with fresh, healthy options from breakfast and brunch to hearty mains. Their coffee is smooth and consistent, with plenty of choices to keep you fueled. Located on Jalan Raya Ubud, just a short walk from the Monkey Forest, Ivy manages to feel relaxed despite being in a busy area.
True to its name, HOME Cafe feels warm, cozy, and… well, like home. It’s the kind of place where you can settle in for a few hours of focused work or casual online meetings without distraction. The Wi-Fi is strong and reliable, making it popular with digital nomads. On the menu, you’ll find fresh breakfasts, tasty lunches, and light snacks. The coffee is top-notch too, with specialty brews and unique drinks that get rave reviews.
If you’re hunting for a coffee shop Ubud with view, The Sayan House delivers more than just caffeine, it’s all about the scenery. Perched on a cliff above the Ayung Valley, this spot is famous for its fine dining and dreamy atmosphere rather than being a work-friendly cafe.
While you’ll find Wi-Fi here, it’s not really built for long laptop sessions. Instead, think of it as a place to indulge in Asian–Latin fusion dishes, sip coffee, and soak up unforgettable views. Perfect for a romantic dinner or a special night out in Ubud.
Tucked away in the rice fields, Sari Organik is one of the best cafes in Ubud with a view for anyone who loves being surrounded by nature. The open-air setting gives you endless green paddy views and a serene vibe, though it’s more of a chill-out spot than a focused workspace.
Their Wi-Fi is decent but can be spotty, thanks to the location. The food is fresh and wholesome, with ingredients harvested straight from their own organic garden. Pair that with locally sourced coffee, and you’ve got a laid-back Ubud gem worth the walk (since it’s only accessible by foot or motorbike).
Looking for a cafe in Ubud with rice terrace view that’s calm and inspiring? Wyah is the spot. With its modern tropical design and open layout, you’ll be sipping coffee while gazing straight out at lush green fields. It’s a favorite for remote workers too, thanks to plenty of tables, power outlets, and Wi-Fi that’s fast and reliable, perfect for video calls or long laptop hours.
The menu covers everything from hearty breakfasts and brunch to healthy vegetarian and vegan options. Of course, the coffee is a highlight, with rave reviews for its rich flavor. If you’re curious, you can also try luwak coffee Ubud style here, along with a variety of other drinks. Nestled on Jalan Raya Sayan, Wyah offers a peaceful escape surrounded by nature, away from the busier parts of Ubud.
Coffee Shop in Ubud is Not Just Coffee
Finding the right coffee shop in Ubud isn’t just about caffeine. It’s about atmosphere, views, and that perfect balance of work and play. From hidden roasteries and artsy corners to eco-friendly cafés with rice terrace views, Ubud has endless options whether you’re a digital nomad, a traveler looking for inspiration, or simply a coffee lover chasing the best brews in Bali.
For a stay and enjoy Ubud with luxury, check out Ini Vie Hospitality accommodation, known as the best hospitality in Bali. It’s the perfect way to round off your Ubud adventure.

title: What Currency Is Used in Bali?
content:
If you are wondering what currency Bali uses, then this page is for you. All payments are made in local currency. Most shops, especially in traditional areas, won’t accept foreign cash or international debit cards. Make sure to exchange your money before you arrive or at the airport when you land.
Bali is one of the most popular travel destinations in the world. The island blends surf spots, sacred temples, rice terraces, yoga retreats, and vibrant beach clubs. It’s perfect for solo trips, group getaways, or a romantic honeymoon, offering the ideal mix of nature, culture, and modern comfort. So, what currency does Bali use? Your guide to money in Bali, Indonesia.
What Currency Is Used in Bali, Indonesia?
The currency in Bali is the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR or Rp), since Bali is part of Indonesia. All payments are made in rupiah. Banknotes range from Rp1,000 to Rp100,000. ATMs are easy to find in tourist areas, and most hotels, big restaurants, and modern shops accept credit cards. But for small warungs or traditional markets, cash is preferred.
Foreign currency isn’t usually accepted, and if it is, the exchange rate may not be fair. It’s safer and more practical to use rupiah. Money changers are everywhere, but stick to official places or banks to avoid scams. 1$ US in Bali usually equals around 16,274 Rupiah, so it’s worth converting your money to avoid overpaying.
Currency Denominations and Money-Saving Tips
The currency used in Bali is the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR or Rp). The coins you’ll find are Rp100, Rp200, Rp500, and Rp1,000. For paper money, the most common banknotes are Rp1,000 up to Rp100,000, which is the largest one. Rp100,000 is about USD 6 to 7, depending on the exchange rate.
If you’re coming from Australia, $100 AUD in Bali usually equals around Rp10,624, making it easy to enjoy food, shopping, and transport at a great value.
Cash in Bali is Essential
Even though Bali is getting more modern with digital payments and cards, cash is still important for daily use. Many local places don’t take cards or QRIS, especially small warungs, souvenir stalls, parking spots, and temple ticket counters. You’ll need cash when shopping at Sunday markets or exploring more traditional areas.
In some parts like Ubud, Sidemen, or remote beaches, weak phone signals can make card machines or QR codes unreliable. Even where cards are accepted, there’s often a minimum spend of Rp50,000 to Rp100,000. Some places also add a 2–3% fee for international cards. So it’s smart to carry some Bali currency with you at all times.
There are plenty of money changers in Bali, but not all of them are safe. To avoid scams, always go to official spots that are clear, secure, and trustworthy when exchanging currency in Bali.
1. BMC (Bali Money Changer)
You’ll find BMC in Seminyak, Legian, and nearby areas. They have a proper office setup with cashiers behind glass, not open counters. Just watch out for fake changers using the “BMC” name.
2. Central Kuta Money Exchange
Located in Kuta, Seminyak, Sanur, Nusa Dua, Legian, and Ubud, Central Kuta is one of the most reliable options. It’s registered with Bank Indonesia and offers good rates, no extra fees, and fast service.
3. Dirgahayu Valuta Prima
This one’s also officially registered and easy to find in big malls or popular tourist spots. Their service is secure, with printed receipts for every transaction.
If you’re wondering what currency they use in Bali, it’s the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), and these places make sure you get it safely and fairly.
Tips for Using Cash and Keeping Small Bills Handy in Bali
Even though places like Ubud, Seminyak, and Canggu are becoming more digital, cash is still key in many parts of Bali. Local food stalls like halal food restaurants, markets, parking areas, street vendors, and small spas or guesthouses usually only take cash. Here are some simple tips to manage money in Bali:
1. Keep Small Bills Handy
Rp2,000 to Rp20,000 is useful for snacks, water, parking, and tipping.
2. Ask for Small Bills When Exchanging
At official money changers, request a mix of denominations so you’re ready for smaller purchases.
3. Use a Separate Wallet
Keep your small change in a different pocket or pouch so it’s easy to grab and safe to carry.
4. Use Mobile Payment Apps
Apps like GoPay and OVO work well in cafes, restaurants, and stores. Top ups are easy via ATM or minimarket, and you might get cashback too.
5. Bring Extra Cash for Remote Trips
You’ll find ATMs in cities, but not always in rural or coastal areas. Carry extra cash just in case.
6. Always Check Your Change
At markets or when using larger bills, count your change to avoid mistakes.
Tips of Rp5,000 to Rp20,000 are appreciated by drivers, staff, and spa therapists.
The currency used in Bali is the Indonesian Rupiah. The best currency to take to Bali is USD, AUD, or EUR; they’re easy to exchange island wide and usually get good rates. However, keep in mind that the exchange rate to the rupiah may fluctuate over time, depending on Indonesia’s economic conditions.
Essential Money Tips for Travelers in Bali
Managing your money well while traveling can help you enjoy your time in Bali without stress. Here are some easy and practical tips:
1. Always carry enough cash
While Bali is becoming more digital, especially in areas like Seminyak and Ubud, many small shops, local warungs, markets, and tourist spots still prefer cash. It’s smart to bring small notes like Rp10,000 to Rp50,000. For reference, 1 NZD in Bali dollars is usually around Rp10,000.
2. Stick to trusted bank ATMs
Use machines from big banks like BCA, Mandiri, or BNI. Avoid isolated ATMs and always check for anything unusual on the card slot.
3. Exchange money at official spots
Use licensed and trusted places like Central Kuta, Dirgahayu, or BMC. Avoid shady money changers offering rates that sound too good. What currency does Bali use? The Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), and official money changers will give you fair rates.
4. Use e-wallets when possible
Apps like GoPay and OVO are widely accepted at restaurants, stores, and for rides. They’re fast and sometimes offer cashback too.
5. Split your cash for safety
Keep some money in your wallet, some in your bag, and the rest in your hotel safe. That way, you won’t lose everything if something goes wrong.
How to Avoid Scammers
1. Stay away from shady money changers
Skip the tiny booths or random stalls that offer exchange rates that seem too high. They’re often scams. Stick with certified money changers like Central Kuta, BMC, or Dirgantara. These places show clear rates and don’t sneak in extra fees. It’s the safest way to deal with money in Bali.
2. Watch out for ATM skimming
Use ATMs located inside banks or places with security cameras. Avoid those random ATMs on the street or in small shops. Always check the card slot and keypad to make sure nothing looks off.
3. Book stays through trusted sites
Go with well known platforms like Booking.com, Agoda, or Airbnb. Be careful with random Instagram or WhatsApp accounts offering deals that feel too cheap. If you book through social media, make sure the account looks legit and uses secure payment options.
4. Don’t scan random QR codes
Some QR codes in public places can lead to fake sites or steal your info. Only scan codes from reliable sources like official menus or apps like GoPay and OVO.
In short, what currency does Bali use? It’s the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), and it’s essential to carry it for daily expenses, especially when exploring traditional markets, local warungs, or remote beaches. Whether you’re paying for a quick meal, shopping at a Sunday market, or tipping a driver, having the right currency makes everything easier.
