title: What Is Holistic Wellness? Physical, Mental, and Spiritual Health
content:
Have you ever wondered what holistic wellness truly means? This is one of the most fulfilling activities in Ubud, the most popular wellness center in Bali. It goes beyond achieving physical balance; it represents a complete approach to well-being that embraces the body, mind, and spirit.
For those looking to begin or deepen their journey toward holistic well-being, Bali offers a natural sanctuary. From yoga retreat Bali experiences and Bali silent retreat programs to sacred sites like Pura Tirta Empul Bali, here’s everything you need to know about what is holistic wellness and how to live it fully through Bali’s holistic concept of health.
What is The Meaning of Holistic Wellness?
Based on Peggy Swabrick and Jay Yudof’s “Wellness in Eight Dimensions,” holistic wellness is the recognition that we are whole beings, encompassing balance, contentment, and meaningful relationships. It is about feeling good in the present while believing in our ability to thrive in the future, despite challenges
It recognizes how emotional and mental imbalances can manifest as physical symptoms, and thus promotes comprehensive care. In Bali, holistic wellness care is experienced through mindful practices like yoga, meditation, nature therapy, and healthy eating.
From spa treatments to immersive Bali silent retreat experiences, Bali brings the holistic concept of health to life through culture, nature, and spirituality. It’s a fulfilling journey related to holistic well-being, suitable for solo travelers, couples, and even families seeking meaningful things to do with kids in Bali
7 Components of Holistic Wellness
Swabrick and Yudof’s model embraces the eight key components of holistic wellness, including intellectual wellness. However, in Bali, the focus is primarily on the seven components that are deeply rooted in Balinese customs.
From physical health to financial peace of mind, nurturing each of these areas contributes to achieving a complete balance and overall holistic well-being. Let’s dive deeper into each element:
1. Physical Wellness
This includes maintaining a healthy body through movement, rest, nutrition, and routine care, including avoiding tobacco products, drinking caffeinated and sugary beverages. It is not about perfection but about listening to your body’s signals and acting with intention.
You can enjoy surfing in Canggu, join yoga classes in Seminyak, or try walking meditation in Ubud. To complement your activity, enjoy spa experiences like those at Svaha Spa Ubud or Svaha Spa Sanur for muscle relaxation and rejuvenation.
2. Emotional Wellness
Emotional wellness is the ability to understand, express, and manage emotions in a way that nurtures inner peace and supports healthy relationships. It’s a vital element within the holistic health definition.
At Svaha Spa Seminyak, many treatments are tailored to reduce stress and enhance emotional balance using massage, aromatherapy, and holistic touch. It’s one of the most enriching things to do in Seminyak if you need an emotional reset.
3. Environmental Wellness
Environmental wellness involves creating a harmonious connection with the natural world, promoting mental clarity, focus, and emotional resilience to manage stress and maintain balance. It’s about being present, navigating challenges with ease, and approaching life with a grounded and healthy mindset.
Environmental wellness is also achieved by doing simple things like regularly cleaning your living and work environment, disposing of garbage, removing spoiled food, and purchasing recycled items. You can also take short breaks to reconnect with nature to better understand its importance.
Many yoga retreat Bali programs emphasize enhancing environmental wellness by incorporating nature-based practices like breathing exercises, journaling, and sound therapy. This is one of the reasons why Bali is a top destination for those seeking a deeper, balanced wellness experience, including couples activities to strengthen their connection with both nature and each other.
4. Spiritual Wellness
Spiritual wellness isn’t always about religion; it’s about connecting with purpose and finding a sense of balance and peace. This core aspect of well-being can involve reconnecting with nature, personal values, or your true self.
One of the best ways to achieve spiritual wellness, which is not related to religion, is through regular personal reflection. It’s helpful to manifest the meaningfulness of life and your personal goals.
Spiritual wellness is an important part of Balinese beliefs. A visit to Pura Tirta Empul Bali offers a unique spiritual experience through sacred water purification, and it is open to everyone, including non-Hindus.
Social wellness refers to building strong, meaningful relationships and feeling connected to your community. It involves fostering bonds with friends, family, and the broader community, while also showing interest in and concern for the well-being of others.
In Bali, social wellness flourishes through shared experiences in lifestyle retreats, group yoga sessions, and healing circles. You can join community classes in Ubud, Seminyak, Sanur, or Canggu, and immerse yourself in the island’s warm and welcoming spirit.
6. Occupational Wellness
Occupational wellness is about finding purpose and fulfillment in your work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. It often aligns closely with both spiritual and emotional wellness, as well as with your sense of self-worth and personal values.
In Bali, the rise of balancing-focused coworking spaces makes it easier to blend productivity with personal growth. Recharge with spa sessions at Svaha Spa Canggu or take mindful breaks during your stay, aligning work with well-being.
7. Financial Wellness
Financial wellness means having confidence in managing your finances to support the life you envision. It helps reduce stress and supports long-term personal development, including building financial security and wealth.
One of the best aspects of wholeness is its accessibility. With budget-friendly yoga classes, plant-based cafés, and affordable spa treatments, Bali proves that achieving well-being doesn’t have to come at a high cost.
Self-Care vs Holistic Wellness: What’s the Difference?
While self-care often involves short-term fixes like spa days or relaxing activities, holistic wellness is a continuous, intentional lifestyle. It’s about long-term habits that foster growth, balance, and clarity in all life dimensions.
In Bali, from yoga retreat Bali programs to curated lifestyle retreats, the focus is on helping you build sustainable rituals. Holistic living encourages you to reflect on deeper questions, what truly feeds your soul, brings purpose to your life, and guides you to live with greater intention.
Final Thoughts on a Holistic Wellness
Holistic wellness is about creating harmony across your body, mind, and soul, not just surviving, but truly thriving. Bali, with its sacred temples like Pura Tirta Empul Bali, affordable spa offerings, and immersive lifestyle retreats, is the ideal destination to begin or continue your journey.
Ini Vie Hospitality is proud to be the best hospitality management in Bali, offering curated experiences designed to support your complete well-being. Check out our blog to find more recommended things to do in Bali.
Source: https://www.center4healthandsdc.org/uploads/7/1/1/4/71142589/wellness_in_8_dimensions_booklet_with_daily_plan.pdf

title: Best Honeymoon Destinations in the World: Bali and Beyond
content:
Do you ever wonder about the best honeymoon destinations around the world? It brings an unforgettable experience with your partner.
You can enjoy the tasty culinary delights, mesmerizing panoramic views, or even a meaningful cultural experience in your honeymoon destinations.
Here is a list of destinations to visit if you want to have a refined honeymoon experience.
Best Honeymoon Destinations in World
Bali has been known as one of the best honeymoon destinations in the world. You can stay in many tourist hotspots, like staying in Ubud’s resort. It offers you tranquil surroundings, which is perfect for an intimate night with your partner.
Planning to visit cultural places like Garuda Wisnu Kencana (GWK) in Uluwatu and Desa Penglipuran is also ideal for honeymoon destinations in 2026. It enhances your honeymoon because you can learn about Balinese culture alongside, with affordable prices and various options of private villas for couples. Bali has become the first destination for romance. It is where you can blend romance and intimacy in one moment.
Not much difference from the honeymoon in Bali, the Maldives has become one of the most romantic honeymoon destinations in Asia. It is an archipelagic nation in the Indian Ocean that offers an oceanfront spot.
Turquoise water views enhance a laid-back moment, which is ideal for honeymooners. You can swim back and forth in the ocean, or just stay in the daybeds to enjoy the beautiful ocean view in the Maldives.
If you’re looking for tropical honeymoon destinations to experience the difference of staying in a typical tourist area, the Maldives is ideal. It is a romantic place to unwind together with your partner while enjoying the tropical ambiance.
Thailand is frequently included in the honeymoon destinations in Asia. It is because Thailand has several extraordinary, stunning places to visit with a partner, such as Pattaya or Phuket.
Besides the tropical view, you can also experience the beauty of natural scenery in areas like Chiang Mai. It is one of the most romantic places for a honeymoon because the area has a romantic, slow atmosphere.
Just as Bali offers holiday packages, you should find a package for a honeymoon in Thailand. The packages will help you explore more places offering captivating backdrops, which will forever linger in your and your partner’s minds.
Japan offers you luxury honeymoon destinations. You can visit several temples to experience how locals live and their culture. You will also experience the sophisticated features of technology, where sakura blooms beautifully.
Visiting Dotonburi in Osaka to take a picture with the Glico Man backdrop is mandatory. It is a location where you may showcase Japan’s beauty to those seeking a sophisticated honeymoon experience.
This dramatically changes with each season, making every honeymoon feel different. In spring, you will see cherry blossoms, while in summer, there are many festivals and fireworks. Autumn is when you will see red and golden maple leaves, and winter with snow scenery.
Sri Lanka is one of the most unique honeymoon destinations. It is a country where you can experience more than a beach holiday with your partner. The country feels adventurous, romantic, and deeply memorable.
Sri Lanka’s honeymoon destinations are divided. You can travel to Bentota for opulent beachside resorts, Yala National Park for safaris and animals, or Nuwara Eliya for nature and cool temperatures.
You have to prepare a budget for the honeymoon destinations. Budgeting around $2.000–5.000 is enough to experience a luxurious, fancy holiday in Sri Lanka. It already includes a 4-star hotel and romantic dinners.
6. Santorini, Greece
Santorini is built on volcanic cliffs overlooking the sea. It creates breathtaking panoramic views almost everywhere you go. Many honeymoon hotels are carved into the cliffs.
Not much different from romantic villas in Bali, Santorini is a place where you can stay in extraordinary villas. Enjoying candlelight dinners with oceanfront views transforms your honeymoon.
Oia has become one of the most famous sunset views in Santorini. You can take your partner here to see the iconic sunsets while staying in luxury hotels with a romantic atmosphere.
Paris is already known as one of the best honeymoon destinations around the world. Imagine having dinner with the Eiffel Tower as the backdrop. It elevates your dining experience into something more refined.
In addition, experiencing dinner cruises along the Seine River will give you unforgettable memories after the honeymoon ends. It is where you can get closer to your partner, talking intimately while the cruise sails along the river.
It makes Paris a luxurious destination for couples who are just getting married. The intimacy, romance, and all blends that create a beautiful ambiance during the honeymoon session.
8. Amalfi Coast, Italy
Imagine spending time in the dramatic cliffs, colourful seaside villages, Mediterranean views, and romantic Italian atmosphere. All of these can be found in Italy’s Amalfi Coast.
Slow mornings with views of the sea are a feature of the Amalfi Coast. It is what elevates the honeymoon experience and makes the coastline ideal for sunset dinners with pasta and wine.
The atmosphere feels luxurious yet relaxed. It is ideal for newlyweds who want both romance and beautiful scenery. The memory will forever linger after having a fantastic sunset and dinner time in the Amalfi Coast.
9. Dubrovnik, Croatia
Dubrovnik is in Croatia and has been popular among honeymooners as one of the most beautiful coastal destinations. It offers a mix of medieval charm, Adriatic sea views, with peaceful, romantic atmosphere.
Called the “Pearl of the Adriatic”, Dubrovnik feels elegant and cinematic. A combination of culture, relaxation, history, and coastal beauty without overwhelming crowds makes it ideal for newlyweds.
The city becomes romantic during sunset. The golden light reflects off the stone buildings and the Adriatic Sea. The golden light reflecting off the stone buildings and Adriatic Sea creates a scene that leaves visitors truly mesmerized.
Bora-bora is considered one of the world’s ultimate honeymoon destinations. Thanks to its crystal-clear turquoise lagoons, overwater villas, and private island resorts, equipped with a peaceful tropical atmosphere.
This honeymoon destination feels more like a secluded paradise designed specifically for romance. For many couples, it represents the dream tropical honeymoon experience that is unforgettable.
You can wake up directly above the lagoon, then swim from their private deck. Even experiencing a floating breakfast is possible here. It is ideal for you and your partner to spend time together without getting disturbed by the outside world.
With untouched beaches, giant granite rock formations, and turquoise waters, Seychelles is one of the most romantic places for a honeymoon. It feels more exclusive because it is less crowded than most honeymoon destinations.
Seychelles is a nature-focused honeymoon destination compared to the busier tropical destinations. If you want something private, you can go to the destination to have the best night with your partner.
Experiencing white sand beaches and crystal-clear ocean waters allows you to enjoy the whole honeymoon session. The experience creates a calm and intimate memory for the newlyweds.
Sitting in the Caribbean, Saint Lucia has become one of the most beautiful honeymoon destinations. It is known for its dramatic volcanic mountains, luxury cliffside resorts, and romantic atmosphere.
A combination of beaches with lush mountains is perfect for couples. You can experience both relaxation and unforgettable memories during the honeymoon. So, visiting Saint Lucia will leave you with a great impression once the honeymoon is over.
Why Bali Consistently Tops Global Honeymoon Destination Lists
As one of the honeymoon destinations in Indonesia, Bali has consistently remained popular among couples seeking intimacy after getting married. The combination of romance, luxury, culture, wellness, nature, and affordability is all things you can experience.
Offering multiple honeymoon styles: Staying in Bali’s honeymoon resort or having jungle wellness retreats are available. You can also experience adventures, nature, and cultural exploration.
Private pool transforms honeymoon experience: Bali is a popular destination for honeymooners since it offers private infinity pools. Additionally, you may experience floating breakfast and flower baths.
Romantic experience beyond the hotel: Besides the beautiful resort, you can enjoy sunset dinners by the ocean. Or, experiencing a couple of spa treatments with traditional Balinese healing rituals.
Bali honeymoon destinations, like Ubud, Canggu, Seminyak, and Uluwatu, bring a different experience. From lush jungle to vibrant, high-energy, and serene location, you can have it all on one island.
Planning a visit to the best honeymoon destinations will elevate your honeymoon experience. Wherever you go, the best honeymoon is the one that feels made for both of you and your partner.
If you are choosing Bali as a destination, Ini Vie Hospitality is ready for your perfect escape. We offer stunning, personalized accommodations to make your honeymoon feel more refined and unforgettable. Let’s book and don’t miss out on the chance of having an unforgettable honeymoon in Bali.

title: The Most Romantic Honeymoon Resort in Ubud
content:
Bali has become one of the most popular destinations for honeymooners around the world, making it a consistent inclusion in the list of best honeymoon destinations by various international travel publications. The tranquil natural beauty of Bali forest-town, with its lush green rice fields, tropical forests, and an array of enchanting honeymoon resorts in Ubud, provides the perfect setting for an intimate honeymoon experience with your partner.
This article will guide you through the best honeymoon resorts in Ubud, offering luxury, privacy, and unforgettable honeymoon packages. Here are the top choices for a couple staying in Ubud, each one promising a unique and romantic escape.
1. Kaamala Resort and Spa – Romantic honeymoon resort in Ubud
Kaamala Resort and Spa is a luxury honeymoon resort in Ubud, renowned for its breathtaking views of the green valley. This tranquil getaway is a popular choice for couples seeking tranquility and privacy, featuring luxurious villas equipped with high-end amenities.
Kaamala often offers an all-inclusive Ubud honeymoon package, which includes romantic dinners and special spa treatments. Guests can explore the resort’s three outstanding dining options: Habitat Bistro, specializing in Italian cuisine; Shichirin Ubud, offering elegant teppanyaki, sushi, and gyukatsu; and Seven Paintings Ubud, an immersive fine dining experience.
For spa and wellness, guests can experience traditional Balinese massages and floating sound healing at Svaha Spa Bisma. This couple’s sanctuary also features a yoga chapel, perfect for those seeking serenity and balance, overlooking lush greenery.
2. Aksari Resort – Romantic places to stay in Ubud
Aksari Resort is the perfect choice for couples looking for a honeymoon resort in Ubud with an all-inclusive experience and a strong Balinese traditional feel. It offers a range of rooms with forest views, ideal for couples who want to connect with nature.
Aksari blends modern design with natural elements, offering beautiful villas and high-class amenities, including private pools, scenic bathtubs, and spacious rooms. It also features delightful dining options, including Ankhusa Restaurant, which offers a royal Balinese dining experience with the “Megibung Feast,” known for its bold, flavorful dishes made from locally sourced ingredients.
For authentic Japanese cuisine, guests can visit Kojin Japanese Restaurant, offering irori-style cooking and a genuine taste of every ingredient. To rejuvenate and reconnect with your inner balance, relax in the enchanting Balinese massage at Svaha Spa Kenderan and enjoy morning yoga in its bamboo venue, overlooking the tropical forest.
3. Asvara Resort – Honeymoon resort in Ubud surrounded by nature
Asvara is an excellent choice for couples seeking a honeymoon resort in Ubud with a scenic private pool and jacuzzi, offering the privacy and intimate moments that are perfect for a romantic retreat. Each villa room also features a sunbed, where you can lounge by the pool and enjoy breathtaking views.

title: How Much Does it Cost to Go to Bali in 2026: Hot Updated Guide
content:
If you are planning a trip to Bali in 2026, and wondering how much does it cost to go to Bali, the good news is Bali is one of the most flexible destinations for any budget. You can plan a simple backpacking trip or enjoy a luxurious, exclusive getaway, all tailored to your budget.
This guide breaks down the costs for everything from mid-range to high-end travel, giving you a clear and updated look at what to expect for a trip to Bali. Here’s a practical overview to help you plan your adventure, no matter your budget.
Average Price of Trip to Bali
Here’s a simple guide to getting around Bali, with different options for every style and bali trip budget.
1. Hotel Shuttle Service
Many hotels and villas offer shuttle services, which can help manage your bali vacation cost. Always check if your accommodation provides this, whether it’s free or paid. For example, properties under Ini Vie Hospitality often include free shuttles.
If there’s a fee, expect IDR 200,000–450,000 depending on distance. If not available, hotels usually recommend trusted private drivers, which can be safer and more convenient, especially when planning a special honeymoon in Bali.
2. Private Car with Driver
This is the most comfortable way to explore. Ideal for families or groups, it takes the stress out of navigating and can include local insights from the driver.
Prices range from IDR 500,000 to 850,000+ per day, usually covering the driver and fuel. This is a great option when planning things to do in Bali with kids, as it offers flexibility and comfort throughout the day.
3. Renting a Scooter
Renting a motorbike is popular in busy areas like Seminyak and Canggu, and it’s very affordable at IDR 70,000–150,000 per day. It’s perfect for couples or solo travelers who are confident riders.
Always wear a helmet, carry a valid license, and be cautious in traffic. This option can help lower your overall trip to bali cost if you’re comfortable on two wheels.
These ride-hailing apps are convenient for short trips, with fixed prices shown in the app, no haggling needed.
They work well in many areas, though some tourist zones restrict pick-ups. Using Grab or Gojek is a budget-friendly way to get around and fits easily into any bali trip budget.
5. Kura-Kura Bus (Tourist Shuttle)
For one of the cheapest transport options, try the Kura-Kura Bus. It connects major tourist areas like Kuta, Seminyak, Ubud, and Nusa Dua, with fares from IDR 20,000–80,000.
The buses are comfortable with AC and Wi-Fi, but they run on a schedule and stop service around 8 p.m. It’s a good choice for backpackers or travelers looking to save on their bali vacation cost.
Where to Stay: Accommodation Prices
Bali is famous for its wide range of affordable and flexible accommodation options, making it easy to travel the island on almost any budget. From simple backpacker stays to dreamy villas for a romantic honeymoon, Bali truly has something for everyone.
The prices generally range from around IDR 400,000 to IDR 7,000,000 per night and beyond, depending on the experience you’re looking for.
Mid-Range Stays (Popular for Couples & Small Families)
This category balances comfort and cost, with prices from IDR 400,000 to 1,800,000 per night. You’ll typically get a 3- or 4-star hotel, a boutique hotel, or a small villa (often without a private pool).
Amenities usually include a private bathroom with hot water, air conditioning, breakfast, access to a shared pool, and daily cleaning.
If you’re wondering is Bali expensive, this range shows you can enjoy comfort without overspending. It’s also a practical choice if you’re visiting Bali in December, as you get good value during the busier season.
A peaceful villa near the beach in Canggu, set among serene rice fields. It features a modern tropical design with warm wood accents, private pools, and bathtubs near the bed.
They can arrange beautiful flower displays in the pool or on the bed for special occasions. It’s private and quiet but still just 5–10 minutes from the beach and the best things to do in Canggu.
This villa has a chic, minimalist design with modern touches like smart TVs and lighting systems. Some rooms have hammocks or nets over the pool, and there’s a stylish communal area.
Located close to Canggu’s popular cafes and restaurants, it offers both convenience and privacy, a great way to balance your bali cost while staying in a trendy area.
Nestled in the heart of Seminyak, this villa combines elegant design with total comfort. The interiors feel luxurious, with dramatic lighting and some units including kitchenettes. Their floating breakfast is a local favorite.
The location is perfect, you’re minutes from dining, shopping, and nightlife, yet the villa itself is a tranquil retreat. Ideal if you want to explore easily while keeping your bali trip budget in check.
Here’s a look at Bali’s luxury stays—perfect for honeymooners or anyone wanting extra comfort and beautiful surroundings. Prices in this category range from IDR 2,000,000 to 7,000,000 per night and include 5-star resorts or private pool villas with amenities like butler service, beautiful views, on-site spas, and world-class facilities.
When spending your currency in Bali, remember that these luxury stays are an investment in comfort and experience.”
1. Kaamala Resort Ubud
This iconic luxury resort blends modern comfort with stunning jungle views, located close to the Monkey Forest yet perfectly peaceful. It features an infinity pool overlooking the valley, a high-end restaurant, and an exclusive spa.
Rooms include Smart Room technology, making it ideal for honeymooners who want privacy with easy access to central Ubud. They also offer activities for guests who want to experience the diversity of Bali.
You can even bring home Balinese handicrafts as souvenirs from participating in activities at the resort.
Part of Ini Vie Hospitality’s newest portfolio, Maar Resort is a wellness-focused retreat with majestic architecture that blends into the natural surroundings. Villas offer open-air living areas and spacious private pools with lush rice paddy views.
They also offer various holiday packages to make your stay even more affordable, with various inclusions. It’s perfect for those seeking absolute tranquility and a luxurious escape into nature.
3. Sini Vie Resort Seminyak
This resort combines modern luxury with eco-friendly service, featuring rooms equipped with Alexa voice control for convenience. On-site, you’ll find Shichirin Seminyak, an authentic Japanese teppanyaki restaurant, a relaxing pool bar, and Svaha Spa Seminyak for rejuvenation. It’s designed for comfort, privacy, and a seamless, tech-enhanced stay.
4. Astera Resort Canggu
Located in trendy Canggu, Astera Resort offers luxury amidst green rice paddies that are becoming rare in the area. The resort includes two restaurants, Svaha Spa, and a beautiful pool with paddy views.
All villas feature Alexa voice control, and the location offers quiet relaxation while still being close to cafes, beaches, and even a nearby pilates studio in Canggu for those wanting to stay active. It’s ideal for travelers who want a peaceful retreat without missing out on Canggu’s vibrant scene.
Here’s a look at Bali’s ultra-luxury stays, designed for those seeking total privacy and exceptional comfort. These are renowned international resorts or exclusive multi-bedroom villas, often found in exclusive areas of Uluwatu or the lush jungles of Ubud. Amenities can include private chefs, private beach access, and stunning architectural designs.
If you’re wondering how expensive is Bali, this category represents the high end, where every detail is curated for an unparalleled experience.
1. Equipoise Luxury Resort
Equipoise offers a perfect balance of modern luxury and natural serenity in Ubud. Designed around the theme of “balance,” the resort blends seamlessly into the lush paddies and jungle valley.
Each villa features a private pool that appears to merge with the treetops, offering exceptional privacy. With 24/7 personalized service and a world-class spa focused on holistic wellness, it’s ideal for travelers seeking absolute tranquility and a deep connection with nature in a luxurious setting.
2. Seascape Resort Uluwatu
Perched on the cliffs of Uluwatu, Seascape Resort delivers breathtaking views of the Indian Ocean from every angle. The resort features contemporary design and premium materials, with accommodations like the Two-Bedroom Ocean View Villa with Private Pool.
Guests can enjoy authentic Japanese cuisine at Tsune Uluwatu, relax at Svaha Spa Bingin, stay active at the fitness center, or unwind by the stunning infinity pool overlooking the horizon. Staying here also places you close to unforgettable things to do in Uluwatu.
Eating in Bali: Culinary Highlights & Costs
Here’s a simple guide to eating in Bali, with options for every taste and budget. Not only just to know but also helping you understand how much does it cost to go to Bali when it comes to food.
When planning your 7-day trip to Bali cost, you can mix and match these options. Enjoying street food and warung meals most days, with perhaps one special fine dining experience, allows you to savor Bali’s food scene without overspending.
Street food is the tastiest and most affordable way to try authentic Balinese flavors. You’ll find it at morning markets and night markets (Pasar Senggol). Look for stalls popular with locals and try treats like Klepon (sweet rice balls), Laklak (mini pancakes), pork satay, or grilled corn on the beach. Estimated cost: IDR 5,000 – 25,000 per item.
2. Warung (Local Eateries)
Warungs are casual local restaurants that are the heart of Balinese everyday dining. You can choose from set menus or Nasi Campur (rice with a mix of sides). Must-tries include Nasi Campur Bali, Babi Guling (roast pork), or Ayam Betutu (spiced chicken). For halal options, look for signs like “Warung Muslim.” Estimated cost: IDR 25,000 – 60,000 per person, including a drink.
Bali is home to world-class restaurants, often with stunning views. These spots offer everything from tasting menus and modern Indonesian fusion to premium seafood. Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends. Estimated cost: IDR 800,000 – 3,000,000+ per person, depending on the menu and drinks.
Bali offers the perfect balance of relaxation and energy, making it easy to design a trip that fits your mood. Many travelers split their time between the peaceful vibe of Ubud and the lively coastal areas like Canggu or Seminyak.
From Unwind to Vibrant
Find Peace & Rejuvenation
If you’re looking to unwind, Bali is a wellness paradise. Start your day with a yoga class overlooking green rice fields, treat yourself to a flower bath at a tranquil spa, or simply enjoy a quiet sunrise on Sanur Beach.
For the best serene experience, head to Ubud, Sidemen, or Munduk, these cooler, rural spots are perfect for recharging. Estimated cost: Yoga classes from IDR 120,000; spa treatments from IDR 250,000 to IDR 1,500,000+.
Embrace Vibrant Energy
If you’re in the mood for fun and social energy, southern Bali is the place to be. Spend the day at a stunning beach club, catch waves in Canggu, enjoy live music in Seminyak, or experience the powerful Kecak Dance in Uluwatu.
These areas are filled with stylish cafes, boutiques, and nightlife that lasts well into the night. Estimated cost: Kecak Dance tickets around IDR 150,000; beach clubs often have free entry but a minimum spend for daybeds (usually IDR 500,000 and up).
Complete Your Bali Journey with Exceptional Stays by Ini Vie Hospitality
Ultimately, how much does it cost to go to Bali depends on what kind of holiday you want. Because this island gives a flexible range for any budget. With thoughtful planning for transport, dining, and accommodation, you can create a memorable experience that aligns with your financial comfort.
To complete your Bali journey with exceptional comfort and style, consider staying with Ini Vie Hospitality. They offer the finest accommodations on the island for couples, families, and groups, ensuring every moment of your stay is as special as the destination itself.

title: 6 Best Ice Cream dan Gelato Spots in Canggu, Bali
content:
Canggu’s warm tropical weather, especially during the dry season, makes gelato and ice cream in Canggu a popular choice for both travelers and locals looking to cool down during the day. From refreshing fruit sorbets to creamy artisan creations, enjoying ice cream has become part of the area’s laid-back café and beach lifestyle.
Over the years, Canggu has also developed into one of Bali’s best destinations for artisan gelato, with many shops combining traditional techniques and high-quality local ingredients to create unique flavors. In this guide, we’ll explore 6 of the best ice cream & gelato spots in Canggu, Bali.
Top Ice Cream & Gelato Spots in Canggu
Known for its authentic Italian approach, Ettore Gelato Canggu has become one of the most recommended places to enjoy artisan gelato in the area. Created by Italian chef Ettore Chiodini, the gelato here is made without pre-mixed ingredients, resulting in richer textures and more natural flavors, with the Pistachio variant standing out as one of the customer favorites.
One of the unique menu highlights is the Gelato Brioche, where cold gelato is served inside a warm brioche bun for a combination of soft, creamy, and buttery textures. Located on Jalan Pantai Pererenan No. 88, this spot is a great stop after exploring nearby shopping areas.
Prices start from around IDR 35,000 for a small cup and approximately IDR 65,000 for a larger serving with three flavors.
Located close to Echo Beach, Gaya Gelato Canggu is a popular choice for visitors looking for refreshing gelato after a beach day. The shop focuses on using natural ingredients without artificial coloring or preservatives, with tropical fruit sorbets and coconut-based flavors becoming some of the most popular menu options.
The atmosphere is simple and relaxed, making it ideal for a quick takeaway dessert or a casual stop before sunset near the coastline. As one of the spots often included in recommendations for the best gelato in Bali, Gaya Gelato is especially convenient after exploring the beaches around.
Located near Batu Bolong Beach, Nalu Canggu gelato is a popular stop for visitors looking to enjoy a cold dessert after surfing, sunset watching, or exploring the nearby cafés and shops. The shop is known for its smooth gelato texture and refreshing flavors, ranging from rich Dark Chocolate to lighter fruit-based options that are especially enjoyable during Canggu’s warm afternoons.
Besides gelato, Nalu also serves soft cookies with crispy edges and generous fillings, making it a favorite snack spot for both adults and families. With its simple open-air design and convenient location on Jalan Pantai Batu Bolong, it has become one of the most popular dessert spots in Canggu and a casual option for travelers looking for relaxing things to do with kids around the beach area.
4. Mishki Protein Gelato
For visitors searching for a lighter dessert option, Mishki Protein Gelato offers a different take on ice cream in Bali, with high-protein and lower-sugar gelato selections. Flavors such as Peanut Butter and Double Chocolate are especially popular for their creamy texture and rich taste while still appealing to health-conscious travelers.
The shop features a clean and modern interior that reflects the wellness-focused atmosphere around Batu Bolong and nearby fitness cafés. Located on Jalan Pantai Batu Bolong No. 45B, Mishki is a great alternative for those wanting a more balanced dessert experience while exploring the café and lifestyle scene that has made Canggu one of Bali’s most visited destinations.
5. Gelato Secrets – Canggu
Gelato Secrets is known as one of the early artisan gelato brands in Bali, combining traditional Italian techniques with locally sourced ingredients to create unique flavors. Favorites such as Chocolate Valrhona and seasonal fruit sorbets made from passion fruit or soursop have made this shop one of the most recommended Canggu dessert spots for visitors exploring the Batu Bolong area.
The café features a cozy and modern atmosphere that makes it a popular meeting point throughout the day. Located on Jalan Pantai Batu Bolong No. 56, it is also a convenient stop for travelers moving from Seminyak to Canggu while searching for relaxing places to enjoy dessert after visiting cafés, surf spots, or a nearby shopping spot.
6. PARA Treats Canggu
PARA Treats recently expanded to Canggu with its second Bali branch, offering a refreshing selection of premium frozen yogurt and smoothies that are perfect for Bali’s warm weather. Popular menu choices include the strawberry cheesecake froyo and the Canggu-exclusive Pistachio PARÁ, known for its creamy texture and rich nutty flavor.
Designed with a warm terracotta-inspired outdoor space and a minimalist modern interior, the venue creates a comfortable atmosphere for relaxing after spending time at a nearby beach club. Located on Jalan Nelayan No. 4, PARA Treats has quickly become one of the newer favorites for visitors searching for where to eat in Canggu.
Vegan & Dairy-Free Options
For visitors looking for lighter dessert options, vegan ice cream Canggu has become increasingly popular thanks to the area’s strong wellness and café culture. Many gelato shops now offer fruit-based sorbets and plant-based alternatives that still deliver rich flavors and creamy textures without using dairy products.
Gelato Secrets – Sorbetto
Gelato Secrets offers a refreshing selection of dairy-free sorbettos that focus on natural fruit flavors and a cleaner finish. Popular options include the tangy Passion Fruit and locally inspired Mango sorbet, both known for their smooth texture despite being completely dairy-free.
Gaya Gelato – Oat Milk Options
Gaya Gelato also provides plant-based alternatives through its oat milk gelato collection, created for visitors looking for a lighter but still satisfying dessert. Flavors such as Oat Milk Chocolate and nut-based varieties remain popular for their creamy consistency and rich taste while staying completely dairy-free.
What time do most gelato shops open in Canggu?
Most places serving ice cream Canggu are usually open from around 10:00 or 11:00 AM until late evening, making them easy to visit after the beach, dinner, or sunset sessions. Some popular spots even stay open until midnight or later, giving visitors plenty of options for late-night desserts around Canggu.
Can I order gelato through GrabFood or GoFood?
Yes, many of the well-known gelato and dessert shops in Canggu are available through GrabFood and GoFood for delivery. To keep the gelato in good condition during Bali’s warm weather, it’s usually recommended to choose faster delivery options and check whether the shop provides insulated or thermal packaging.
Is Ettore Gelato worth the queue?
Ettore is often considered one of the most popular artisan gelato spots in the area, so waiting lines are quite common, especially in the evening. Many visitors feel the quality, texture, and authentic Italian-style flavors make it worth visiting, particularly for signature options like Pistachio and Gelato Brioche.
Final Thought on Ice Cream and Gelato in Canggu
Ice cream in Canggu has become more than just a refreshing dessert option, but also part of the area’s café, beach, and lifestyle culture. From authentic Italian-style gelato and protein-based desserts to vegan sorbets and frozen yogurt, Canggu offers a wide variety of spots that suit different tastes and travel styles throughout the day.
Whether you are stopping by after surfing, sunset watching, café hopping, or exploring the beachside areas, there are plenty of dessert spots worth trying around Canggu. If you want to discover more cafés, restaurants, and local food recommendations around the island, you can also explore the complete Bali food and travel guide at Ini Vie Hospitality.

title: Let’s Try Indonesian Food in Canggu: 20 Recommended Spots
content:
Indonesian food is nominated as one of the 10 World’s Best Cuisines by TasteAtlas, known for diverse traditional dishes with bold aromatic spices and complex flavors. When you travel to Bali, trying Indonesian food in Canggu should be on your bucket list.
Some must-try Indonesian foods include Nasi Goreng, Mie Goreng, Rendang, and Nasi Campur. Gladly, there are endless options of places to eat in Canggu that offer Indonesian food. Here are 20 recommended spots for Indonesian food in Canggu that you must try during your holiday in Bali.
Recommendation Indonesian Restaurant in Canggu
Traditionally, Indonesian foods are sold in warungs, small food stalls usually run by a family. But modernity has elevated this concept, and many warungs have transformed into small to mid-scale restaurants. Here are the recommended restaurants in Canggu.
This spot is a strong contender for the best warung Canggu because of its clean and modern vibe. They serve a Nasi Campur-style menu where you pick what you want from a glass display.
Warung Local is located in the hustle and bustle of Jalan Pantai Batu Bolong, surrounded by villas and sports centers. It is perfect for a quick and healthy lunch after visiting the gyms in Canggu.
Still in the Batu Bolong area, Warung Bu Mi is legendary among travelers and locals for offering the best Indonesian food in Canggu at very affordable prices. You can choose from red, yellow, or brown rice, along with dozens of side dishes like ayam goreng, rendang, satay, and tempe.
The ambiance is simple and rustic, focusing entirely on the delicious variety of food. Beyond the food, it also offers Jamu, a special Indonesian turmeric tonic that is good for your health.
Located near Batu Bolong Beach, Varuna is one of the best warungs in Canggu for surfers and beach lovers. The menu features classic Indonesian dishes such as Nasi Kuning (turmeric rice), tempe, satay, ayam goreng (Indonesian fried chicken), and fresh juices in a relaxed, open-air setting.
The restaurant has a two-floor dining area, where the second floor is perfect for enjoying a meal while overlooking the neighborhood. It is a great pitstop before heading to the beach in the Canggu area.
4. Waroeng Bernadette
If you want a unique artistic atmosphere, this is the best warung in Canggu for you. From the outside, it looks like an industrial-style restaurant, but as you step in, colonial-style art and vintage decorations greet you.
Their signature dish is Rendang, which is rich in spices and melts in your mouth. They also serve some popular Indonesian snacks and desserts like lumpia goreng (fried dimsum), perkedel jagung (corn fritter), and tape cake.
Located near Canggu’s shopping spots and beaches, Warung Sika has gained popularity due to its wide variety of Indonesian foods. It features unique traditional Bali architecture with intricate designs and decorations, making you feel like you are visiting a local friend’s home.
It serves many food selections with home-cooked styles, like a traditional warung with a buffet style. But if you prefer a package or à la carte, simply tell the staff. Some notable menu items here include noodle soup, chicken soup, and satay.
This small and cozy spot feels like eating in a local home. They serve some of the best Indonesian food in Canggu with a focus on home-cooked flavors, and their friendly staff makes you feel right at home.
Some of their popular menus include Nasi Goreng and Chicken Satay. If you feel that bold spices are not suitable for your palate, you can also order their international menu items such as Cordon Bleu or Tenderloin Steak.
7. Iwa Restaurant at Hotel Tugu Bali
If you are looking for an upscale Indonesian restaurant in Canggu that is perfect for a candlelight dinner or special occasion, Iwa is a must-visit. Located in a 5-star hotel, it serves many exquisite foods with generous portions.
One of their popular menu packages is Pasar Sate Nusantara, which serves 6 popular types of satay in Indonesia. If you want a more diverse menu including seafood, meats, and vegetables, you can try The Congklak Sets, a 5-course meal from appetizer to dessert.
Warung Nads offers a cleaner and more modern take on the traditional warung. It is one of the best warungs in Canggu if you have a sensitive stomach but still want local spices.
The food presentation is neat, and the flavors are always consistent. Some favorite menu items here include Ikan Bakar Rica, Nasi Campur Mewah, and Nasi Bakar Rendang. The ricefield view and cool air make it perfect for lunch or early dinner.
This place is unique because it employs deaf staff members to create an inclusive environment, as the name suggests. Aside from the inspiring mission, they serve the best Indonesian food in Canggu with a modern twist.
The industrial design, combined with tropical decoration, makes it very stylish and comfortable. Most customers who visit praise their Nasi Campur and Balinese Sate Babi. For a more universal menu, you can try the Smoked Brisket or burgers.
Famous for its Crispy Duck, Warung Eropa is a must-visit for dinner, especially for those who want to try bold spices. While it is slightly pricier, it is the best warung in Canggu for a special meal with meat, but the vibes make it all worth it.
The ambiance is slightly more upscale compared to a typical roadside stall. It has a combination of Balinese intricate design with European style, making it perfect for a casual lunch or romantic dining.
Recommended Indonesian Warungs in Canggu
We also gather some authentic Indonesian Warungs in Canggu with local vibes and taste. Check these best warungs in Canggu for authenticity, and they are deeply rooted in local heritage.
11. Tulis Tiwa Canggu
Hidden away in a quiet alley, Tulis Tiwa is the definition of a “hidden gem” that locals whisper about. It offers a truly authentic home-cooked experience that feels like dining in a Balinese family’s kitchen.
Their menu focuses on rich, comforting flavors, with the Nasi Campur being a standout favorite for its generous portions and perfectly spiced side dishes. The vibe is simple, unpretentious, and intimate, making it a perfect spot if you are staying at a nearby hostel in Canggu.
Living up to its name, which translates to “Story of Spices,” this restaurant takes you on a flavorful journey across the archipelago. The Beef Rendang here is legendary, slow-cooked to perfection until tender, and their Sate Ayam offers a smoky sweetness that pairs perfectly with warm rice.
The setting is arguably one of the best for a warung Canggu, featuring a stunning 360-degree view of lush rice paddies. The open-air bamboo structure allows for a breezy dining experience, making it an ideal spot for a sunset dinner where you can enjoy affordable luxury amidst nature.
13. Ketela Eatery & Lifestyle
Ketela offers a unique “guilt-free” dining experience located within the sustainable Theanna Villa complex. While they are famous for their vegan-friendly options, their Indonesian meat dishes like the Oxtail Soup (Sop Buntut) and Grilled Pork Ribs are surprisingly decadent.
The kitchen focuses on using fresh, locally sourced ingredients to create healthy yet satisfying meals. The design is a masterpiece of bamboo architecture, creating a zen-like atmosphere that is a must-visit after a session at the pilates studios in Canggu.
Ulekan elevates the traditional warung Canggu experience into something chic and sophisticated. Named after the traditional stone mortar and pestle, the kitchen prides itself on making spice pastes from scratch daily. You absolutely must try their Crispy Duck and the slow-cooked Beef Rendang, which are presented with a level of finesse rarely seen in casual dining spots.
The interior is beautifully designed with a mix of colonial charm and modern tropical aesthetics, featuring warm lighting and tasteful art. It is a fantastic choice for a celebratory dinner where you want the flavors of a warung but the comfort of a high-end restaurant.
Rasa Kitchen is the go-to spot for reliable, delicious Indonesian comfort food that hits the spot every time. It is particularly loved for its “wok-hei” style dishes, such as the smoky Nasi Goreng and savory Black Pepper Beef. The menu is extensive and approachable, making it a safe bet for those new to Indonesian cuisine.
The ambiance is casual and laid-back, typical of a modern eatery that focuses more on flavor than frills. It’s a bustling spot often filled with expats and locals alike, perfect for a quick, satisfying lunch or a no-fuss dinner after a long day at the beach.
For travelers seeking an authentic roadside experience without sacrificing hygiene, Warung YASA is a top contender. The “Nasi Goreng Kampung” (Village Fried Rice) and fresh Gado-Gado are crowd pleasers, offering a true taste of local daily life with wallet-friendly prices.
The open-air setting allows you to watch the world go by, capturing the energetic bustle of Canggu. It has a rustic, traditional charm with simple wooden furniture and a friendly, communal vibe. It is the best place to go when you want to eat like a local and enjoy a cold drink in a relaxed environment.
Located near popular Canggu shopping spots like Love Anchor Canggu, Anita’s offers an interesting “Indo-Italian” fusion concept, but their Indonesian section is surprisingly robust and authentic. While you might be tempted by pasta, their Nasi Goreng and Cap Cay (stir-fried vegetables) are cooked with a homey touch that rivals dedicated warungs.
The venue often features a garden-like atmosphere that feels airy and open. It strikes a balance between a European cafe and a tropical warung, making it suitable for a leisurely brunch or a slow dinner where you can linger over drinks and conversation.
Often praised as one of the friendliest spots in town, The Luhron (sometimes spelled Luhroh) is a family-run best warung for Indonesian food in Canggu that exudes warmth. Mama Luh, the owner, ensures every dish tastes as if it came from a grandmother’s kitchen, with simple decor and traditional touches making it feel cozy.
The Sate Ayam and Pepes Tuna (spiced tuna wrapped in banana leaf) are standout dishes that offer deep, complex flavors. Located on the second floor, the restaurant offers a breezy vantage point above the street.
Pali is a destination for those who appreciate culture as much as cuisine. Housed in a traditional Javanese Joglo, the restaurant serves authentic dishes from across the archipelago, including rare finds like Sumatran cassava leaves in coconut milk.
Their Gado-Gado is prepared the traditional way and is widely considered one of the freshest in Canggu. The atmosphere is incredibly romantic and serene, especially in the evening when the Joglo is dimly lit and overlooks the rice fields. After a day of pampering at the best massages in Canggu, this is the perfect place to unwind.
Stepping into Casa Tua feels like visiting a quirky, charming colonial home. The menu features elevated Indonesian classics, with the “Timbungan” (dishes slow-cooked inside bamboo) being a rare and delicious specialty you must try. They also serve a fantastic Nasi Goreng that balances sweet soy and savory spices perfectly.
The venue is famous for its whimsical garden where friendly rabbits hop around freely, delighting both kids and adults. The vintage decor, combined with the lush tropical garden, creates a magical, fairy-tale ambiance that is unique in Canggu.
Taste the Real Indonesia in Canggu
Exploring the culinary scene is one of the main reasons why Canggu is so popular. Whether you choose a simple street-side stall or a modern venue, the flavors of Indonesia will amaze you.
We hope this list helps you find your favorite meal in Bali. If you are looking for more dining options or western food, check out our guide to restaurants in Canggu or relax at a cafe in Canggu nearby. Get ready for your next holiday in Bali!

title: Intimate Wedding Bali: How to Plan a Private and Romantic Ceremony
content:

Even though it is more intimate than the regular wedding ceremony, you can still enjoy a refined and elegant wedding experience, which happens in Bali’s beautiful landscapes. For better insight, let’s discover an intimate wedding in Bali explanation in this article.
What Makes an Intimate Wedding in Bali Special

Unlike big ballroom weddings, Bali has spaces that feel personal. Cliff edges, jungle backdrops, private villas, or quiet beaches at sunset are available. This setting naturally brings people closer together during a private wedding in Bali. Every moment here feels shared.
Best Locations for an Intimate Wedding in Bali
You might wonder what the best location for an intimate wedding venue in Bali is. The setting is not just about the view. Whether it is the dramatic cliffs of Uluwatu or the quiet jungles of Ubud, each destination offers a different kind of magic.
With vast landscapes and breathtaking backdrops, the Island of the Gods naturally becomes the perfect setting for a meaningful wedding ceremony. It allows newlyweds to remember the whole experience for the rest of their lives.
With beautiful backdrops of the jungle, Ubud has become a perfect place for a Bali wedding ceremony. You can choose the location based on your preference, whether it has a jungle setting or even a lush rice field view.
To experience an intimate setting, you can choose wedding venues in Ubud provided by Ini Vie Hospitality. It offers venues to make your wedding ceremony unforgettable and meaningful. One of the venues to choose from is Aksari Resort.

Besides Aksari Resort, you can choose Kaamala Resort Ubud as the wedding venue in Bali. It offers a unique charm, with a V-shaped Wedding Chapel that opens to lush jungle views. It is perfect for couples who want an intimate and modern ceremony.

Having a dream of getting married with sunset as the backdrop? You can choose the Seminyak Beachfront area for an intimate wedding. It blends romance, accessibility, and effortless elegance perfectly.
Iconic sunset backdrop creates a naturally cinematic setting for the ceremony. As the sky turns golden and the waves soften, your wedding moment feels warmer, intimate, and deeply emotional, even with minimal decoration.
Unlike any other hotspot tourist areas, Seminyak is located in the center of the tourism spot in Bali. Its central location makes it convenient and easily accessible for you and your guests. There is no need to pass through the rocky street or steep terrain, so the ceremony proceeds smoothly.
Imagine marrying someone you love with the vast ocean views and crashing waves above the cliffside Uluwatu. This experience will remain as the core memory for newlyweds, lingering forever in their minds.

Even this area has a breathtaking sunset view, which hits different from any other wedding venue across the island. The light softens, the sky turns warm, and everything feels slower. It creates a perfect moment for vows, photos, and quiet connection.
These two open space areas are perfect for taking vows. They are all accessible, allowing the ceremony to go smoothly without any obstacles. It is creating a seamless and enjoyable wedding experience.

The dining placement is already set in the Bali wedding package. It usually uses a long table or a single table setup to keep guests connected. Linen and tableware in soft colors are sometimes provided with earthy tones.
The photographers are also included, so the moment of taking vows with Bali’s pretty backdrop can be captured. They will wander around to capture all the moments happening during the wedding ceremony.
Tips for Planning an Intimate Wedding in Bali
Following these tips for planning a wedding in Bali is a must. These tips help ensure your wedding runs smoothly, preventing obstacles that might ruin your best day as you take vows with someone you love.
1. Setting Wedding Arrangements in the Dry Season
Since the weather in Bali is quite unpredictable, you can set the wedding arrangements during the dry season. The season itself starts from April to October, so you can plan to get married in that period to avoid rain messing up your wedding.
2. Inviting People Who Truly Matter to You
Furthermore, an intimate wedding is about being intentional. You can invite only the people who truly matter to both parties. It creates a deeper emotional connection and allows newlyweds to mingle with people whom they care about.
3. Choosing the Legally Recognized or Symbolic Ceremony
You can also choose between legal or symbolic ceremonies. For a legally recognized wedding in Bali, couples must follow Indonesian regulations, including a religious ceremony and civil registration.
While a symbolic ceremony is not legally binding. It is purely going for the experience, emotion, and celebration. Most couples doing this option are already legally married in their home country. They just want to have a moment of taking vows again with Bali’s landscape as the backdrop.
4. Booking the Venue in Advance
Another Bali wedding tip to follow is booking the venue in advance. Many places are often fully booked, so you have to book the venue around:
6-12 months before: It is before the peak season dates and popular venues
3-6 months before: It is possible for an intimate wedding, but options become more limited
1-3 months before: It is suitable for very small setups with flexible expectations.

title: Is Bali Expensive? Honest 2026 Cost Breakdown for Every Travel Style
content:
Is Bali expensive is a question many travelers ask before planning their trip. While Bali is no longer the ultra-cheap destination it once was, it still offers excellent value compared to many tropical destinations around the world.
Prices for accommodation, dining, and activities have increased in popular areas like Canggu, Seminyak, and Uluwatu, but there are still plenty of options for different budgets. In this guide, we break down Bali’s honest 2026 cost breakdown for every travel style.
Is Bali Still Affordable in 2026?
How much does a trip to Bali costs depends on your travel style, but Bali still offers options for almost every budget. While prices have increased in popular areas such as Canggu and Seminyak, affordable stays, boutique hotels, and luxury resorts continue to coexist across the island.
As part of this Bali budget guide, here is a general estimate of daily expenses in 2026:
Budget Traveler: IDR 450,000–750,000 ($30–$50) per day
Mid-Range Traveler: IDR 1,200,000–1,800,000 ($80–$120) per day
Luxury Traveler: IDR 4,500,000–7,500,000+ ($300–$500+) per day
One of the biggest factors affecting your spending is location. Bali accommodation prices in tourist hotspots are usually higher, while areas slightly away from the crowds often provide better value, more space, and a comfortable stay without the premium price tag.
Accommodation Costs in Bali
Accommodation is often the biggest part of your Bali travel expenses, but the island offers plenty of choices for different budgets and travel styles. From simple guesthouses to luxury resorts, there’s something for everyone.
Budget (Hostels & Guesthouses)
If you’re planning a trip to Bali on a budget, you can find basic rooms with shared facilities for around $10–$25 per night. Air-conditioned rooms are usually available from $20–$40 per night, especially in Kuta and some parts of Ubud.
Mid-Range (Boutique Hotels & Villas)
This category is popular among travelers looking for comfort without overspending. For $40–$120 per night, you can stay in stylish boutique hotels or private villas that often include breakfast and a swimming pool, making them a great choice for a honeymoon.
Luxury (5-Star Resorts & Private Villas)
Luxury stays typically start at $200 per night and can exceed $1,000 for premium resorts and private villas. Many offer beachfront locations, personalized services, and easy access to a fancy restaurant for a complete holiday experience.
For travelers creating a Bali daily budget, accommodation costs can vary significantly depending on location and season. If it’s your first time in Bali, a mid-range villa or boutique hotel often provides the best balance between comfort, convenience, and value.
Food & Drink Costs in Bali
Food is one of the easiest areas to adjust based on your budget. Whether you prefer local street food, trendy cafés, or upscale dining, the Bali food cost can range from very affordable to surprisingly luxurious.
Eating Like a Local (Warungs)
Local warungs offer some of the best value on the island. Famous dishes such as nasi goreng, mie goreng, and soto typically cost between IDR 15,000–35,000 ($1–$2.50), while drinks like fresh juice or young coconut are usually under IDR 40,000, making them a great option for solo traveling.
Mid-Range Cafes & Restaurants
Modern cafés and casual restaurants serve everything from Western breakfasts to smoothie bowls and fresh salads. Most meals cost around $5–$15 per dish, with daily spending at cafés generally ranging from $20–$40.
Beach Clubs, Fine Dining & Tourist Spots
Dining and drinking in Bali’s popular tourist areas come with higher prices. Cocktails usually cost $7–$12, while premium dining experiences can range from $20–$50 per main course, similar to what you might find when comparing Bali vs Thailand travel costs.
Overall, many travelers still find Bali to be cheaper than Thailand in certain categories, especially when eating at local warungs and family-run restaurants. However, luxury dining and beach club experiences can be just as expensive as those in other major tourist destinations.
Transport Costs in Bali
Getting around Bali can be as reasonably priced or as comfortable as you want. The cost of transport in Bali depends on the type of vehicle you choose and how far you plan to travel each day.
Renting a scooter is the most budget-friendly option, with prices typically ranging from $4–$8 (IDR 60,000–120,000) per day. It’s a popular choice for travelers who want the flexibility to explore at their own pace.
For short trips, ride-hailing apps like Grab and Gojek are convenient and cost-effective. Most rides cost between IDR 15,000–45,000 ($1–$3 ), making them ideal for quick journeys around town.
Car Rental & Private Driver
Hiring a private driver or renting a car with a driver usually costs around IDR 550,000–950,000 ($35–$60) per day. This option is good for families and travelers booking holiday packages that include multiple destinations.
Transfers from Ngurah Rai Airport to South Bali areas such as Seminyak, Jimbaran, or Nusa Dua generally cost between IDR 230,000–380,000 ($15–$25). Booking in advance can often make the process smoother.
Self-Drive Car Rental
If you prefer driving yourself, car rentals typically range from IDR 380,000–700,000 ($25–$45) per day. This can be a practical option for travelers planning longer stays or road trips across the island.
Activity & Sightseeing Costs in Bali
Activities and attractions can fit almost any budget, making them a flexible part of your Bali travel expenses. From cultural landmarks and nature spots to wellness experiences, there are plenty of ways to explore the island without overspending.
International visitors are required to pay a one-time tourist levy of IDR 150,000 upon arrival. Since the currency in Bali is the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR), it’s useful to have a basic understanding of local prices before your trip.
Cultural & Natural Attractions
Many of Bali’s most famous attractions are surprisingly wallet-friendly. Entrance fees for temples usually range from IDR 20,000–50,000, while waterfalls often charge between IDR 10,000–30,000, and the Ubud Monkey Forest costs around IDR 80,000 per person.
Bali offers a variety of activities for active travelers. Yoga classes generally cost $5–$15 per session, while private surf lessons typically range from $15–$35, depending on the location and instructor.
Tours & Wellness Experiences
Full-day tours usually cost around $20–$40 and are a convenient way to visit multiple attractions in one trip. For relaxation, traditional Balinese massages start from $10–$25 per hour at local spas, while premium spa experiences at luxury resorts can range from $40–$100 or more.
Is Bali Worth the Money?
So, is Bali expensive? Not necessarily. While Bali is no longer as cheap as it once was, it still offers outstanding value, with everything from budget-friendly stays to luxury experiences available across the island.
The key is choosing the right area and travel style for your budget. Whether you’re visiting for a backpacking trip or a honeymoon, Ini Vie Hospitality offers a collection of thoughtfully designed stays that combine comfort, location, and value in some of Bali’s most popular destinations.

title: Is Bali Safe for Tourists? Travel Advice and Updates 2026
content:
Maybe you’re wondering if Bali is safe or not, and the answer is absolutely! This tropical island is generally a safe place to visit for everyone, solo travelers, couples for a honeymoon, or families. The crime rate is low, especially when it comes to serious incidents involving tourists. That said, like any popular destination, it’s still smart to watch out for small stuff like pickpocketing or tourist scams.
Most people find this island of the Gods not only safe but also super welcoming. Locals are friendly, the vibe is peaceful, and many travelers keep coming back because they feel at home. As long as you stay alert and use common sense, you’ll have an amazing (and safe) time. But if you’re still wondering, is Bali safe for tourists? This travel advice and updates for 2026:
Yes, Bali is safe for international travelers. Every month, thousands of tourists come to enjoy its beaches, culture, and natural beauty without any major problems. Locals are friendly and respectful, and their tourist spots in Bali like Seminyak, Ubud, Canggu, and Nusa Dua are well-developed with good security. Still, it’s smart to be cautious of a few common issues:
Scams or tourist traps around money exchange or transport
Pickpocketing in crowded spots
Traffic accidents, especially for inexperienced motorbike riders
As long as you stay alert and use common sense, this island is a great and safe place to explore.
The Bali crime rate is relatively low, especially when compared to big cities in other countries. Serious crimes targeting tourists are rare. The local government takes safety seriously, especially in popular tourist hubs like Kuta, Seminyak, and Canggu, which have more security and tourist police. Overall, you can feel comfortable visiting Bali; it’s peaceful, safe, and traveler-friendly.
What Crimes Often Occur in Bali and How to Avoid Scammers
Here’s a simple breakdown of common risks in this island and how to avoid them, nothing too serious, but it’s always smart to stay informed. If you’re wondering about crime in Bali or Bali travel warnings today, these are the real things to watch for:
1. Scammers & Booking Fraud
This usually shows up as fake villa listings on social media, “tour guides” who aren’t legit, or big discount deals that don’t exist. How to avoid it:
Book through trusted platforms like Booking.com, Agoda, Airbnb, or directly via the resort’s website.
Don’t send money to personal accounts without a proper invoice.
Be cautious with pushy salespeople or offers that seem too good to be true.
2. Health & Safety Issues
From upset stomachs to sunburn or minor bike accidents, these are common traveler hiccups. How to avoid it:
Only drink bottled water, and avoid ice from unknown sources.
Use sunscreen and drink plenty of water even when it’s the rainy season in Bali.
Always wear a helmet if riding a scooter, and only rent if you’re confident driving.
Travel insurance with health coverage is highly recommended.
This typically happens in crowded areas like beach clubs, art markets, or night markets.
Don’t carry all your money or valuables with you.
Use a secure sling bag or anti-theft fanny pack.
Leave your passport and extra cards locked in your hotel safe.
4. Currency Exchange Scams
Some unofficial money changers use sneaky tricks when counting. How to avoid it:
Only exchange at licensed places marked “Authorized” and registered with Bank Indonesia.
Count your cash on the spot before walking away.
Skip money changers in shady alleys or too-good-to-be-true spots.
5. Transportation Scams
Some taxi drivers may offer off-the-app rides at inflated prices. How to avoid it:
Use ride apps like Gojek or Grab.
For taxis, go with Blue Bird—they use meters and are reliable.
Always agree on a price upfront if you go off-app.
6. Watch Out for Animals
Bali is full of wildlife, and while most animals are harmless, some can cause trouble. Monkeys, especially in places like Monkey Forest Ubud, love grabbing things like sunglasses, phones, and snacks. Stray dogs can sometimes be aggressive, and rural areas might have snakes or lots of mosquitoes. How to avoid it:
Don’t carry visible food when visiting monkey spots.
Avoid touching or getting too close to stray dogs, definitely no eye contact or sudden movements.
Use mosquito repellent and stay away from dark, damp spots at night.
7. Avoiding Food Poisoning
Not every stomach is ready for local eats, and food poisoning is one of the most common travel hiccups. Symptoms include nausea, diarrhea, and cramps, no fun during vacation. How to avoid it:
Stick to busy, clean-looking restaurants.
Skip the ice unless you’re sure it’s from filtered water.
Avoid seafood that looks off or food that’s been sitting out too long.
Pack activated charcoal or basic meds just in case.
Final Thoughts on a Bali Vacation
Absolutely, Bali is safe for everyone. Even when it comes to concerns like spiders or money-related matters, as long as you stay aware and follow basic safety tips, Bali remains one of the most welcoming, peaceful, and enjoyable destinations in the world. Most travelers feel right at home thanks to the island’s kind locals, vibrant culture, and laid-back vibe.
For those looking for a secure, comfortable stay, Ini Vie Hospitality stands out as one of the best in Bali. Known for boutique resorts with international standards, Ini Vie is trusted by travelers for its excellent service and transparent booking process, far from scams or surprises. If you want a Bali experience that’s both beautiful and worry-free, Ini Vie is a name you can count on.

title: Is Bali Safe for Solo Female Travelers? Safety Tips and Local Advice
content:
The question of ‘Is Bali safe for solo female travelers?” often appears as they want to visit Dewata Island alone. Female travelers do not have to worry because Dewata Island’s culture is genuinely warm, as locals are known for being kind and respectful.
Having a solo trip on the Island of the Gods is possible for women. Bali is known for its tourism, so female travelers can come there alone. Knowing ‘Is Bali safe for solo female travelers’ is important, so here is the explanation.
The Reality of Solo Female Travel in Bali
A Bali solo trip will make women feel excited. They can visit many tourist places which are already famous, such as Canggu Beach, Panglipuran Village, and beach clubs like Tropical Temptation Beach Club.
However, struggling with anxiety is inevitable when having a solo trip in Bali. They might wonder whether it is the right choice for them to travel or not because they will visit a new place with different cultures and traditions.
Realistically, having Bali solo travel for a female is fun. They will feel safe since the locals are warm and love to greet them with a smile. All the locals are respectful, making women feel secure while wandering across the island.
To ensure traveling is fun in Bali, they have to calculate the cost to spend during the trip. A guide to know how much it cost to go to Dewata Island helps travelers to budget their money well, so they will not encounter a money shortage.
Upon arrival on Dewata Island, female travelers have to buy the local SIM card or eSIM. Following the Bali SIM card guide will enable them to use the internet during the trip, avoiding them being afraid of losing signal.
It is also important to know more about the tourist tax on the Island of the Gods. The tourist tax explanation helps tourists to pay it on time with a precise amount.
The Safest Areas to Base Yourself in Bali
Experiencing tourism, like wellness tourism, brings excitement for a traveler. The Island of the Gods is definitely safe for women because locals here believe in Balinese karma, which works by deeds.
In Dewata Island, karma comes from Balinese Hinduism, which blends Hindu philosophy with local traditions. The core itself defines karma as “Every deed, good or bad, creates a consequence.”
Balinese karma is not an instant consequence for locals. It is more like a long-term balance system affecting locals’ current lives and future lives. No wonder people in Bali are respectful to each other to avoid karma.
With this belief, the crime rate in Dewata Island is relatively low. It is not zero since petty and opportunistic stuff crime may happen during a Bali solo trip. However, the violent crime is very rare, making them feel safe when it comes to Dewata Island.
Overall, the crime rate in Dewata Island is divided into three parts, which are:
Violent Crime: Very rare
Petty Crime: The most common
Tourists-targeted scams: Occasional yet manageable.
The petty crime might happen in the high-traffic tourist areas like Kuta, Seminyak, and Canggu. So, it is recommended for women to visit and stay in areas that are safe for tourists, so they can find a community and join other solo trippers to explore Bali more.
One of the safest areas in Dewata Island is Sanur. There are many things to do in Sanur, like walking on the beachfront to enjoy the scenery there. This area offers a slower crowd, which is less chaotic than Canggu
Since it is less crowded compared to other hotspots in Dewata Island, they can enjoy the sunrise in calm. The moment of seeing how the beautiful sun rises and shines over the whole island.
Stepping into the south of the Island of the Gods, they can come to Nusa Dua since the place is not as crowded as Canggu. Following a guide to things to do in Nusa Dua will help them to visit the right place for zero stress.
The environment in Nusa Dua is respectful, making it part of Dewata Island safe for women. They can walk on the beachfront and even swim since the water is relatively calm, so it is perfect for them to spend their best time during their trip in Dewata Island.
Besides, they can come to Ubud to experience Bali retreats for solo travel. Doing yoga and meditation with beautiful scenery will bring tranquility, helping travelers to reach peace after having to hustle and bustle in the city.
Getting Around Bali Safely as a Solo Woman
Traveling around the Island of the Gods as a woman is truly fun. There are many places to explore across this island. Therefore, ensuring safety during Bali solo travel for a female is important, so a woman should know the rides to take.
For a safe trip, female travelers can book a ride. In Bali, there are many ride-hailing options to choose from, like Gojek, Grab, and Maxim, to get around Dewata Island safely. They can mobilize from one place to another without having to be scared of getting lost on the island.
2. Private Rental Car
Private rental cars are also available, making Bali safe for women. They can rent a car with a private driver to wander across the island easily, so that they arrive safe and sound at their destination.
Since it offers ultimate comfort during the trip, women have to spend more money to rent a private car. For a full-day trip, they have to pay around IDR 600.000 – 800.000 and IDR 400.000 – 600.000 for a half-day trip.
These prices have already included the driver, parking fee, and hotel pick-up and drop-off. Therefore, women only have to wait for the driver to fetch them, then go to the destination in comfort.
During a Bali solo trip, women travelers can also rent a scooter to help them get around quickly from one place to another. Riding a rental scooter helps travelers avoid traffic jams.
However, female travelers have to be careful while riding the scooter. Making sure to use a helmet during riding can help them to avoid injuries from accidents. So, the traveling moment will be more enjoyable if a traveler follows the rules for riding a scooter.
5 Safety Tips for Female Travelers in Bali
As an answer to “Is Bali safe for solo female travelers?” Women travelers should follow all the safety tips. These tips help women to prevent dangers and accidents that they never expected. Here are 5 safety tips to follow:
1. Proposing Travel Insurance
For advanced safety in having a Bali solo trip, women should consider travel insurance for their safety. This insurance helps them to cut the cost if accidents happen there. Insurance also avoids women during trips from flights and luggage drama.
2. Avoiding Drinking from Tap Water
Never try to drink tap water. It can trigger women travelers to get Bali belly, a term for travelers’ diarrhea due to unclean food and water. It is important to avoid eating foods that have been sitting for a long time since they are not fresh anymore.
3. Do Not Use Phone during Riding a Motorcycle
Petty thieves come unpredictably; they might come when female travelers ride a scooter. The thieves can snatch travelers’ phones easily, so female travelers have to avoid using the phone during riding a motorcycle.
4. Paying Attention to Their Belongings
When female travelers come to tourist areas, whether it is a beach, restaurants, or drink place, they have to pay attention to their belongings. Petty theft might happen when the opportunity to steal is there.
If female travelers want to drink, they should find Bali female travel communities. This helps them to drink together, avoiding petty theft or flirtatious men with bad intentions to take goods from travelers.
5. Meeting other Solo Travelers
When the trip becomes overwhelming, female travelers can meet other solo travelers to ask for the best guide or recommendation for the place to visit. Solo travel in Bali for a female will be more fun if meeting other travelers to share some insight about Dewata Island.
Here are some frequently asked questions (FAQs) that appear when a women planning a Dewata Island solo trip:
1. Where are safe areas to stay in Bali for solo travelers?
For travelers, they can choose Sanur or Nusa Dua to stay. These areas have respectful environments and are relatively calm, creating ultimate tranquility for travelers.
2. Is Canggu safe at night?
Yes, it is generally safe, but the area is busy and quite chaotic. Female travelers still have to take care of their belongings during the trip in Canggu at night to avoid petty thieves taking the opportunity to steal.
3. Is Ubud safe for solo female travel?
Yes, Ubud is a safe place for solo female travelers. The place offers tranquility and respects local culture, making them comfortable and welcome. If they are interested in going there solo, women have to know the guide to things to do in Ubud.
4. Where are the best places in Bali for solo travelers?
If solo travelers seek peace from the hustle and bustle, they can come to Ubud, Sanur, and Nusa Dua since these three places are pretty calm, less crowded, yet still have many recreational activities.
But if they want to have a great night, they can come to Canggu, Seminyak, or Kuta and visit all the nightclubs there. The nightclubs offer a remarkable night for them through drinks and dancing all night long.
5. Where are the safest areas in Bali for tourists
