The safest areas in Bali are Nusa Dua and Sanur. Nusa Dua has a very clean area and is well-organized, making it easier for solo travelers to walk around. While Sanur is completely calm with walkable beachfront paths, they can enjoy their day and night on the beach.

title: Italian Dinner at Cantina Classe Canggu: Here’s What We Think
content:
Cantina Classe Canggu was already on my list long before this visit, mostly because everyone kept calling it one of the best Italian spots in Canggu, which happened to be my first stop in Bali. This Italian restaurant near the Batu Bolong area is located right in the heart of Canggu on Padang Linjong Street, making it easy to reach from most villas, cafés, and even shopping centers in the Canggu area.
From the moment I walked in, I was greeted by a charming and rustic interior and attentive staff who kindly opened the door for me. The aroma of freshly cooked food immediately made me realize this was not just another Italian restaurant Canggu is known for, but a place that truly takes flavor and dining experience seriously, something that stands out in the Italian Canggu scene.
If you’re searching for the best Italian restaurant Bali has to offer or simply craving the best pasta with Canggu style, this review should help you decide if this place deserves a spot on your dinner plans. I’ll try to be completely honest with you.
Location and Dinner Timing at Cantina Classe Canggu
Cantina Classe Canggu sits in a lively part of Canggu, surrounded by beautiful villas, cheap yet stylish Canggu hostels, and rice fields. The greenery helps balance the tropical heat, so while the weather can still feel humid, it’s not overly hot, especially in the evening.
The location is strategic, but like most popular spots, including a big playground, making this area also perfect for those visiting Canggu with kids. Traffic can build up quickly around sunset, so in my opinion, the best time to arrive is before 6 PM or after 8 PM if you want to avoid traffic and enjoy a smoother drive.
Parking is available nearby, but coming by scooter, as I did, is definitely the easiest option. For cars, I recommend a quick drop off right in front of the restaurant, then finding parking a bit further down the street.
Ambience and Experience
The vibe instantly gave me date night energy, but I also noticed groups of friends enjoying long, relaxed dinners together. It works beautifully for both romantic evenings and social gatherings, which is not always easy to achieve.
The restaurant features a rustic style with exposed brick walls, and the chandelier adds an enchanting touch to the space. Wooden seating keeps the atmosphere casual yet intimate, especially when you visit with your loved ones.
Cantina Classe Canggu offers both indoor and outdoor seating. The indoor area feels cozy and warm, while the outdoor section is breezier and more relaxed. The noise level is lively but not overwhelming, making it the kind of Italian restaurant near you where you can linger, chat, and maybe order one more glass of wine without feeling rushed.
The menu is classic Italian with a confident modern touch. Everything feels well curated rather than overwhelming, very much like a traditional trattoria you’d expect from a quality Italian restaurant that Canggu diners appreciate.
Antipasti and starters feature a wide range of simple plates that highlight quality ingredients.
Pasta styles and sauces range from creamy to tomato-based and rich, slow-cooked options, all made fresh and homemade, which explains why many people call this one of the best pasta spots in Canggu.
Pizza is available with thin, crispy bases and balanced toppings, staying true to traditional Italian style.
Mains and sharing plates include chicken and meat dishes that feel hearty without being too heavy.
Desserts are comforting and classic, with crème brûlée being a crowd favorite among guests.
We arrived at Cantina Classe Canggu around 8 PM, just after a heavy Canggu downpour. Since we had not eaten anything after brunch, my friend and I decided to go all in and order quite a big feast, especially because this Italian restaurant, which Bali visitors love, offers so many tempting Italian dishes.
The menu follows a classic trattoria style, but their unique touch truly elevates each dish. As this was our first visit to what many consider the best Italian Canggu, we chose familiar items so we could really taste how well they execute the classics.
1. Pumpkin Soup and Eggplant Parmigiana
The Eggplant Parmigiana was good, offering a balanced sweet and sour flavor from the eggplant and tomato sauce. It worked nicely as a starter to cleanse our palates, but my personal favorite was the Pumpkin Soup.
The Pumpkin Soup was warm, comforting, and easy on my digestion. Cantina Classe’s version has a beautiful harmony of natural sweetness from the pumpkin and savory depth from herbs, finished with a subtle creamy touch that made it truly enjoyable.
2. Fettuccine Truffle Carbonara and Gnocchi Creamy Sauce
This was the overall favorite and easily lived up to its reputation as one of the best pasta Canggu has to offer. The Fettuccine Truffle Carbonara was rich, creamy, and deeply savory, with an intense earthy aroma from the truffle. The grilled beef on top was smoky and tender, while the crispy garlic added texture along with a hint of sweetness and nuttiness.
To balance the richness, we ordered the Gnocchi Creamy Sauce with seafood. The dish had a creamy and umami flavor from the shrimp, enhanced by nutmeg and their homemade fresh gnocchi. It felt lighter yet still satisfying.
3. Four Cheese Pizza and Salami Picante
The Four Cheese Pizza immediately caught my attention with its blend of mozzarella, gorgonzola, goat cheese, and parmesan. Combined with béchamel sauce and fresh parsley, the flavors were rich and beautifully layered.
Each bite was creamy, savory, and melted perfectly in the mouth, making it a great companion for cocktails. For contrast, we also ordered the Salami Picante.
This pizza leaned more toward a fresh and meaty profile, with strong umami from the tomato sauce, mushrooms, and spicy salami. Ordering both pizzas worked well, starting with cheesy richness and finishing with a lighter and savory bite.
4. Pork Loin Schnitzel and Chicken Parmigiana
The Pork Loin Schnitzel was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. The flavor was simple yet satisfying, with the natural savory taste of the pork shining through. Paired with arugula salad and fries, it felt comforting without being heavy.
The Chicken Parmigiana had more layered flavors from melted mozzarella, tomato sauce, and a hint of lemon. While the chicken breast itself was milder than the pork, the house tomato sauce elevated the dish nicely.
5. Creme Brulee and Tiramisu
Cantina Classe Canggu only serves two desserts, crème brûlée and tiramisu, so we ordered both. I personally love desserts that are not overly sweet, and Cantina’s crème brûlée was exactly that. It was creamy, lightly sweet, and refreshing, especially when paired with fresh strawberries.
The tiramisu was more classic, featuring mascarpone and a bold cocoa flavor. If you enjoy a slightly bitter chocolate profile, this dessert will definitely hit the spot.
To finish the meal, we ordered a Red Sangria. It followed the traditional red wine base but included local ingredients that added a unique fruity twist. Bold, refreshing, and well-balanced, it paired perfectly with the creamy dishes we had ordered.
If you’re visiting Cantina Classe Canggu, I highly recommend starting with the Pumpkin Soup, especially during Bali’s rainy season. For pasta lovers, the Truffle Fettuccine Carbonara is a must-try and easily justifies its place among the best Italian restaurant bali experiences.
For pizza, I personally prefer the Salami Picante, especially after eating creamy pasta. The Four Cheese Pizza is still excellent, particularly if you love rich and cheesy flavors.
For mains, the Pork Loin Schnitzel stands out as a satisfying and straightforward option. While they also offer steak, I found the pork more distinct compared to the beef already featured in the pasta. To end the meal, the crème brûlée is the dessert I would order again without hesitation.
Overall, Cantina Classe Canggu truly earns its reputation as one of the best Italian Canggu destinations and a standout Italian restaurant that Bali food lovers should not miss.
Portion Sizes and Sharing Tips
Portions at Cantina Classe Canggu are generous without being overwhelming. Some menu items offer small and regular portions, such as the gnocchi, which is why we chose the small size. The fettuccine, however, only comes in a regular portion, which is quite filling on its own.
For pizza, we ordered two slices of Salami Picante and a small Four Cheese Pizza. This combination worked perfectly for two people and did not feel too heavy, especially when paired with pasta. Sharing like this is a great way to enjoy more variety without over-ordering at this Italian restaurant in Canggu.
The wine list leans heavily toward Italian labels, which fits the concept of this Italian Restaurant that Bali diners appreciate. Cocktails are available, but wine clearly takes center stage. There are also mocktails and non-alcoholic options if you prefer something lighter.
Since it was only my second day in Bali, I did not want to drink too much and chose something familiar, the Red Sangria. That said, I was very tempted by their innovative cocktails like the Aperol Mule and Negroni di Bali, both of which highlight Balinese tropical flavors in a creative way.
On average, expect to spend a mid-range amount per person. It is not cheap, but the pricing feels fair for the quality you receive. The most expensive dish we ordered was the Fettuccine Truffle Carbonara, priced at IDR 255,000, or around 15 USD.
What feels premium here is the pasta and overall execution. The drinks pricing feels more average, which is quite standard for Canggu. Overall, for the best Italian restaurant Bali experience, the value feels well-balanced.
The service was friendly, attentive, and well paced. Even on a busy night following a heavy downpour, the staff handled orders smoothly and checked in regularly without hovering.
They were also helpful with menu guidance, especially when explaining pasta options. This kind of service makes a big difference during peak hours when the restaurant is full.
Vegetarian options are easy to find, particularly among the pasta and pizza selections. Gluten-free options are limited, but it is worth asking the staff, as they are accommodating whenever possible.
What Customers Are Saying
Most customers praise the food quality, especially the pasta and consistency across visits. Complaints usually focus on busy hours and waiting times, which is common for popular restaurants.
Overall, Cantina Classe Canggu has built a strong reputation for consistency, which is why it is often mentioned as one of the best Italian restaurant Canggu destinations.
This place is perfect for date nights, relaxed group dinners, and anyone craving authentic Italian food. If you are looking for the best Italian restaurant Canggu has to offer, this should be high on your list.
I would rate it highly for food, atmosphere, and consistency. It is a solid choice whether you live in Bali or are visiting and exploring an Italian restaurant in Bali.
1. Do I need a reservation at Cantina Classe Canggu?
Yes, especially on weekends and during dinner hours.
2. What’s better, pasta or pizza at Cantina Classe Canggu?
Pasta, without question. Almost all of the pasta is homemade and uses locally sourced ingredients, which makes it truly shine.
3. What’s the budget estimate at Cantina Classe Canggu?
Mid-range spending of around IDR 400,000 to IDR 600,000 per person, depending on drinks and sharing style.

title: 15 Best Italian Restaurants in Bali, Authentic Nonna-Style Flavors
content:
If you’re craving the true taste of Italy right on the island, Italian restaurants Bali offer just that. From handmade pasta to wood-fired pizzas, many of these restaurants are owned or led by Italian chefs who stay true to authentic recipes and top-quality ingredients. Some even imported straight from Italy.
Whether you’re planning a cozy date night, a family dinner, or just craving comforting Italian food, this guide has you covered. Here are 15 of the best Italian restaurants in Bali serving up those rich, nonna-style flavors everyone loves.
If you’re looking for an Italian restaurant in Canggu that feels both laid-back and elegant, Cantina Classe is a must-visit. With its cozy red-brick interior, it’s the perfect spot for a romantic dinner or an intimate catch-up with friends.
The restaurant is known for its handcrafted Italian dishes, made with care and passion. Their pasta is made fresh daily. Don’t miss the Fettuccine Truffle Carbonara, Tagliatelle Seafood Base, and their signature wood-fired pizzas, which are some of the best on the island.
Nestled in the heart of Ubud, Habitat Bistro is one of the best Italian restaurants in Bali, offering a bold twist on classic bistro flavors. Its menu highlights indulgent dishes like Lobster Spaghetti, Lamb Pappardelle, and perfectly cooked Ribeye Steak.
Set against the lush greenery of Ubud, this best restaurant in Ubud delivers a calm, relaxing vibe, ideal for a peaceful breakfast or a cozy evening meal away from the crowds.
For a truly refined Italian restaurant experience, Amici Bali delivers sophistication with every bite. Perfect for romantic dinners or special celebrations, this chic spot serves up creative takes on classic Italian food in a stylish, elegant setting.
Must-try dishes include Uovo 62° e Tartufo, a slow-cooked eggs with pecorino cream and black truffles. Don’t forget Tartare di Manzo e Midollo, a rich Wagyu beef tartare with bone marrow. With its high ceilings, natural tones, and cozy terrace bar, Amici is where fine dining meets Italian warmth. You don’t have to always look for typical Balinese food, a little twist will make your holiday better.
4. Rustica Cucina Italiana
If you’re craving comforting, home-style Italian food, Rustica Cucina Italiana is the place to be. Known for its authentic recipes from Mamma Luigina, this cozy eatery serves hearty dishes like Lasagna, Prosciutto Cotto & Funghi Pizza, and Margherita Pizza, all made with fresh, simple ingredients.
The rustic wooden interiors give it that Italian family-home vibe, perfect for a relaxed meal with loved ones. For anyone hunting down the best pasta in Canggu, Rustica is a must-try.
5. Baliterraneo Restaurant Bali
Blending the flavors of Italy and the Mediterranean, Baliterraneo is one of the best restaurants in Seminyak for an elegant yet relaxed dining experience. The menu highlights fresh seafood and Italian food favorites like Spaghetti ai Sapori di Mare, Rigatoni alla Norma, and Quattro Formaggi Pizza.
Its serene ambiance, Mediterranean-inspired design, and lush poolside setting make it a perfect escape for a romantic dinner or leisurely lunch, a true hidden gem that could easily be mistaken for a Greek restaurant in Seminyak.
6. Otello’s Osteria Italian Restaurant
Tucked away in Umalas, Otello’s Osteria is a one of cozy Italian restaurants in Bali that feels just like your friendly neighborhood trattoria. Known for its relaxed vibe and honest, homemade Italian food, Otello’s serves classic dishes made from scratch, no fancy tricks, just pure flavor.
Favorites include Tagliatelle Pesto Alla Genovese, Tagliatelle Sorrentina, and Gnocchi Sorrentina, all crafted with love. With its simple yet inviting charm, it’s the perfect place for lunch, a sunset aperitivo, or a laid-back dinner with friends, the true taste of il dolce far niente (the sweetness of doing nothing).
7. L’Osteria Pizza e Cucina
One of the one of popular Italian restaurants in Bali, L’Osteria Pizza e Cucina has earned a reputation for serving some of the best pasta in Bali and the most authentic Neapolitan pizzas on the island. Its famous location is in Ubud, making it the most sought-after Italian restaurant in Ubud.
Their handcrafted dough and traditional recipes bring Italy to your plate. Don’t miss the Capricciosa Pizza or one of their rich pasta dishes. The interiors are bright and elegant yet relaxed, with a strong Italian vibe perfect for casual gatherings or date nights. Pair your meal with a cocktail or their house-made limoncello for the full experience.
8. Artista Cucina Bali
Located in the heart of Canggu, Artista Cucina is a charming Italian restaurant Canggu known for its homemade pasta, cozy atmosphere, and irresistible desserts. The space may be small, but the flavors are big, from the juicy Porchetta to the flavorful Spaghetti Vongole with Bottarga.
Their tiramisu is also a crowd favorite. With its café-style charm and reasonable prices, Artista Cucina is perfect for brunch or a relaxed evening dinner with a touch of Italian warmth.
If you’re looking for the best Italian restaurant in Bali for a romantic night out, Mauri Restaurant is the definition of elegance and artistry. Led by Chef Maurizio Bombini, this fine-dining gem showcases refined Italian cuisine crafted with fresh ingredients, many sourced directly from their own rooftop garden.
The Signature Tasting Menu, a five-course culinary journey, perfectly captures Chef Mauri’s modern take on Italian flavors. With its Puglia-inspired white interiors, serene ambiance, and exceptional service, Mauri promises a truly unforgettable dining experience in Seminyak.
10. Numero Quattro Echo Beach
Located in the vibrant Canggu area, Numero Quattro brings the one of warmth of an authentic Italian restaurants in Bali to the laid-back beachside scene. Known for its cozy, homey atmosphere and open kitchen, this spot serves Italian comfort food with flair.
Must-try dishes include the Spicy Gin Rigatoni and Maltagliati Beef Shin Pasta, both bursting with rich, smoky flavors. The wooden interiors and seaside vibe make it perfect for casual dinners, good wine, and easy conversations, Italian dining at its most relaxed.
11. Milano Italian Restaurant
A local favorite in Berawa, Milano is one of the best Italian restaurants for those who love hearty, comforting Italian food in a friendly, laid-back setting. The menu focuses on familiar classics done right, from Gnocchi Alla Sorrentina and Pappardelle Con Tartufo to Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe, each dish feels like a warm Italian hug.
With its inviting outdoor area and casual charm, Milano is perfect for everything from a sunny lunch to an intimate dinner under the Canggu sky.
12. Lusiana’s Kitchen
A true hidden gem, Lusiana’s Kitchen is a favorite Italian restaurant in Bali for those who love generous portions, homemade flavors, and great prices. Locals and travelers alike come for its fresh pasta and signature sourdough pizza, both made with care and heart.
Must-try dishes include the rich Ravioli alla Norcina and tender Steak Tenderloin, perfect for any meal of the day. While the small roadside setting adds a bit of buzz, the food and warm service make every visit feel like dining at a friend’s home, simple, honest, and full of flavor.
For something completely different, Sa’Mesa redefines Italian dining in Bali with its “communal dining” concept, where guests share a long table, an 18-course rotating feast, and plenty of laughter. There’s no menu to choose from, only a surprise lineup of authentic Italian dishes inspired by La Nonna Carmela.
Every night feels like a family gathering, where you come as strangers and leave as friends. It’s more than dinner, it’s an experience filled with stories, music, and that signature Italian warmth.
14. Massimo Italian Restaurant
An icon and the best restaurant in Sanur, Massimo is often called the heart of authentic Italian food in Bali. Run by Chef Massimo Sacco, this lively spot is always buzzing, especially the gelato counter out front, where lines form daily.
The restaurant specializes in homemade pasta, mozzarella, burrata, and wood-fired pizza, all rooted in the Salento region’s traditions. Don’t miss their creamy Pistachio Gelato or Lasagna al Forno, both crowd favorites. With its cozy, family-style atmosphere and friendly charm, Massimo feels like stepping straight into a cheerful Italian neighborhood, right here in Bali.
15. Tiamo Restaurant & Gelato Seminyak
If you’re looking for a cozy yet stylish Italian restaurant Seminyak, Bali. Tiamo is the perfect all-day dining spot that captures the essence of Italian comfort and charm. From hearty breakfasts to elegant dinners, every dish here is made with fresh, high-quality ingredients.
Must-tries include the Pappardelle Alla Coscia Di Agnello e Retrizione Ossobuco and the perfectly creamy Classic Carbonara, both bursting with authentic Italian flavor. Don’t skip their homemade gelato, a crowd favorite for a sweet finish.
The space is bright and welcoming, featuring a lush, greenery-filled upstairs area and a charming heart-shaped photo spot outside. With warm, attentive service and a relaxed atmosphere, Tiamo delivers a delightful taste of Italy in the heart of Seminyak.
Final Thoughts on: Savoring Authentic Nonna-Style Flavors in Bali
Exploring an Italian restaurant Bali means diving into a world of rich flavors, handmade pasta, and heartwarming dishes that feel just like home. From fine dining gems to cozy trattorias, each spot captures the true essence of Italy, where every bite tells a story of passion and tradition.
And if you’re craving a luxurious coastal dining experience, don’t miss a seafood restaurant Seminyak for the perfect mix of ocean views and Mediterranean flair. For the best curated culinary and stay experiences on the island, Ini Vie Hospitality stands out as Bali’s leading hospitality company, redefining comfort, creativity, and exceptional service across every destination.

title: What to Do in Kintamani Bali: What to See, Eat, and Where to Stay
content:
The beach in Bali might be the most well-known attraction, but there are many other destinations to explore, including Kintamani Bali, the island’s northeast highland region. This area is centered around the massive Batur caldera, which encompasses the active Mount Batur Kintamani volcano in Bali and the stunning Lake Batur.
Visiting this highland offers a cultural and natural experience that is completely different from the southern resort areas, showing you that there are so many things to do in Bali beyond the beach. From a sunrise jeep adventure to enjoying local coffee and dining with panoramic views, there are countless activities to add to your Kintamani tour in Bali.
Kintamani Things To Do
Your focus here should be on maximizing the region’s volcanic landscape and natural beauty. This area of Bali is generally considered safe for travelers, and the main attractions are well-managed. Here are the best activities to include in your itinerary:
1. Mount Batur Sunrise Jeep Tour
The most popular activity in Kintamani Bali, is the Mount Batur sunrise jeep tour. From here, you can watch the sunrise over the eastern horizon, with rays of light reflecting on the dramatic black lava fields.
A 4×4 jeep will take you closer to the caldera, offering unforgettable panoramic views. If you want something more adventurous, trekking to the summit of Mount Batur Kintamani, Bali, is a bucket-list experience.
Starting before dawn, this trek rewards you with spectacular views of the entire Kintamani volcano region. For families, this activity is safe and kid-friendly, making it an accessible way to experience this iconic Bali adventure.
2. Discover Kintamani’s Geological Wonders Museum
Many tourists do not realize that this area is home to the Batur UNESCO Global Geopark, which highlights the area’s complete volcanic landscape, including caldera walls, craters, geothermal activity, lava fields, and Lake Batur.
The museum showcases how communities have adapted to living in harmony with the volcanic environment for centuries. This attraction enriches any Kintamani volcano tour in Bali, offering both educational and cultural insights, perfect for filling up your Bali itinerary.
3. Pinggan Sunrise View Pohon Cinta
Locals call this viewpoint the “village above the clouds” because, at sunrise, the fog often blankets Mount Batur. From Pinggan Village, located across the caldera, you can enjoy one of the most breathtaking perspectives of the Batur Volcano and Lake.
The spot is popular for photography and is often used for camping. It’s a peaceful escape that showcases the untouched beauty of Kintamani Bali, perfect for travelers who want more than the usual tourist trail and unique things to do in Bali.
Lake Batur, the crescent-shaped volcanic lake at the base of Mount Batur, is a tranquil counterpart to the rugged volcano. You can visit the floating fish farms, take a lakeside stroll, or simply relax at a small café.
Local coffee stalls like Kopi Danu serve traditional coffee with a modern twist, offering the perfect place to enjoy the views. For a complete cultural experience, include a stop at Kintamani temple in Bali, which overlooks the lake and is often used by locals for spiritual ceremonies.
5. Enjoy a Bite to Eat on Penelokan Main Road
Penelokan, which means “place to look,” is lined with restaurants and cafés offering direct views of the volcano and the lake. Popular coffee shops such as Paperhills, Akasa Specialty Coffee, and TeguKopi create a modern atmosphere, while international brands like Starbucks have also found a home here.
Stopping for a meal or coffee along this road is an essential part of any tour here, as the views from Penelokan are some of the most striking in the region.
6. Volkswagen Jeep Adventure to Explore the Black Lava of Mount Batur
For a unique twist on the classic tour, take a ride in an open-air Volkswagen Jeep across the black lava fields left by Mount Batur’s historic eruptions. This thrilling activity gives a close-up view of the stark volcanic terrain while adding a fun retro vibe to your Kintamani volcano tour in Bali.
Many travelers dress in jeans and boots for photos, creating stylish, adventurous memories. For couples looking for a sweet and romantic photo, this place will be your perfect place to go.
7. Kintamani Scooter Tour
Exploring Kintamani by scooter allows you to set your own pace and discover hidden corners. Popular routes include Kedisan to Buahan, which runs along Lake Batur, and Toya Bungkah, which provides closer views of the volcano.
If you love more active adventures, try the downhill cycling tours. These guided rides start with the cool morning air and descend through traditional villages, rice fields, and temples before ending near Ubud. It is one of the most enjoyable ways to immerse yourself in the landscapes and communities here.
Best Spot to Eat in Kintamani, Bali
Dining in Kintamani, Bali, Indonesia, is all about the view: scenic sunrises, dramatic black lava fields, and of course, the magnificent volcano. Many restaurants and cafés here combine great food with breathtaking scenery, making them the perfect stop during your tour.
Ritatkala Cafe is known for its fantastic photo spots and wide-open views of Mount Batur Kintamani, Bali. It is a perfect stop for a mid-day meal or coffee break during your Kintamani volcano tour in Bali.
Their most popular dish is Mujair Nyatnyat (Mozambique Tilapia), a local staple in this region. For snacks, try Pisang Goreng (banana fritters) paired with an Americano or Long Black, a combination that has become a Balinese breakfast favorite.
This stylish café is a favorite among young locals, offering excellent coffee and contemporary light meals with an incredible backdrop of the Kintamani volcano view Bali. Their menu includes both local and international options, with Chicken Cordon Bleu and Furikake Rice Bowl being two of the most popular.
For sharing, the truffle fries are a great choice, especially in the cool air. It is an ideal morning or early afternoon stop during your Kintamani tour in Bali.
Paperhills offers a chic and modern setting, making it a favorite among influencers, travelers, and those seeking an upscale dining experience. The highlight of this café is not just its food but also the unique addition of a Kintamani hot spring Bali pool, which creates a dreamy atmosphere paired with a breathtaking volcano view.
Signature dishes like Shakshuka are best enjoyed at their poolside lounge, where you can soak in the sun and the fresh highland breeze. Arrive around 5:30 PM to secure the best seats for sunset.
Tegukopi is one of the pioneer coffee shops in Penelokan, offering spectacular Kintamani volcano view in Bali at more affordable prices compared to other cafés in the area. With its industrial décor, it has become a favorite for solo travelers and young adults.
Their coffee, made with local Arabica beans from local farmers, is presented in a modern style while keeping the authentic Balinese flavor. The menu also features a mix of local and Western dishes such as Mujair Nyatnyat and Big Brekkie. Families will love their buffet option, which offers great value.
These spots typically open from 5:30 AM to 9:00 PM, making them ideal for early risers who want to chase the sunrise. The average cost is around IDR 250,000 per person, similar to mid-range dining in Seminyak or Uluwatu, depending on what you order.
Best Place to Stay in Kintamani
To fully appreciate the beauty of Kintamani Bali, staying overnight is highly recommended. Many accommodations take advantage of the incredible Kintamani volcano view Bali, offering unique stays that combine comfort with natural splendor.
1. Black Lava Camp & Cafe
Black Lava Camp & Cafe allows you to camp directly on the black lava fields of Mount Batur Kintamani Bali, creating an immersive experience under the stars with the volcano as your backdrop. Though designed like a tent, the camp offers hotel-level amenities, including a hot spring pool and an on-site café.
Guests can enjoy breakfast with a sunrise view over Lake Batur, making it a standout choice for adventurous travelers.
Desa Oculus is a modern nature retreat, combining comfort with stunning views. It is an excellent base for your activities, including visits to Kintamani hot spring, Bali, and nearby temples.
Guests can wake up to mountain views and enjoy sunrise right from their windows. Beyond being a place to stay, Desa Oculus also organizes unique experiences such as jeep tours, hiking, water purification ceremonies, sunset picnics, Trunyan village tours, and lively evening events at Oclub.
Experience a Memorable Stay in Kintamani with Ini Vie Hospitality
Ini Vie Hospitality is recognized as one of Bali’s leading hospitality brands, known for creating stays that blend comfort, culture, and discovery. Guests staying at Kaamala Resort and Spa Ubud can enjoy curated experiences such as the exclusive Kintamani volcano tour, a journey that showcases Bali’s breathtaking landscapes and spiritual charm. Book your stay today to enjoy special rates and let Ini Vie Hospitality turn your Bali holiday into an unforgettable experience.

title: 5 Exciting Things to Discover at Love Anchor Canggu
content:
Love Anchor Canggu is a must-visit spot in this lively coastal village, which has quickly become one of Bali’s trendiest destinations. Located between Seminyak and Tanah Lot, Canggu offers a unique mix of beautiful beaches, cool cafes, urban art, and a thriving digital nomad scene.
In the heart of this vibrant area, Love Anchort stands out as a hub for shopping, local culture, and a laid-back tropical lifestyle. This boho-chic market is where you’ll find local designs, ethical fashion, and plenty of Instagram-worthy moments. If you’re planning to visit, here are 5 exciting things to check out at Love Anchor Canggu!
Love Anchor Location in Canggu
Love Anchor Market is located at Jl. Pantai Batu Bolong No. 56, just a 5-minute walk from Batu Bolong Beach, one of the most popular beaches in Canggu. This lively market is conveniently situated near Roomates Hostel by Ini Vie Hospitality, making it an easy and fun spot to explore for guests staying there. Surrounded by trendy cafes, boutique shops, and surf schools, it’s the perfect place to soak up Canggu’s vibrant atmosphere.
If you’re staying in Canggu, this market is just a short ride by motorbike or bicycle. From Seminyak or Berawa, it’s only about 15–20 minutes away. The area is also buzzing with ride-hailing services like Gojek and Grab, and there’s plenty of parking for bikes and cars, though it can get crowded on weekends or afternoons.
If you’re looking for a place to stay, Atap Resort or Astera Resort & Spa Canggu are great options for a comfortable vacation near all the action. And if you’re looking for a great way to experience local culture, be sure to check out the Sunday markets in Bali at Love Anchor Market, a perfect spot for unique finds! Plus, if you need to exchange currency, you’ll find plenty of spots nearby.
Things to Discover at Love Anchor Canggu
Love Anchor Bali isn’t just another market, it’s a hotspot for those who love the tropical lifestyle, local creativity, and Balinese vibes. Here’s what you’ll find when you visit Love Anchor Market Canggu:
1. Boho-Chic Fashion & Boutiques
Love Anchor boutique is home to a variety of local boutiques offering boho, tropical, and relaxed Balinese styles. You can shop for linen clothes, crochet tops, beach dresses, ethnic outerwear, and unique swimwear that’s hard to find anywhere else. Many of the items are limited edition and made from natural materials, making it a great spot for lovers of sustainable fashion. You can buy your outfits here before heading to your favorite beach club in town.
2. Houseware & Decor Bali Style
If you’re a fan of Canggu shopping with a Balinese touch, head to the houseware section at the market. You’ll find beautiful rattan decorations, bamboo chandeliers, woven baskets, and natural fiber wall art. Plus, by shopping here, you’re supporting local artisans and their creative work.
3. Vibrant & Dynamic Daily Bazaar
Every day, but especially on weekends, this shopping hub comes alive with a colorful outdoor bazaar. You’ll find everything from souvenirs, essential oils, and rattan bags to handmade jewelry, leather sandals, and lifestyle products like natural soaps and aromatherapy candles. This Sunday market Canggu, is perfect for picking up aesthetic and quality souvenirs.
4. Instagrammable Photo Studio
If you’re into snapping photos for your feed, this market has got you covered. There are cool spots like photo booths and tropical mini-studios for perfect social media content. The teak wood buildings, rattan walls, and iconic “LOVE ANCHOR” sign make this place super Instagram-worthy. It’s also a popular spot for pop-up events and mini fashion shows.
For those staying in Canggu or the surrounding areas, this market now offers alcohol delivery! You can easily order a variety of premium wines, spirits, and liquors straight to your villa or accommodation with a simple WhatsApp message. It’s perfect for villa parties, romantic dinners, or just chilling out at home. To keep your delivery costs down, you can stay at nearby resorts, such as Canggu Cabana Resort & Spa. In addition, its close location will make your travel easier.
Love Anchor Canggu opening hours are from 8 AM – 10 PM, making it the perfect place to visit any time of day. Whether you’re heading from Seminyak to Canggu or just exploring the area, you’ll find this market is a great stop. And don’t worry, Bali is safe for tourists, so you can enjoy everything this lively market has to offer with peace of mind. Be sure to check out Love Anchor Canggu reviews to see why this place is a must-visit in Bali!
Shopping in Canggu, especially at Love Anchor, isn’t just about picking up souvenirs; it’s about soaking in the laid-back Balinese vibe and lifestyle. Here are some tips to make your shopping experience fun, smart, and memorable:
1. Arrive Early for the Best Selection
This famous market opens daily, but it can get crowded in the afternoon. If you’re after unique items like handmade accessories, linen clothes, or rattan bags, arriving early will give you the best pick of the lot before the crowds arrive.
2. Bargaining Is Allowed, But Be Polite
While you cannot barter at Love Anchor, you can still get a good deal by bargaining. You can bargain, especially if you’re buying more than one item. Just remember to be polite and friendly during the process. Many stalls are run by local businesses, so a good attitude will not only help you get a better deal but also support the local economy.
3. Bring Your Own Shopping Bag
To stay eco-friendly, bring your own cloth bag for shopping. It’s a practical choice and makes you look like a mindful traveler who cares about sustainability.
4. Prepare Cash and E-Wallet
Although many vendors accept digital payments like QRIS, some still prefer cash. It’s a good idea to bring both cash and have your e-wallet ready for a smooth shopping experience. ATMs are nearby in Batu Bolong if you need cash.
5. Snap Photos at Aesthetic Spots
After your shopping spree, don’t miss the chance to take some photos at the market’s iconic spots like the “LOVE ANCHOR” neon sign and the rattan backgrounds. It’s perfect for a great Instagram post or just a beautiful memento of your time in Canggu.
Final Thought on Love Anchor Canggu
If you’re exploring Canggu, Love Anchor Canggu is a must-visit destination for shopping, local culture, and a relaxed tropical vibe. From stylish boutiques to Instagram-worthy photo spots, it perfectly captures the essence of Bali’s creative community. For those looking for exceptional hospitality during your stay, Ini Vie offers the best hospitality management in Bali with top properties in the Canggu area.

title: Tsune Uluwatu: Our Honest Take on the Sushi and Japanese Menu
content:
If you are currently sitting in your villa or nearby stay in Uluwatu, scrolling through your phone, and wondering where to find the most authentic lunch in the Bukit Peninsula, Tsune Uluwatu is the answer you have been searching for. My friend and I recently spent a sunny afternoon exploring the cliffs.
After working up a massive appetite, we stumbled upon this absolute gem of a Japanese restaurant in Bali that completely changed our day. Tsune Uluwatu is located right in the heart of the action, making it an easy pitstop for anyone exploring the southern beaches.
In this article, we are going to break down every single detail of our visit, from the texture of the rice to the smile of the servers, to give you in-depth information about our Tsune Uluwatu review. Here is our complete guide to enjoying a midday meal at one of the best Japanese restaurants on the island.
Getting There and Best Lunch Window
Getting to any location in the Bukit Peninsula area can sometimes feel like a little bit of an adventure, and finding Tsune Uluwatu is no exception to the rule. The restaurant is situated on the main road that snakes through the area, which means it is incredibly accessible whether you are coming from Padang Padang or heading down from the Pecatu entrance.
However, the traffic in this region has picked up significantly in recent years. If you are driving a car, you might find yourself moving quite slowly behind construction trucks or tour buses, so patience is definitely key.
For the absolute best experience at this Uluwatu Japanese restaurant, we highly recommend timing your arrival carefully to avoid the peak rush hours. We arrived right around 12:30 PM, which turned out to be the perfect window because the morning surf crowd had already eaten and the late lunch crowd had not arrived yet.
If you come too late, say around 2:00 PM, you might run into more traffic on the road as people head to the beaches for the sunset sessions.
Traffic notes and ideal arrival time
The traffic in Uluwatu can be unpredictable, often changing from clear roads to a complete standstill within minutes, depending on temple ceremonies or construction projects. We noticed that the roads are generally clearer just before noon.
If you are riding a scooter, you will have a much easier time weaving through the congestion, but always remember to wear a helmet and drive carefully on the winding asphalt. Ideally, you want to be walking through the doors of Tsune between 12:00 PM and 12:30 PM before your coffee break in Uluwatu.
This timing gives you the best choice of tables and ensures that the kitchen is fully prepped and ready to serve you without any significant wait times. It also allows you to finish your meal comfortably before the afternoon heat really sets in outside.
Parking, walk-in vs reservation
Parking is always a hot topic in Bali, and at Tsune Uluwatu, the situation is decent, but space is definitely at a premium. There is a designated area right in front for motorbikes, which is very convenient, but car parking can be a bit tricky if the designated spots are full. If you are driving a car, you might have to park a little further down the road and walk back, so keep that in mind if you are bringing the whole family.
Regarding seating, we decided to try our luck as walk-ins, and since it was a weekday lunch, we had no trouble getting a table immediately. However, if you are planning to visit during the high season or on a weekend, this Japanese restaurant in Uluwatu can get packed very quickly.
Making a reservation via WhatsApp just a few hours beforehand can save you the stress of waiting in the heat, especially if you are a large group. Here are the best tips for ensuring you have a smooth arrival experience at the restaurant.
Atmosphere at Tsune Uluwatu
The moment you step off the busy, sun-baked street and into Tsune Uluwatu, the atmosphere instantly feels calmer and incredibly refreshing. The semi-outdoor setting lets the ocean breeze brush your skin, and even with a bit of humidity, it’s still comfortable and easy to enjoy.
The interior design embraces a modern Bohemian aesthetic that meets Japanese elegance, utilizing plenty of light wood, clean lines, and soft lighting to create a space that feels both sophisticated and welcoming. Unlike the loud, bass-heavy vibe you get at many beach clubs in Uluwatu, this spot prioritizes tranquility and conversation.
We were able to talk without shouting, which is a rare luxury in some of the more popular tourist spots. The background music was a soft, lo-fi jazz playlist that set a relaxed mood without dominating the room. It feels like a place where you are meant to slow down and truly appreciate the food in front of you.
Calm lunch vibe vs lively vibe
During lunch hours, the vibe is decidedly calm, making it perfect for digital nomads looking to grab a quick bite or couples wanting a quiet date. The natural light floods in through the large windows, making the space feel airy and open.
It is a stark contrast to the nighttime atmosphere, which we hear gets a bit more lively and energetic as the dinner crowd rolls in for sake and platters. If you are looking for a party scene, this is not it, but if you want a sanctuary to recharge your batteries, it is perfect.
The energy is focused on the culinary experience rather than social posturing. You see people genuinely enjoying their food rather than just taking photos for Instagram, although the food is certainly pretty enough to photograph.
Seating recommendations
The restaurant offers a mix of seating options to suit different preferences, from solo diners to larger groups. We chose to sit at a table near the window to do some people-watching, but I found myself eyeing the counter seating.
Sitting at the sushi bar allows you to watch the chefs at work, slicing fish with precision and assembling rolls, which adds an element of entertainment to your meal. For a more intimate experience, there are tables tucked away in the corners that offer a bit more privacy.
The chairs are comfortable, designed for lingering over a meal rather than rushing through it. If you are staying at one of the boutique hotels in Uluwatu nearby, you will find that the level of comfort makes it hard to leave to go back to your room. Here are the best seats in the house, depending on your mood.
Sushi and Japanese Menu Overview at Tsune Uluwatu
When you look at the menu at Tsune Uluwatu, it becomes clear that the chefs have a deep respect for traditional Japanese culinary arts while understanding the local palate. It is not just about raw fish; it is a comprehensive tour of Japanese flavors.
As a leading Japanese restaurant in Uluwatu, they have curated a selection that covers everything from cold appetizers to steaming hot bowls of comfort food. The menu is well-organized and easy to navigate, even if you are not fluent in Japanese food terminology.
Each section is clearly labeled, and the staff is always on hand to explain what “aburi” or “ponzu” means if you get stuck. The focus is clearly on high-quality ingredients, which is the most important factor when you are dealing with simple dishes like sushi and sashimi.
Sushi and sashimi style
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the sushi selection in Uluwatu. They offer a wide range of nigiri (fish on rice), sashimi (slices of raw fish), and maki (rolls). The style leans towards traditional Edomae sushi but with some modern twists to keep things exciting.
The fish selection includes local catches like tuna and prawn, as well as imported favorites like wagyu, salmon, and unagi. We noticed that the rice-to-fish ratio was excellent. Often, restaurants will load you up on rice to fill you up cheaply, but here, the fish slice is generous and drapes beautifully over the small ball of vinegared rice.
The rolls range from simple classics like Salmon Mentai, Spicy Tempura Maki, Spicy Otoro, and a wide selection of Nigiri, accompanied with wasabi and gari (pickled ginger) for those who like a flavor explosion.
Hot dishes and comfort dishes
If raw fish is not your thing, do not worry, because the hot kitchen is just as capable as the sushi bar. They serve a variety of grilled fish sets that include rice and miso soup that feels like a warm hug for your stomach.
We also saw fancy items like Rib Eye MB5+ and Saikoro Wagyu Goma Dare, which are perfect for a hearty lunch or candlelit dinner. These dishes are great if you are feeling really hungry after a surf session and need some carbohydrates and protein to recover.
Portion sizes and freshness notes
The portion sizes at Tsune Uluwatu are surprisingly generous for a high-end Japanese spot. In many fine dining sushi places, you leave feeling hungry, but here, the rolls are substantial, and the rice bowls are packed. You definitely get your money’s worth in terms of quantity.
Regarding freshness, it was impeccable. As a premier Japanese restaurant in Bali, they cannot afford to serve anything less than pristine seafood. The tuna was a deep ruby red, not brown or dull, and the salmon had that perfect, vibrant orange sheen.
You could taste the ocean in every bite, but in a clean, sweet way, not a fishy way. Here is a breakdown of the specific items that landed on our table.
What We Ordered at Tsune Uluwatu
We decided to order a mix of items to truly test the range of the kitchen, from the cold raw bar to the hot grill. My friend and I have very different tastes; she loves the pure taste of sashimi, while I enjoy the texture and sauce of fusion rolls, so we covered a lot of ground. We wanted to see if Tsune Uluwatu could satisfy both purists and modern eaters.
Item list + quick bites and texture notes
This was our starter, and it set the bar high immediately. It featured thin slices of fresh salmon that were arranged beautifully on a long plate, generously topped with torched mentai sauce, generous spoonfuls of ikura (salmon roe), and fresh microgreens.
Texture: The contrast was incredible, silky smooth fish, and the creamy, slightly charred mentai sauce were perfectly accompanied by the crisp zucchini underneath, which added a surprising and necessary crunch.
Flavor: This dish is an umami bomb. It has rich, creamy, and savory flavors from the mentai; the ikura gives a salty “pop” in your mouth, while the zucchini keeps it fresh.
We couldn’t visit a high-end Japanese restaurant in Uluwatu without testing their premium cuts. The Otoro (fatty tuna belly) was served with a spicy kick that elevated the natural richness of the fish.
Texture: It literally melted in our mouths like butter. The fish requires almost no chewing, while the garnish adds a tiny bit of resistance.
Flavor: The natural sweetness of the tuna fat was balanced perfectly by the heat of the spice. It wasn’t overwhelmingly hot, just enough to cut through the richness of the belly fat.
3. Saikoro Wagyu Goma Dare
Moving to the hot dishes, we tried this cubed steak dish served with a traditional sesame dipping sauce. “Saikoro” refers to the diced style of the beef, making it easy to share.
Texture: The beef cubes were seared on the outside but remained incredibly tender and juicy on the inside.
Flavor: The beef was savory and smoky, but the star was the Goma Dare (sesame sauce). It added a nutty, deep profile that made the meat taste even more luxurious.
4. Salmon Teriyaki Set
For a complete lunch option, my friend ordered this set. It arrived as a massive tray that included the main grilled salmon, a bowl of steamed rice, hot miso soup, and several small side dishes (pickles and salads).
Texture: The salmon skin was grilled to a perfect crisp, while the flesh flaked apart easily with chopsticks. The rice was fluffy and sticky, just how it should be.
Flavor: The teriyaki glaze was the real deal, savory with a hint of sweetness, not the thick, sugary syrup you get at fast-food joints. It soaked into the rice beautifully.
We have a separate stomach for dessert, and this French-Japanese fusion pastry was calling our names.
Texture: The choux pastry was light and airy with a slight crispness to the shell, filled to the brim with smooth cream.
Flavor: If you love matcha, this is for you. The bitterness of the tea cream balanced the sweetness of the glaze, making it an indulgent treat that wasn’t too heavy.
6. Matcha Butterscotch Sea Salt
This was one of their signature beverages, and honestly, it could almost double as a dessert.
Texture: Creamy, velvety, and smooth.
Flavor: This was a rollercoaster. First, you get the earthy notes of the matcha, followed by the deep, caramel-like sweetness of butterscotch, and finally, a hit of sea salt that ties it all together. It is an addictive combination.
To wash everything down and cleanse the palate, I stuck with a warm cup of Hojicha (roasted green tea).
Texture: Light and warming.
Flavor: Unlike grassy green tea, Hojicha has a toasty, nutty, and almost caramel-like aroma. It was the perfect, soothing end to a very rich meal.
Must-Order Picks at Tsune Uluwatu
After tasting our way through the menu and eyeing what other tables were eating, we have compiled a definitive list of the best items. If you are overwhelmed by the choices of the best Japanese in Bali contenders, simply stick to this list, and you will not be disappointed.
The Spicy Otoro is non-negotiable. It offers the luxurious melt-in-your-mouth texture of fatty tuna belly, but the spicy topping adds a modern kick that cuts through the richness.
The Saikoro Wagyu Goma Dare. Forget standard steaks; these diced wagyu cubes are incredibly tender, and the nutty sesame dipping sauce (goma dare) is so good you will want to pour it over your rice.
The Salmon Mentai. It is the perfect crowd-pleaser, savory, creamy, and slightly smoky from the torching. The pop of ikura on top adds a texture that gets your palate ready for the main course.
The Matcha Butterscotch Sea Salt. It sounds like a lot, but it works. The saltiness elevates the caramel notes of the butterscotch, while the earthy matcha keeps it from being too sugary.
You simply must leave room for the Matcha Eclair. It is lighter than a cake but just as satisfying, with a crisp choux pastry shell and a filling that strikes the perfect balance between bitter tea and sweet cream.
Dining in Bukit can range from cheap local eats to incredibly expensive hotel restaurants, and Tsune Uluwatu sits comfortably in the middle-upper range. For the quality of ingredients, especially premium cuts like Otoro and Wagyu, we felt the pricing was fair. It is not a budget meal, but it is an accessible luxury.
Lunch spend estimate
For our meal, which included the premium Wagyu, Otoro, a set meal, and fancy drinks, the total bill came to roughly IDR 850,000 – 900,000 for two people. However, if you stick to just a set meal and tea, you could easily get out for under IDR 200,000 per person.
Best value choices for sushi lovers
If you want high-quality fish without breaking the bank, the Salmon Mentai offers great value. You get a substantial amount of fish and rich toppings that make it feel like a heavy, satisfying dish for a reasonable price.
Best value choices for non-sushi eaters
The Salmon Teriyaki Set is the undisputed value king. It is a complete meal on a tray, huge grilled salmon, miso soup, rice, and side dishes, that will leave you completely stuffed for a single fixed price.
Service in Bali is generally known for its warmth, and Tsune Uluwatu combines that Balinese hospitality with Japanese efficiency. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with a loud “Irasshaimase!” (Welcome!) from the staff, which sets a fun tone right away.
Timing, attentiveness, recommendations
Our waiter was incredibly attentive without hovering. He filled our Hojicha tea refills before we even had to ask. When we asked for recommendations, he didn’t just point to the most expensive item; he actually steered us toward the Saikoro Wagyu for sharing, which was a fantastic tip.
The timing of the food was also spot on. The Salmon Mentai appetizer arrived quickly, followed by the sushi, and the hot Salmon Teriyaki Set came out piping hot just as we finished our starters. This pacing allowed us to enjoy each course without the table getting cluttered.
We know that travelling with dietary restrictions can be a headache, but this Japanese restaurant in Uluwatu is very accommodating. They seem used to the diverse crowd that visits Bali and are ready to adjust dishes to suit your needs.
While we indulged in fish and beef, we noticed plenty of options for vegetarians, such as vegetable tempura and cucumber rolls. The kitchen is also happy to swap ingredients in the salads if you ask.
If the idea of raw fish scares you, the Salmon Teriyaki Set and Saikoro Wagyu are safe, delicious bets. Even the Salmon Mentai is torched, meaning it’s partially cooked, which is a great middle ground for those hesitant about fully raw sashimi.
They take allergies seriously. The menu clearly marks items, but always tells your server. Gluten-free diners should be aware that the teriyaki sauce contains soy (and wheat), so you may want to opt for salt-grilled fish (Shioyaki) instead.
Quick Tips for First-Timers
If you are walking into Tsune Uluwatu for the first time, the experience can be a little intimidating if you are not used to Japanese dining. But do not worry, it is a very casual and friendly environment. Here is a quick cheat sheet to help you order like a pro.
What to order if you have never tried sushi
Start with the Salmon Mentai. The creamy sauce and torched flavor make it taste very familiar, almost like a savory grilled dish, so it’s not as “scary” as raw fish. Alternatively, the Salmon Teriyaki Set is a safe and delicious cooked option.
What to order if you are a sushi person
Go straight for the Spicy Otoro. It shows off the quality of their sourcing. If you love texture, the Saikoro Wagyu is a must-try side dish to complement your sushi.
What Customers Are Saying
Before visiting, we did a quick scan of online reviews to see if our experience matched the consensus. It seems that Tsune Uluwatu has built a very loyal following in a short amount of time, with a high rating across Google and TripAdvisor.
Common praise and common complaints
Almost everyone raves about the Salmon Mentai sauce and the generous portions of the set meals. The aesthetic is also frequently mentioned as being peaceful and perfect for a midday escape.
The most common complaint is that the popular items (like the Otoro) can sometimes sell out if you arrive too late in the evening. Some also mention the price is higher than local warungs, but for a high-quality Japanese restaurant in Bali, the prices are standard.
After wiping our plates clean and finishing the last sip of our Hojicha, my friend and I looked at each other and nodded. This was a win. Tsune Uluwatu delivers on its promise of fresh, authentic Japanese food in a setting that is perfect for the laid-back vibe of the Bukit.
It is the kind of place you want to return to. Whether you are craving a light matcha treat or a heavy wagyu feast after surfing Uluwatu’s waves, this kitchen has you covered.
Who will love it most:
Foodies looking for premium bites like Otoro and Wagyu.
Friends who want to share a variety of plates, like Salmon Mentai.
Matcha lovers hunt for the best Matcha Eclair on the island.
Food: 9/10 (The flavors are complex and fresh)
Ambiance: 8.5/10 (Beautiful, calm, and cool)
Value: 8/10 (You get what you pay for, premium quality)
Service: 9/10 (Fast and friendly)
Is it good for non-sushi eaters?
Yes! The Salmon Teriyaki Set and Saikoro Wagyu are fantastic options that require no raw fish consumption.
How much does lunch cost?
A typical lunch for two averages around IDR 750,000 to 900,000 if you order premium items and drinks. However, you can dine for less if you stick to the set menus.
Do I need a reservation?
It is recommended for dinner when it gets busy, but for lunch, you can usua
